A rename or policy change is a `supersedes`; closing the room is a `withdraws`. The `community:` stem is closed to this leaf. | positive-only | **Yes:** signed by a current `moderate`-holder of the community it names; one live row per community |
| `trust:{job}:{version}` | The trust-root grant and acceptance edges, carried as `dimension` values on `delegates_to` rows — the wire type is unchanged, so 1+4 is untouched. A root's charter is the `charter` member of its bundle, and no row is a charter. The job `blessing` is retired: a row bearing `trust:blessing:v1` gives no grant and no standing. Retracted by `withdraws`/`recants`, never by a negative score. Conferral planes, the acceptance-edge rule and the liveness banding: [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2). | positive-only | **Yes — [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)** |
| `accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the kill-switch invocation, semantics and canonical bytes at [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1) / [CC 4.2.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1.1). Lowercase per R3 (not `CONSTITUTIONAL`). | +1.0 only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |
| `accord:invoke:notify:{notify_id}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); federation-wide accord-holder communication, [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1). | +1.0 only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |
| `accord:invoke:drill:{drill_id}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); accord-holder exercise, [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1). | +1.0 only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |
| `accord:lifecycle` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the accord heartbeat, wire `accord:lifecycle:v1`, [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1). | +1.0 only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |
| `accord:lifecycle:{kind}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the two lifecycle rows that answer a `constitutional` halt: `{kind}` ∈ `active` \| `confirmed` — closed. `active` is resumption from the halt, [CC 4.2.1.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1.3). `confirmed` is a strict majority's confirmation of a one-holder halt within its fuse, [CC 4.2.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1.1) / [CC 4.2.1.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1.3). | +1.0 only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |
| `accord:human_dignity` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); a leaf no accord holder signs, since accord authority gives no verdict on an agent's conduct, [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1). | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |
| `accord:*` | **Reserved** — only `identity_type=accord_holder` may emit. **Closed**: the rows above are its whole leaf set. One of several reserved families in this table alone (`ownership:*`, `trust:*`), and more at [CC 3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4); the generated registry is the count of record. What is distinctive is the *keying*: with `transport:canonical_rebind` ([CC 3.4.7](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.7)), this reservation is held by a **closed roster slot** rather than by a role conferred on the delegation plane, so no root can confer it. The roster occupying the slot is an instance parameter per the [CC 1](part_1_foundation.md) reading rule. | see [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1) | **Yes — [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.1)** |

### 3.1.2 `attestation` — CIRISVerify — attestation ladder, provenance, transparency

**Steward**: the verifier. These prefixes serve integrity: each is a checkable claim about how far a build, key, or license has climbed the trust ladder.

| Prefix | Description | Polarity |
|---|---|---|
| `attestation:self_verify` | Running CIRISVerify binary attests itself against its function manifest. (Consumer-side ladder: corresponds to L1; see CC 4.4.3.32 Policy I.) | boolean-via-score |
| `attestation:hardware_rooted` | Hardware-rooted attestation (TPM 2.0 / Android Keystore / iOS Secure Enclave). (Ladder L2.) | boolean-via-score |
| `attestation:registry_consensus` | 2-of-3 multi-source registry consensus on key / build / license validity. (Ladder L3.) An `Indeterminate` consensus is no row, never a third point; a consumer resolves the absence fail-secure (RESTRICTED). | boolean-via-score |
| `attestation:license_validity` | License-validity claim (Registry-signed, Verify-verified). (Ladder L4.) | boolean-via-score |
| `attestation:agent_integrity` | Agent source-tree byte-equal against registered manifest. (Ladder L5.) | boolean-via-score |
| `provenance:slsa:{level}` | SLSA build provenance levels 1-3. Registry emits these on build registration; Verify consumes them as `AttestBundle.provenance.slsa_level`. | boolean-via-score |
| `provenance:build_manifest:{target}` | Per-target canonical-staged-runtime manifest hash equality. The pipeline that built it signs the row, and the manifest blob is unsigned (CC 3.1.2.1). | boolean-via-score |
| `provenance:build_manifest:{target}:locale:{lang_code}` | Per-locale signed sub-manifest within a target's manifest tree. Parent target manifest is Merkle root over per-locale leaves. A non-power-of-two leaf count is padded by repeating the last leaf to the next power of two — not RFC 6962's split, and not the per-level duplication of [CC 6.1.1](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.1); the leaves and parents carry RFC 6962's `0x00` / `0x01` prefixes, and the list is one leaf per locale. Detection surface for locale-targeted attacks. Canonical-bytes spec at [CC 3.1.2.1](#3.1.2.1). | boolean-via-score |
| `provenance:skill_import:{source}` | Community-skill import provenance. `{source}` ∈ `registry:{registry_id}` \| `direct:{url}` \| `local:{path}`. Envelope: `{skill_manifest_sha256, signer_identity, import_timestamp, capability_declaration}`. Canonical-bytes spec at [CC 3.1.2.1](#3.1.2.1). | signed |
| `rollback_detected:{revision_field}` | Anti-rollback — decrease in revocation revision. | -1 only |
| `cert_validity:{authority}` | Validity of a certification authority's signature. A certification authority's validity self-attestation is a **producer claim** ([CC 4.2.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.2.1)); the trust root itself is the GenesisBundle — tamper-evident, and authentic only against the consumer's out-of-band anchor ([CC 5.3.4](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.4), [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T5) — never a steward-key self-report. | boolean-via-score |
| `hardware_custody:{platform}` | Where the key's seed lives — the custody **mechanism**, not the certified class ([CC 4.2.2](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.2) `hardware_class` answers that, and is a member of a key record's `attestation_evidence`, never a value of `{platform}`). `{platform}` ∈ `android_keystore` \| `android_strongbox` \| `ios_secure_enclave` \| `mac_os_secure_enclave` \| `tpm_discrete` \| `tpm_firmware` \| `intel_sgx` \| `software_only` \| `aws_cloud_hsm` \| `azure_hsm` \| `gcp_cloud_hsm` \| `yubi_hsm` \| `external_secure_element` — **closed**, the one enumeration every custody policy keys on; an emitter that spells a run-together form (`tpmdiscrete`) or a retired token (`tpm`, `android`, `software_fallback`) is refused, never folded. | boolean-via-score |
| `identity:canonical_binding:{canonical_hash}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the claim that federation key K is the identity behind canonical hash H, semantics and admission consequence at [CC 3.3.14](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.14). Carries no version segment (`_meta.case_rule.version_segment.exempt`): the suffix is the hash. | positive-only |

#### Assurance ladders (registry rows; rules at CC 3.4.11 / CC 3.4.12)

Both ladders are attestation ladders in the sense of this section: a registered witness climbs a rung about a subject. Both are ruled in [CC 3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4) and catalogued here, as [CC 3.1.7](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.7) R1 requires of any gated family. The subject-signed `age_self_declared:` counterpart is catalogued here too: it is *not* witness-reserved, but it carries an admission rule at [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11), so R1 requires its row.

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version}` | Witness rung of the age ladder — `{level}` ∈ `provider` \| `government` (closed; `self` is refused here), `{band}` ∈ `minor` \| `adult` \| `under_13` \| `13_15` \| `16_17` (closed — the [CC 3.4.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.13) Q1 finer bands spelled as the substrate's `AgeBandFine`; `unknown` is a consumer's fail-secure *resolution*, never a wire token), canonical `{version}` = `v1`. There is no `self` level on this prefix: the self rung rides `age_self_declared:` below. A consumer unions both and the witness rung outranks the self rung, save that a self-declared lower band lowers the reading ([CC 3.4.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.13)). Full ladder + protective gate at [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11). | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)** |
| `age_self_declared:band:{band}:{version}` | Subject's own age-band declaration — `{band}` ∈ `minor` \| `adult` \| `under_13` \| `13_15` \| `16_17` (closed — the [CC 3.4.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.13) Q1 finer bands spelled as the substrate's `AgeBandFine`; `unknown` is a consumer's fail-secure *resolution*, never a wire token), canonical `{version}` = `v1`. Carries **no** `{level}` token: its level is `self` by construction, and a level token on this prefix is malformed. The literal `band` segment marks the rung (`age_self_declared:band:adult:v1`); the two-segment `age_self_declared:{band}:{version}` is not a registered shape. Non-reserved but not open-sender: admitted only where the signer acts for the subject, per [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11). | signed | No |
| `capacity_assurance:{level}:{domain}:{band}:{version}` | Witness rung of the adult decision-capacity ladder ([CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)): a registered qualified assessor attests a per-domain band; the subject cannot self-emit it and the proposed steward cannot be the attester. `{level}` ∈ `provider` \| `panel` \| `government` (closed — the two reversible-cause companions below are their own rows, never a `{level}`); `{band}` ∈ `capacitated` \| `incapacitated` (closed); `{domain}` is the open per-domain vocabulary. Aggregation across domains is forbidden — capacity is a vector, never collapsed to a scalar. | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)** |
| `capacity_assurance:reversible_excluded:{domain}:{version}` | Reversible-cause exclusion companion ([CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)): the assessor attests that delirium, infection-confusion, depression and polypharmacy are ruled out for the domain. A mandatory predicate on any continuing `incapacitated` rung; witness-reserved like its parent. | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)** |
| `capacity_assurance:reversible_pending:{domain}:{version}` | Acute-window companion ([CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)): exclusion in progress, not skipped; admissible for the T1 provisional tier only, and the binding MUST lapse unless it resolves to `reversible_excluded` within its `valid_until`. Witness-reserved. | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)** |

#### 3.1.2.1 `provenance` — Canonical-bytes contracts for provenance primitives

A provenance claim is only as trustworthy as its preimage is reproducible. The three contracts below state what a producer signs and a consumer recomputes, so a skill import, a per-locale manifest or an agent text manifest statement verifies identically across implementations.

#### The build-manifest Contribution (normative reading)

**One claim.** A build manifest is published as **one** claim: a `scores` Contribution on `provenance:build_manifest:{target}`, signed by the key of the pipeline that built it. Its `sub` is the pipeline's own identity reference: the row is the pipeline's statement about its own output. `agent_files:build:{target}` ([CC 3.1.9.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.1)) is **a different claim by a different attester** — the canonical attester's statement that an agent may load that file set, composed under [CC 4.4.3.33](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.33) — and cites the same bytes. A pipeline does not emit it, and emitting both from one key would be two claims about one fact.

**The row.** The row's payload carries a top-level member `build`, a map of exactly four members. `project` and `version` are text. `manifest_hash` is the manifest blob's digest, and `manifest_size` is the blob's length in bytes, at least 1. All four are REQUIRED, and the table of [CC 2.6.1.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.4) lists them. `build` is the descriptor [CC 5.3.2.11](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.2.11) binds, so a fetcher checks size before hashing. The row MUST cite the blob by its digest in `evidence_refs[]`. The row MUST name in `refs.head` the bundle in force when it is signed ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1), an act names its head). That bundle is the one the pipeline's grant names or a later bundle of the same lineage. A row whose head is on another lineage, or is older than the grant's, is refused, `build_row_other_head`. The row MUST also name in `refs.also.stands_on` the acceptance of the grant it stands on ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). Its `cohort_scope` is `federation`.

**The manifest blob.** The blob is unsigned: the row's signature covers its digest. It is the deterministic encoding ([CC 2.6.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.2)) of a map, and it MUST NOT carry a float. Its members are exactly `format`, `project`, `version`, `target`, `binary_hash`, `functions_root`, `tool` and, where the table is carried inline, `functions`. `format` has the value `ciris-binary-manifest/1`, and a reader MUST check it before it reads any other member. `tool` is text that names the generator and its version, and it says nothing of the run. The blob states no instant: it is a function of the file, the project, the version, the target and the tool. The signed instant is the row's `asserted_at`. `binary_hash`, `functions_root` and each function's `hash` are byte strings of 32 bytes, since the format string pins SHA-256. The blob's CDDL and its known answers are the verification library's, an open encoding ([CC 2.6.1.12](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.12)). They are registered as `manifests/binary_manifest_v1.cddl` and `manifests/binary_manifest_v1_vectors.json`. That CDDL defines a function's `offset` for each executable format.

**The function table.** A blob MUST carry `functions_root`, the Merkle root over its function table, and MAY carry the table inline as `functions`. A reader that holds the table MUST recompute the root, and MUST refuse a blob whose table gives another root, `build_manifest_functions_root_mismatch`. The tree is the locale tree's, with its prefixes and its padding (*Per-locale Merkle composition*, below). The leaves stand in the byte order of the function names. A leaf is the deterministic encoding of a map of exactly `name`, `offset`, `size` and `hash`. The offset base of each executable format is stated in the blob's CDDL.

**The blob's refusals.** A blob is at most `build_manifest_max_bytes` long, and a reader checks its length before it decodes it. A reader refuses a blob on any line of this table.

| Refusal | The fault |
|---|---|
| `build_manifest_oversize` | the blob is longer than `build_manifest_max_bytes` |
| `build_manifest_not_deterministic` | the bytes are not the deterministic encoding of what they decode to |
| `build_manifest_float` | a floating-point value stands anywhere in the blob |
| `build_manifest_not_a_map` | the top-level item is not a map |
| `build_manifest_wrong_format` | `format` is absent or is not `ciris-binary-manifest/1` |
| `build_manifest_unknown_member` | a member outside the closed list stands in the blob or in a function entry |
| `build_manifest_missing_member` | a required member is absent |
| `build_manifest_malformed` | a member is off its type or its bound |
| `build_manifest_empty_functions` | an inline `functions` table has no entry |
| `build_manifest_duplicate_function` | one function name stands twice |

**The pipeline's standing.** The pipeline's standing is not a member the producer writes about itself. A reader evaluates it under [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T2, on the plane that conferred it and never an inferred one. The standing is a grant: a `delegates_to` row with the dimension `trust:confers:v1`, counted as [CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1) states. The grant names the pipeline's key as its `sub`, by identity reference, and names the bundle in force in `refs.head`. It carries `scope`, a set of scope tokens, and `projects`, a set of at least one project name. A build pipeline's scope token is `infra:attest:provenance:build_manifest`: the capability, sub-scoped to this family's stem ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5)). A bare `infra:attest` is valid and confers every attest family, and the ceremony SHOULD issue the sub-scope. A reader matches the token by the directional rule of [CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5). A grant is a pipeline's where it carries `projects`. A label on the key's record decides nothing, since `identity_type` confers no standing ([CC 3.4.7.1](#3.4.7.1)). A pipeline's key is a `node` or an `agent` key, because its grant needs an owner's acceptance and an owner-binding binds only those ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). The bounds on a pipeline's grant, its role and its end among them, are those of [CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1).

**The projects a grant lists.** A grant with no `projects` member confers a build manifest for no project. A manifest whose `build.project` its pipeline's grant does not list is refused, `build_manifest_project_not_granted`.

**The owner's acceptance.** A grant confers nothing until its acceptance is held, and an acceptance is of one grant. It is a `membership:acceptance:v1` row at `cohort_scope` `federation` that names the grant in `refs.answers`. Its `sub` is the grantee. It names in `refs.also.cites` the owner-binding it is made under: exactly one row, live, and placed at `federation` as the acceptance is. One owner's rows re-signed at other scopes are one ownership, and one acceptance serves them ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). An owner who withdraws the row an acceptance cites accepts again, citing a live row. A grant to a machine with no binding at `federation` is relied on only where its binding is held. The pipeline's owner signs it, and the owner is a person. A reader takes the owner from the owner-binding ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)) that names the pipeline's key, as that binding stood at the acceptance. The pipeline's own key MUST NOT sign the acceptance. A pipeline with no owner has no acceptance, and its grant confers nothing. An acceptance names no head. The owner's `trust:accepts:v1` edge ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T3) is a different row. That edge roots the owner's nodes in the root and is no consent to any grant. Where a node or an agent that holds a grant is bound to a new owner, the new owner MUST accept that grant before it confers for acts under the new binding. Each binding needs its own acceptance, a binding back to an earlier owner included, and an earlier acceptance confers nothing under a later binding. Once a reader holds the binding that replaced an act's own, that act is in force for nobody unless it was receipted. This entry does not say what a new owner's decline or withdrawal of an acceptance does to acts already signed.

**Lapse.** A build row does not lapse while a node's `attestation:self_verify` that has not lapsed cites it ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). A pipeline's key record states `valid_until` as any machine key's does, and the pipeline renews it by a further record ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)).

**Two faults of a manifest.** Two rows of one pipeline for one project, version and target MUST NOT differ in `build` unless one supersedes the other. A reader refuses both, `build_manifest_equivocation`. A row whose `build` disagrees with the blob it cites is refused, `build_manifest_descriptor_mismatch`. That one name covers every disagreement: the blob's length, its digest, its `project`, its `version`, and its `target` against the target of the row's family.

**What a read answer contains.** A read route answers for one project, version and target, and the route's path is the server's ([CC 5.3.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.5)). The answer holds:

- the build-manifest row, with every statement of it, and its blob;
- the pipeline's key record;
- the counted grant, with every voice;
- the owner's acceptance, and the owner-binding it rests on;
- the bundle the grant names and the bundle the row names; and
- every `withdraws` or `supersedes` row that names the manifest row.

Each row and each bundle is a signed statement a reader verifies offline, and the blob is checked against the digest the row signs. The grant is resolved at use against a root the reader trusts ([CC 5.3.4](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.4): nothing a serving install signs on its own account is a root).

**A node that runs a build.** A node's statement that **it runs** a given build is not a second claim on this dimension and needs no new family. It is the build attestation the trust ladder already carries — `attestation:self_verify` for the verifier itself and `attestation:agent_integrity` for an agent's tree, above — signed by the running node about itself and citing the manifest's Contribution. `evidence_refs[]` carries the manifest **blob's** digest (the bytes a holder serves), and `references_attestation_id` carries the manifest Contribution's row id. The member cites a row on any attestation type, and takes composer meaning only on `supersedes` / `withdraws` / `recants`.

**The boot statement.** A node's boot statement, `ceg-boot-manifest/2` ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)), carries `build_manifest_row`, a `row-ref` to the build-manifest row. The member is REQUIRED once such a row exists for the build the node booted. A boot statement of any other build omits it and MUST NOT carry a placeholder in its place.

A rebuild is a `supersedes` on the Contribution it replaces, and a bad build is withdrawn by the pipeline that signed it.

**The verdicts on a manifest's standing.** A manifest whose standing fails on a line of this table confers nothing, and a reader names the line. A grant short of a strict majority is held and waits, and a grant with no holder's voice yet is the same case. A withdrawn row does not count toward `build_manifest_equivocation`. Where several faults of the manifest row apply, a reader names withdrawn first, then superseded, then equivocation.

| Verdict | The fault |
|---|---|
| `build_manifest_scope_not_granted` | the grant's scope does not reach the family under [CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5) |
| `build_manifest_withdrawn` | a `withdraws` of the manifest row stands |
| `build_manifest_superseded` | a `supersedes` of the manifest row stands |
| `grant_other_grantee` | the grant's `sub` is not the row's signer |
| `grant_withdrawn` | a counted withdrawal of the grant stands |
| `grant_declined` | the owner declined the grant; a decline is terminal |
| `grant_contested` | an acceptance and a decline of one grant by the same owner both stand; neither counts ([CC 3.1.3.2](#3.1.3.2)) |
| `acceptance_by_grantee` | the acceptance is signed by the grantee's own key |
| `acceptance_not_by_owner` | the acceptance's signer is not the owner of the grantee's key |
| `acceptance_other_grant` | the acceptance names another grant in `refs.answers` |
| `acceptance_other_grantee` | the acceptance's `sub` is not the grant's grantee |
| `acceptance_withdrawn` | a withdrawal of the acceptance by the owner stands |
| `owner_binding_other_key` | the owner-binding the acceptance rests on names another key than the grantee's |
| `build_row_stands_on_nothing` | the row carries no `refs.also.stands_on`, or the row it names is not a valid acceptance of this grant |
| `acceptance_other_binding` | the acceptance cites no owner-binding of the grantee's key, or cites two, or the one it cites is ended or is another owner's |
| `grantee_has_no_owner` | the reader holds no live owner-binding of the grantee's key, or the live ones name more than one owner |

**A row not yet held.** A row named by `refs.also.stands_on` that the reader does not hold makes the verdict wait. An owner-binding an acceptance cites that the reader does not hold does the same. A reader refuses only where a row it holds is the wrong one.

**After the grant ends.** After its grant ends, a manifest's row counts at its own head and is in force only under a clean receipt of it ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). A reader that reads no receipts treats the row as not standing.

**Whose decline counts.** A decline of a grant is the owner's. The owner is the owner of the grantee's key, read from the owner-binding the reader holds. A decline by any other key is no decline of that grant.

*Checked.* That a row under a root grant stands on both the bundle and the acceptance is checked by the kernel's exhaustive run over the vendored fixture `conferral_two.json` (the kernel's `CONFERRAL_END.md`, section J), and it is not a TLC result.

#### `SkillImportManifest` canonical bytes (v2 — normative)

A skill import manifest is signed with one composite signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)) over its signing bytes. Those bytes cover the pinned domain `ciris.skill_import.v2`, `source`, `skill_manifest_sha256`, `signer_identity`, `import_timestamp`, `capability_declaration` and, where it is set, `valid_until`. `capability_declaration` is a set ([CC 2.6.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.2)). The encoding of those bytes is an open encoding ([CC 2.6.1.12](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.12)). Their earlier form is [CC 8.11.16](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.16).

#### Per-locale Merkle composition (v2 — normative)

A locale manifest is a Merkle tree of one leaf per locale. A leaf is hashed under the RFC 6962 leaf prefix `0x00`, and a parent is SHA-256 over the prefix `0x01`, the left child and the right child. A leaf covers the pinned domain `ciris.locale_manifest.v2`, `target`, `locale`, `files_root`, `build_id` and `signer_identity`. The encoding of a leaf is an open encoding ([CC 2.6.1.12](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.12)), and its earlier form is [CC 8.11.16](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.16).

Locale ordering: lexicographic by ISO 639-1 / BCP 47 byte representation; `"polyglot"` sorts last. Padding: repeat the last leaf to the next power of two (not RFC 6962's split, and not the per-level duplication of [CC 6.1.1](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.1)); one leaf per locale, so no leaf repeats except by padding.

The closed-vocabulary [CC 4.2.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1.1) accord-invocation encoding is intentionally distinct. Its preimage is a discriminator + nonce + enum fields with no attacker-controlled free text, so the injection surface this structured form closes is not reachable there, and genesis-critical bytes stay stable.

#### Agent text manifest statement (v1 — normative)

An agent ships the texts it reasons from, the accord text in every language it carries and its guides, beside a manifest that names each file by SHA-256. A steward vouches for that manifest by signing a statement of it and never the file's own bytes, so a key held on a hardware token signs a fixed-size digest whatever the manifest's length. The statement is a row, signed as every row is ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)), and its family is an open encoding ([CC 2.6.1.12](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.12)). Its earlier form is [CC 8.11.15](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.15).

**The signer.** The signer is a human-held steward key of the canonical attester ([CC 3.1.9.1](#3.1.9.1)), resolved to its hybrid key record. An agent pins the set of signers it accepts, and for the shipped root the signer is an accord holder, whose act [CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1) names. `signer_identity` is inside the signed bytes, so one holder's signature cannot be presented as another's.

**The check.** An agent rebuilds the statement from the manifest bytes it holds, size before digest ([CC 5.3.2.11](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.2.11)), and never takes it from a copy carried beside the signature. It verifies the composite signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)) against the signer's key record before it makes any decision. A missing signature, a signer outside the pinned set, a key record held only in part, or a failed verification stops the agent: it does not run on text nobody vouched for. The signature covers the manifest and the manifest covers each file by its digest, so a changed text fails at the file and a changed manifest fails at the signature.

### 3.1.3 `persist` — CIRISPersist — substrate health

**Steward**: the substrate. The `system:*` dimensions here are substrate-self-reports — emittable only by the running substrate itself ([CC 3.4.3](#3.4.3)), which is what makes them honest: the substrate cannot be made to lie about its own health by a third party.

`system:*` is one family, reserved to the substrate component ([CC 3.4.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.3)) and registered once, here. The persist and edge components of a node each emit on it for that node.

Canonical leaves: `system:*`, `audit_chain:hash_continuity`, `corpus_health:n_eff_measurable`, `identity_continuity:relational_anchor`, `federation_directory:replication_lag`. Polarity: signed. Authors: see [CC 8.1](part_8_appendices.md#8.1) Persist leaf glossary for narrative-name → canonical-leaf mapping.

#### Settlement and ledgers (registry rows; semantics at [CC 3.3.10](part_3_the_namespace.md) and [CC 3.3.10.1](part_3_the_namespace.md))

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settlement:*` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the optional, privacy-scoped linkage of a federation action to its off-stack settlement — a bare `scores` against the paid Contribution, or the `settlement` subject_kind ceremony when an explicit receipt is wanted ([CC 3.3.10](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.10)). Open leaves (`settlement:paid:v1` canonical); `cohort_scope` is the producer's choice. CEG records that a settlement happened and what it paid for; the chain settles the value. | signed | No |

#### The planes as rows (registry rows; cosigned rows, [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md))

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|

Its `attested_key_id` is the group, and its payload carries the fold (seats, roles, `effective_at`s, bounds), with `prev_head_digest` in `refs`. Wire `group:roster:v1`. A `node` or `agent` record states its own end ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). Short of that quorum it is held and revokes nothing; the owner collects signatures through the quorum path. It carries the node's new `transport_destination` and transit key in its payload. It lands Rooted on every node that holds the root and **supersedes the bundle-seeded binding**, so a transit-pair rotation is a quorum act and not a re-mint; a re-bind below that count concludes nothing (`transport_rebind_without_holder_quorum`). A later bundle that re-seats the node at new X-Wing keys does the same. A seated node MUST NOT emit a unilateral rotation that would retire the pinned pair before a re-bind has landed, and no node counts one (`serve_transit_pair_rotation_before_rebind`). Wire `transport:canonical_rebind:v1`. | positive-only | **Yes — the accord holders, a strict majority of the bundle in force**; never a single holder, never the node itself |
| `act:ack` | **A receipt of one or more acts** (registered under CC 3.1.7 R2(a); [CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5), [CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)): the signer acknowledges the acts it names under `refs.also` `ack`, at most 256 of them, and names no head. The family `cosign:{state}` is retired, and a row under the stem `cosign:` is refused `namespace_family_unregistered`. A counted row short of its count is held as its own voices ([CC 3.3.4](#3.3.4)).

#### Retired delegation labels (registry rows — closed)

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `self:delegates_to` | **Closed label, no job.** A dimension value carried on `delegates_to` rows of the Self-at-login composition ([CC 4.4.3.19](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.19)) only so the row carried a version tail.
