These two labels are not a `self:` family — `self` is a `cohort_scope`, and a claim's namespace should not read as one. The `self:` stem is therefore **closed to these two**: any other dimension beginning `self:` is refused `namespace_family_unregistered`, never admitted as open vocabulary (a device's name is `device:label`, [CC 3.1.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.1)).

#### Lineage-witness consent (a retired name)

The family `lineage_witness:{stage}` is retired, and a row under the stem `lineage_witness:` is refused `namespace_family_unregistered`. Naming a Transparency Service in a charter asks no consent and confers nothing ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6).

#### The mesh census and the secret poll (registry rows; semantics at [CC 6.1.9](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.9))

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `census:share:{class}` | **A node's census return, one share of two** ([CC 6.1.9](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.9)): an **addressed** row whose signed `for_key_id` is one of the period's two serve seats, carrying `period`, `return_token`, `share_index` ∈ {0, 1}, `expires_at` = the period's end, and an opaque body (the one-hot share and its proof share). Held by the author and the recipient only; any other node refuses it `federation_addressed_not_recipient`. Reasons: `census_return_recipient_not_seat` (the recipient is not a serve seat; not counted), `census_return_expired` (a node does not take one offered after the period's end), `census_share_index_invalid` (Invalid). Two shares with the same `(return_token, share_index)` in a period at the same seat are contested, and neither counts while they differ (`census_share_duplicate_token`). `{class}` is the scope class the return describes. | signed | **Yes — addressed:** the returning node's key; reach is the named seat only |
| `census:partial:{class}` | **One aggregator's field-wise sum of the shares it accepted** for a period: `period`, `share_index`, `share_count`, `member_commitment_hex` over the accepted tokens, `mass_total`, `aggregation_algorithm_id`, and a body of field elements. Signed by a serve seat (`census_partial_signer_not_seat`); not counted once the period's composite is held (`census_partial_period_closed`); a token with one share of two at period close is dropped and reported `census_share_pair_incomplete`. Federation scope. | signed | **Yes — seat:** a serve seat of the period |
| `census:composite:{class}` | **The mesh census for a class and period**: a `scores` row naming both partials (`partial_a`, `partial_b`) and carrying the [CC 6.1.2.1](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.2.1) inputs — `version = 3`, `source_count`, `n_eff`, `max_source_multiplicity`, `mass_commitment_hex`, `member_commitment_hex`, `aggregation_algorithm_id`, optional `noise_floor_descriptor` — with `mass_total` and the summed histograms. Signed by a serve seat (`census_composite_signer_not_seat`). Refusals: `census_composite_below_k` (`source_count < 10`), `census_composite_mass_total_mismatch` (the cells do not sum to `mass_total`), `aggregation_meta_dominated`, `aggregation_meta_multiplicity`. One whose named partials differ in commitment or share count, or whose `mass_total` is not their sum, concludes nothing (`census_composite_partials_mismatch`). Two composites for one class and period, from any seat, are contested, and neither counts while they differ (`census_composite_duplicate_period`). A `max_source_multiplicity` other than `1` is refused as well ([CC 6.1.9](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.9)). Federation scope. | signed | **Yes — seat:** a serve seat of the period; one per class and period |
| `census:member:share` | **A member's community cell, one share of two**: addressed to one of the period's two tally members of the room (`ballot_share_recipient_not_tally_member`), emitted every period at a fixed size whether or not a poll is open; the body is sealed under the community's epoch key and carries the active bit, a one-hot over an open poll's options plus *none*, and the padding; `poll_id` lives only in the body. Two member shares with one token are contested as for the census share (`ballot_share_duplicate_token`), and a share whose pair is not held is not counted (`ballot_share_pair_incomplete`). Community scope. | signed | **Yes — addressed:** a member of the room; reach is the named tally member only |
| `census:member:partial` | **A tally member's sum** over the community cells it accepted, published into the room with the members of `census:partial`; `ballot_partial_period_closed` after the period's tally. Community scope. | signed | **Yes — tally member:** one of the period's two, drawn from the roster |
| `census:expected_active` | **The community's expected-active count**, the base of [CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13): `period`, `window_periods = 4`, `active_count` (owners active in at least one of the last four periods), `floor_applied`, `member_commitment_hex`. It is published into the room by the period's share-index-0 tally member and recomputed by every member. A row that differs from a member's own recomputation over the two partials is not counted (`census_expected_active_mismatch`). Community scope. | signed | **Yes — tally member:** the period's share-index-0 tally member |
| `ballot:tally:{poll_id}` | **A community's secret poll result**: the composite of the members' poll cells for a period, with the members of `census:composite`, named by the poll it closes; refusals `ballot_tally_mass_total_mismatch` and `aggregation_meta_dominated`; it concludes nothing under `ballot_tally_partials_mismatch` and `ballot_tally_duplicate_period`, which read other rows. A tally carries no standing under Part 4; governance acts stay identified rows. Community scope. | signed | **Yes — tally member:** the period's share-index-0 tally member |
| `ballot:moderator` | **A member's ballot in a moderator election** ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)): `community_id`, the election id (digest of the community id and the last seating row, or of the roster's genesis for an unseated room), `ranks` (up to three member keys in order). One ballot per person, folded as a vote is ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13): agreeing ballots one, disagreeing unwithdrawn ballots none until a withdrawal). A ballot naming an unknown election id or a non-member is kept and not counted; a late ballot is stored, never refused, and is void only against the seating that wins. Wire `ballot:moderator:v1`. Community scope. | signed | **Yes — a live member:** the signer's membership is live at evaluation |
| `ballot:moderator_acceptance` | **The winner's acceptance, binding the ballot set it was seated on**: `community_id`, the election id, the digest of the ballot and withdrawal rows counted and the signer's own key. It waits until the node holds that set. It is not counted unless the count over it yields the signer, the set meets the floor and the node's own 24 h since the lock have passed. Among valid acceptances the larger set seats, and two sets of equal size seat nobody until an acceptance over their union is held. Wire `ballot:moderator_acceptance:v1`. Community scope. | signed | **Yes — the winner:** the signer is the count's winner over the bound set |

#### 3.1.3.1 `session-claim` — `session:*` — which occurrence of a self is handling an exchange (normative)

Distinct from the substrate self-reports above: these are **occurrence** self-reports, not substrate ones. The substrate owns the rows, the projection, the merge rule and the read, and it enforces both rules below. This section is the row those validators read from, so that two of them cannot apply different predicates to one artifact.

**The problem it solves.** A *self* is one federated identity plus the N nodes it stewards — its **occurrences**. An attestation addressed to a fed id fans out to every one of them, because a fed id has no transport path of its own; delivery is therefore N-to-M and **exactly one occurrence may act**. The claim is keyed by `(community, session)`, and the reason is in two questions. The question *"which node is my self?"* has no answer: a self is legitimately doing several things at once, an agent scouting in one community while the person is on video in another. The question *"which node is handling session z in community B?"* does have one. Canonical leaf `session:claim:v1`; the family governs **any addressed, stateful exchange** — a session, a claim flow, a moderation duty, a request expecting one reply — and is not chat-specific.

**Registry row (CC 3.1.7 R1 — this is the catalogue row the validators read).**

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session:{kind}` | Which occurrence of a self is handling an addressed, stateful exchange. Canonical leaf `session:claim:v1`; `{kind}` open vocabulary per [CC 4.5.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.1.1). Keyed by `(community, session)` — a routing table, never a leader election, and not chat-specific. Emitter: **self-report** (`attesting_key_id` = `attested_key_id` = the claiming occurrence). Composition: **convergent merge** — earliest `claimed_at`, ties on the lowest occurrence `key_id`. Projection ceiling **`Cohort`** at every commons tier, no `authority` branch. | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5) self-report** |

**This is a routing table, not a leader election.** Nothing here elects a node, confers standing, or ranks occurrences. Election does not belong on this plane at all.

**Emitter — self-report (normative).** `attesting_key_id` MUST equal `attested_key_id` and MUST be the claiming occurrence. The registry carries this as the family's own reserved rule (`occurrence-self-report`, CC 3.1.3.1) ahead of the substrate-wide self-report rule of [CC 3.4.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.3). That substrate-wide rule does not apply here, because a claim is an *occurrence's* statement, not the substrate's. A row about an occurrence authored by anyone else is not that occurrence's claim and MUST NOT be folded as one. This is the same discipline [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5) states for `config:{scope}`, and for the same reason: a third-party assertion of where you are attending is a rumour.

**Composition — convergent merge (normative).** A claim is keyed by **`(community_id, session_id)`** and timestamped by **`claimed_at`**: three signed envelope members ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1)). `community_id` is the existing member. `session_id` and `claimed_at` are this family's, REQUIRED on every `session:*` row, with `claimed_at` an instant of [CC 2.6.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.2). A row missing any of the three is not a claim and MUST NOT be folded as one. No consumer substitutes `asserted_at`, `context` or a payload field, so identical rows yield identical winners everywhere. There is no compare-and-swap across a mesh, so concurrent claims are **expected rather than prevented** and MUST settle on **earliest `claimed_at`, ties broken on the lowest occurrence `key_id`**. The tie-break is load-bearing, not decoration: a fan-out arrives at once and clocks are coarse, so without a total order two nodes would disagree about the survivor forever, each correctly applying "earliest wins". Because the rule is convergent from either arrival order, every occurrence computes the same holder with **no coordination round-trip**. Consumers MUST still make handling idempotent per attestation id — determinism only bites once views agree, and replication lag means they transiently do not. A claim goes **stale** and becomes claimable again so a dead node cannot hold a session forever. **The horizon is the row's own `valid_until`** ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1)), signed by the claimant and moved only by a renewing row that `supersedes` it. The horizon is never a consumer-local timeout. That is because two occurrences applying different horizons would expire the same earliest claim at different instants and the convergence above would come undone (one acting on a later claim while the other still holds the earliest as holder). The *cadence* of renewal is the claimant's to choose; the *instant* of staleness is the same for every reader. A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family.

**The lease is bounded, and the bound reads the claim alone (normative).** A signature proves who supplied `claimed_at`, not that it is honest. Without a bound, "earliest wins" would let one occurrence hold a session indefinitely by back-dating `claimed_at` and far-dating `valid_until`. The one bound this Part imposes is therefore **self-contained**: `claimed_at < valid_until` and `valid_until − claimed_at` MUST NOT exceed **86 400 seconds**. A lease runs forward from its claim, and for at most a day. The bound is read from the claim's own signed members and nothing else: no community record, no opening row, no receiver clock. So every substrate reaches the same verdict for the same row at any arrival time and in any replication order. A claim over the bound is refused (`session_claim_out_of_window`) and never enters the fold. A claimant that wants to hold longer renews with a `supersedes` row, each renewal bounded the same way. Peers MUST NOT re-apply any arrival-clock check to a replicated claim: the [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.7) clock rule (±5 minutes; a future-dated row is malformed) is applied once, at the emitter's own admitting substrate, and a row it admitted replicates as admitted. **Residual, stated:** a claimant can still back-date `claimed_at`, so earliest-wins can be won against honest occurrences by at most one lease (24 h); that is the accepted cost of ordering on signer-stamped instants with no global clock. Tighter bounds — a per-community lease, or anchoring `claimed_at` to the exchange's opening row — need members the envelope does not carry (a pinned opening-row id, a pinned policy-record id). A community that needs more witnesses its session claims on the [CC 5.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.1) plane.

**The invariant beneath both rules (normative).** **An unclaimed exchange is never acted on** — not by a quorum, not by the lowest id, and **not by a single-node self**. Being the only occurrence is not authority to act; it means there is one place where nobody is home. Attendance is encoded as **presence in the table**: an unattended occurrence is *absent*, never present with a weak claim. A weak-claim value is one a careless comparison can promote into a right to act, so no such variant may exist.

**Projection ceiling: `Cohort` at every commons tier, with no `authority` branch (normative — not a default).** A trust root is not a party to someone else's session. The ceiling is not to be lifted, for this reason. At `Global` the family would publish an **attendance map of a person's devices** — which node they are chatting from, which is running an agent, which is on video — to the whole mesh. That is the [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2) structural-invisibility promise inverted.

**What the substrate does not own.** Attendance itself. *"A human is present here"* / *"an agent is running here"* is not a storage fact, and no substrate can know it; when to claim, renew, and release is the consumer's decision.

#### 3.1.3.2 `membership` — `membership:*` — nobody joins a family or community without their own consent (normative)

This entry says which signed rows seat a key on the roster of a `family` or `community`, and which never do.

**The rule.** Admission to a `family` or `community` is two consents, never one: the group's, under its `consensus_protocol`, and the joiner's own. The admission predicates read this consent as well as the existing members' signatures ([CC 4.4.3.6](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.6), [CC 4.4.3.17](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.17)). Without it a record growing the roster by K would be admissible with no act by K, and one signer could enrol any registered key. The joiner's consent is the joiner's, and no quorum, however large, stands in for it. So the rule binds **every** `consensus_protocol`, `founder_only` included. The group's consent is counted under its declared `consensus_protocol` and under no other fraction, for a widening and for a removal alike. The `community_invite` and `community_remove` rows of the policy table ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)) give the window, the voices and the floor of such a change. The count that enacts it is the protocol's. The floor of two voices stands under every protocol ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)). On an admission by invitation the invitee's acceptance is the second voice, so one member's signature with it admits. A removal has no such second voice, so one signature never removes. The substrate is the steward and enforces it at admission, on the local door and the replicated apply alike, so no host can skip it.

**Registry row (CC 3.1.7 R1).**

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `membership:{stage}` | The membership ceremony, one attestation-plane row per step: `{stage}` ∈ `proposal` \| `acceptance` \| `decline` \| `widening` \| `removal` \| `resignation` \| `keeps` — closed. The first three are single-signer (below); the next three are the roster **events** as cosigned rows ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4)): a widening or removal is cosigned under the group's `consensus_protocol`, a resignation is signed by the leaving member, and each is covered by the next `group:roster` version ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6). A `keeps` row is counted under the group's `consensus_protocol`, as a removal is, and names content kept after a member's seat ends (below). A **proposal** is an invitation to one key K, targeted at the group (`family_key_id` / `community_key_id`), carrying `group_kind`, the offered `role` (nullable), `subject_key_ids = [K]` (exactly one) and a required `expires_at`. On a `public` community whose record declares `consensus_protocol: open:self_admit` (`admission: open` is the shorthand, [CC 3.2](#3.2)), it is a duty holder's **standing** proposal to any requester, whose `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance. An **acceptance** or **decline** is K's answer to exactly one proposal, targeted at the same group, naming it in `refs.answers`, which is the answer's whole binding to it; an acceptance also restates the `role` offered. A reply that carries `proposal_hash`, a member of the earlier form, is malformed and refused. `refs.answers` is carried by a membership acceptance and decline, a grant's acceptance and decline, an objection's `assent` and `raised`, a chat reply and reaction, and a deferral response. A voice of a counted row carries none. | positive-only | **Yes — per-leaf emitter:** a proposal is an inviter's (under `founder_only`, an active founder; otherwise any active member at the proposal's `asserted_at`); an acceptance or decline is the invitee's only — the signer resolves (`signer_acts_for`, [CC 3.4.7.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.7.3)) to the proposal's `subject_key_ids[0]` |

**The proposal is an invitation, not the group's decision.** It carries no quorum. The group decides on the **growth record**: a membership **widening**, the only door that adds anyone. Its primary signer and cosigners are judged under `consensus_protocol` exactly as before. That is one quorum check, not two. Under a quorum protocol K can accept and still not be admitted ("accepted, awaiting the group").

**How an invitation and its answer travel (normative).** This carriage is for a room seated by identity keys: a family, a public room, and a room whose roster its members can read. An invitation and its answer each travel as a sealed envelope of ordinary rows. Each is sealed end to end to the recipient's occurrence key, so a carrier checks what it carries without opening it ([CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6)). The invitation carries the `membership:proposal` and the inviter's occurrence rows, and nothing of the room's roster. The answer carries the `membership:acceptance`, the joiner's occurrence rows, and the joiner's owner-binding re-signed at the room's scope ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). Once the widening seats the joiner, the cohort's ordinary delivery serves it the roster, the members' occurrences and their bindings placed at the room. The welcome carries nothing more. An invitation is sealed to a key the inviter already holds. So a person with no announced node is invited only after a contact has been exchanged ([CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6)). The envelope is no family and adds no member to any row: it holds rows that exist.

**Admission (normative).** A widening seats a key K not active in the group only if all hold:

- (1) an admitted `membership:acceptance:v1` by K references a proposal P for the same group (and, on a widening that assigns one, the same `role`);
- (2) P was neither declined nor withdrawn;
- (3) the member who concludes P's window held the acceptance before P's `expires_at`, read on that member's own clock;
- (4) the widening is that member's landing, signed while P's window is open on its own clock; on a counted widening that member's statement is one voice, and further voices may land later within the hold window of [CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.4);
- **(5) P has not already seated K** (an acceptance is spent by the widening that seats it, so a member who resigns is not re-seated on the old acceptance).

**Expiry closes a window**, as the kernel states ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). P's `expires_at` is P's own stated end, and a late acceptance is closed. The member who concludes reads it on its own clock and signs the widening as the landing, so every node reads the same landing.

**A role change.** A role change for an already-active member is not growth and needs no acceptance. A duty seat is the exception: it carries the holder's own acceptance ([CC 4.5.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.4)).

**A duty seat (normative).** A community's record declares its duties, and community law is stated once, at [CC 4.5.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.4). A duty seat is two consents, the placer's and the holder's, as an admission is the group's and the joiner's. A founding record seats the duty holders it names, each by their own signature on it. The founding confers no standing beyond the seats its signers accepted.

**A geographic community.** Geographic's `location_proof` is required **in addition**, never instead ([CC 4.4.3.6](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.6)).

**Two readings the membership model (pinned by the register) fixes:** A proposal seats a key at most once, so the standing proposal of an open room seats each requester once ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). A widening that cites an acceptance a widening in its past has already spent concludes nothing, so one invitation never admits the same key twice. Two concurrent widenings citing one acceptance are contested until a row naming both decides. Under `unanimous` a removal is signed by every other active member *and* is a strict majority of the roster. The two coincide above two members and diverge at two, where the one other member is not a majority. A two-member roster removes nobody by this door, and resignation is the exit.

**A supersede never adds a member (normative).** A new version of a `family` or `community` record may change its metadata, and may keep, re-list or drop members. It never seats anyone: a key that a roster-growing supersede adds is not counted as a member. Every addition goes through the widening plane, where the proposal's own stated end closes a late acceptance (expiry, above). There is one exception, which consent already covers. An `infrastructure` community's founders' amendment may seat a key that **signed** that version. Founder seats of such a community are added only by that amendment or by the one T7 recovery widening ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)).

**Founding (normative).** A founding record seats a listed member iff that member **signed** the record, as its authority or a co-signer. A family record carries `additional_scrubs` as a community record does. Signing is consent. A listed member who did not sign is not seated and joins only by proposal and acceptance. This is what makes a multi-founder `quorum:M/N` community possible to found at all. The same holds for the birth row of a room named `ciris-canonical`, whose founders, the accord's holders ([CC 3.4.1](#3.4.1)), each sign it once after the genesis. The T7 recovery widening complies for the same reason: the named key signs it ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). In a private room each listed member signs the founding record as a room key, and holds every other listed member's binding before signing. The record lists its members in `members`, each by its `key_id`, read as an identity.

**A node gives no acceptance (normative).** The consent this section requires is the joiner's own: a person's, or an agent's under its own key. A key whose `identity_type` includes `node` has no agency and is never asked for an acceptance ([CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.7.1)). A node member of an `infrastructure` community is seated by the founders' quorum on the widening alone. A canonical serve node is seated to serve by the bundle's `serve_nodes` ([CC 3.2](#3.2) T2), and the bundle seats it in no room.

**What a verifier checks:** A node's seat in an `infrastructure` community is valid when the founders' quorum signed the record that seats it ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). A serve seat stands by the bundle that names it: the accord's genesis bundle seats the node by its own count and rides no key record ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). The node's owner claim is enforced **where the node operates**, not where the roster is verified ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)). The owner-binding is written at `self` scope and only its audience reads it. The owner MAY re-sign it wider ([CC 3.2](#3.2)), and a `serve` seat requires it at `federation` ([CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6)). Carrying it in the bundle instead would publish a person-to-node custody edge to the whole federation.

**A node at founding.** The same holds at founding. A node listed in an `infrastructure` community's founding record is seated by the founders' signatures on that record and never signs it. So the founding rule above (every listed member signed) counts only the persons it lists ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)). A node's standing is still serve, store and replicate, never a vote (CC 3.2, *Infrastructure does not vote*).

**Refusals.** Each reason below is surfaced as the existing `hard_case:community_consensus_protocol_violation` (and the family twin) with a named rule. A RETRYABLE reason waits for the row it names. A reason that reads a row the widening does not name (a decline, a withdrawal, a second reply) concludes nothing for that widening, which seats no one; the code names the reason reported:

- RETRYABLE `membership_acceptance_unresolved` (no acceptance held yet — rows arrive out of order);
- RETRYABLE `membership_proposal_unresolved` (the answer's proposal not held);
- RETRYABLE `membership_binding_ack_unresolved` (a private room's widening cites a duty holder's receipt not held yet);
- terminal `membership_declined`;
- terminal `membership_proposal_expired` (a withdrawn proposal counts as expired);
- terminal `membership_acceptance_mismatch` (group, hash or role);
- terminal `membership_reply_conflict` (both an acceptance and a decline by K to one proposal);
- terminal `membership_founding_member_unsigned`;
- terminal `membership_supersede_cannot_add`.

**Decline, withdrawal, expiry.** `expires_at` is REQUIRED on a proposal, after its `asserted_at` and at most 30 days later. A decline is terminal for its proposal. Two opposite replies by the same K to the same proposal are contested, and neither counts while they differ ([CC 2.7.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.7) rule 6). Asking again is a **new** proposal. The inviter withdraws a proposal with the ordinary `withdraws`. A growth already admitted is never re-judged. Leaving is the member's own `membership:resignation`, which reaches forward only.

**Why K is named in `subject_key_ids`.** The invitee cannot be named in `attested_key_id` under the producer rule of [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1). `subject_key_ids` is the member that already carries consent authority over a Contribution ([CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3)) and is the key the substrate delivers on. A proposal is readable by, and applied on, any node whose self-collective contains that entry, without that node holding the group's roster. In a private room K is the invitee's room key, and the sealed invitation carries no proposal. The proposal names K only after the invitee returns it. It reaches the invitee over the same sealed exchange, and never by delivery on an identity.

**Not a membership rule: reverse quorum.** The reverse-quorum brake of [CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13) governs objection to commons acts. It admits no one and confers no consent on anyone's behalf.

**Who may write (normative).** A room's record MAY name who may publish in it. That is a `publish` right carried as the `role` a membership proposal offers and an acceptance restates, under the room's own protocol. So a member may hold it or not, and the others read. Where the record names no such right every member writes. A member without the right is a member in every other respect. They read, they hold standing over any row that names them ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5)), they vote where the protocol gives them a vote, and they resign or are removed like any member. A row they write elsewhere may name a row of the room, as any row may name any row within its audience; it does not enter the room. This is the one form of a post that cannot be replied to in place: a room where the right is held by few, which is a channel. No author forbids another member's row in a room where that member may write.

**A room's content after a member's seat ends (normative).**

*Which rows.* The content of a room is the rows of the families that the family table marks `room_content`: a chat message and a reaction, a file, a collection and the media families. Every other row placed in a room is read as [CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1) reads an act.

*The series.* A content row names in `refs.prev` a content row its author signed in the same room, where its producer holds one. It MAY name further such rows in `refs.further_prev`, and a producer SHOULD name every other tip it holds, so that branches rejoin. The first row of an author in a room names none. No reader judges the choice. Two rows that name no predecessor are two branches. A content row does not wait for a row it names this way.

*The tips.* A row that ends a member's seat, a `membership:removal` or a `membership:resignation`, names in `refs.trusted_through` the newest content rows of that member that its signers hold good. Those rows are the tips. A counted `membership:keeps` row names further tips for one end, which it cites in `refs.also.cites`, and it names the roster head it is counted over. `refs.trusted_through` holds at most 64 rows on any row, and a row with more is refused, `trusted_through_too_many`. A `keeps` row that cites no end of that member's seat concludes nothing, `keeps_cites_no_end`. Neither row waits for a tip. The seat ends when the end counts, and a tip keeps nothing until it is held.

*What is kept.* While a member sits, every content row they signed at a head they sat at is in the room's content. After an end of the seat counts, a content row of that member is in the room's content only where a tip holds it good. A tip holds good itself and every row it reaches through `refs.prev` and `refs.further_prev` over rows of the same author in that room. A predecessor that is another author's row, or a row of another room, is not followed. A tip at a head later than the end's, or with the end in its past, holds nothing good. Every other content row of that member counts at its own head and is not in the room's content, on every node that holds the end.

*Whose tips.* Where a counted end of the seat counts, only the tips of counted rows are read: those of every counted end and of every `keeps` row. A member's own resignation names tips that are read only where no counted row ends the seat. A second resignation only narrows them, and a `keeps` row adds to them. A `keeps` row that the member alone signs is never read. So once an end counts, nothing the member signs puts a row into the room's content. Whether an end counts depends on its own past alone, and no row signed later changes it.

*A later seat.* A seat is one stay: it begins at the roster version that admits the member and ends with an end of that stay. A row belongs to the seat whose heads it names, whenever it was signed. So a row that names an old head after the member is admitted again belongs to the old seat. A row that names a head at which the member did not sit belongs to no seat and is never in the room's content. Each seat is read by its own ends, tips and `keeps` rows. A later seat restores nothing an earlier end left out, and a `keeps` row MAY still name tips for the earlier end. A tip holds good only rows of its own seat, and a tip that names a row of another seat holds nothing good. An end that names an old head ends the old seat only. The member's own rows are those any key of that member signs.

*Edits and retractions.* An edit, a `supersedes` by the author, is a content row like any other, and an edit signed after the end is not in the room's content. A retraction by the author of their own row takes effect whenever it is signed, in whichever seat ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1), rule 1), since it can only remove.

*What it does not touch.* No key grant is withdrawn and nothing is wrapped again ([CC 4.4.3.22](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.22)). A stream's chunks and a blob's bytes follow the row that carries them. No content row is receipted.

*Reads.* A read that a host renders as the room returns the room's content as stated here. Replication, a read as of a head and an audit read return every row held. A store keeps an end's tips through a purge, since a tip may arrive later.

*Stated, and not decided.* A tip that never arrives keeps nothing. A resigning member MAY name a tip they have signed and have not published, and its id fixes it. This entry does not say how a reader's line bounds two ends at one head, nor what the removal of one of a member's keys does to that key's rows.

*Checked.* The rule is the one the kernel's `content` module computes (kernel-v0.2.2), checked by its exhaustive run over the vendored fixture `conferral_content.json` (the kernel's `CONFERRAL_END.md`, section I), and it is not a TLC result.

**A community declares how its roster is seated (normative).** The founding row of a `community` carries `membership`, which is `private` or `public`. A community whose `membership` is `private` is a **private room**, and it seats voices as the paragraphs below state. A community whose `membership` is `public` seats identity keys, as this entry states above. A founding row with no `membership` reads `public`, since a room founded without it seats identity keys and is public in fact. A node that founds a community writes `private` unless the signers of its founding record chose `public`. An `infrastructure` community and a designated body ([CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3)) MUST declare `public`, since others read their rosters. One that declares `private` is refused, at its founding and at a later version, `membership_private_refused`. An affiliation is not a designated body and MAY be private. A private affiliation's voices are room keys, which sign nothing outside it, so it cosigns no binding and confers no licence that is read outside it. A room MAY move from `private` to `public` by a new version of its record under its `consensus_protocol`. A room never moves from `public` to `private`, since what was signed under identity keys stays provable. A version that declares `private` over a `public` room concludes nothing, `membership_public_to_private`. After such a move new seats are identity keys, a voice seated before it stays a voice, and the move makes nothing signed under it provable. A `self` room and a `family` carry no `membership` and are seated by identity keys. A record of either that carries it is refused, `membership_not_a_community`. `membership` states how a roster is seated and nothing about who reads the content, which `cohort_subkind` states ([CC 3.2](#3.2)).

**A private room seats voices (normative).** In a private room the roster seats a **voice** and never an identity. A voice is a small counted roster of **room keys**, one for each device of its holder. A room key is a hybrid key pair that one device makes for this room only. Every row of the room is signed under a room key: speech, a vote, an admission, a removal, an acknowledgement and every other act of governance. A duty holder, a member, the subject of a row and the recipient of a wrap are each a voice or a room key, and never an identity key. A room key's self-signed `key:record` row travels with the room's rows, and the row that seats the key names it under `refs.also.cites`. The record names the key's one room in `room`, and the key has standing in that room only. A room key states no required end. A room key speaks in the room while it holds a seat in its voice and the voice holds its seat in the room. Its seat in the voice is ended by the voice's own count or by the key's own withdrawal. Its liveness as a key ends only by its own revocation ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). Its record states its `identity_type` as any key's does ([CC 3.4.7.1](#3.4.7.1)), so an agent's room key says that it is an agent's. A count in the room counts voices, however many room keys sign. A room key MUST NOT be used in a second room, and a member admitted again makes a fresh one. A row of another room signed under a room key is refused, `room_key_other_room`. A room key never takes an `identity_occurrence` row or an owner-binding outside the room, since either would tie it to an identity in public. Such an occurrence is refused, `room_key_occurrence_outside_room`, and such an owner-binding is refused, `room_key_binding_outside_room`. A node signs into the room under a room key it holds for that room, and never under its node key. A row of a private room signed under an identity key or a node key is refused, `room_row_signer_not_room_key`. That door reads the seat the row is signed for and not the room alone, since identity keys sign for the seats made after a move to `public`.

**A voice and its keys (normative).** A voice is named by the identity reference of its first room key. The name outlives that key, as a fedID outlives its genesis key ([CC 3.3.6.4](#3.3.6.4)). A voice's keys are a roster of its own, kept as the key roster of a self is kept, and it is not a `group:roster`. A further room key is seated by an `identity:occurrence` placed in the room. That row names the voice in `identity_key_id` and the new key in `occurrence_key_id`. It is counted over the voice's live keys under the policy row `self_roster_add` ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)), and the new key cosigns it. No grant from the first key seats a further key. One room key is never copied to several devices. On every row of the room `iss` is the voice and `kid` is the room key that signed, and a content row's `author` is the voice. Every such row names the head of the voice's key roster under the `refs.also` role `voice`, exactly one row ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). A row concludes only if the room key that signed it is a live key of the voice at that head.

**An agent's voice and a node's room key (normative).** An agent's room key is a voice of its own, and an agent's voice is one room key. An agent's occurrence is single-signer and runs neither path of the self-roster door ([CC 3.3.6.4](#3.3.6.4)). With one key, the voice's own count is that one key, so a stolen key would seat a second with nobody to object. So an agent's voice seats no further key by its own count. A second room key of an agent, for another device of the agent or after a loss, is a second voice. The room admits it by its own count, as it admits any joiner, with its own acceptance and its own in-room owner-binding ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). A node's room key is neither a voice nor a member. It is a key owned in the room by a member's room key, through the in-room owner-binding ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). It is never counted. In a private room no allow list applies on top of a held room key, since a `consent:replication` grant that named a room key would tie an identity to it in a row. The choice for each device there is whether the device makes a room key.

**The binding (normative).** The statement that a voice is a given person's is the **binding**. It is never a row, and nobody signs it. It is a fact made for one addressee, which the addressee can check. The addressee can show others only that the room key's holder named the person, and the person's part stays deniable. A binding is made for each room key of a voice, and a node accepts one only when it was made for that node. It is made to the addressee's room key, never to a node key. The seat row of a room key is that key's own record. It carries a **commitment** to its person, which the binding opens. A binding that does not open the commitment is refused, and so is one whose confirmation does not open or that was made for another key. Those refusals are the addressee's own: a binding is no row, so no door names them. Standing in the room is read from its rows, and no rule of standing reads a binding. A binding is read to show a member who spoke, to check a joiner before a widening, and to count persons. So any holder of a room's rows can read standing in it, and only a node holding the bindings can tell from them who is in the room or who said what ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)).

**Invitation to a private room (normative).** No row names the invitee's identity. The inviter sends the invitee a sealed invitation, which nobody signs. The invitee makes a room key and returns it the same way. The invitation carries no proposal. Only then does the proposal name that room key in `subject_key_ids`, and the acceptance is signed under it. The checks of this entry then run on room keys as written. A member's node MUST NOT cosign a widening until it holds the joiner's binding, and until then its cosignature waits, `widening_binding_not_held`. It MUST NOT cosign one whose binding names a person already seated. Both checks are the cosigner's own, and no door refuses a widening for either, since no rule of standing reads a binding. So a person gains a second voice only where every signer of that admission failed to check.

**A binding before a seat (normative).** Each cosigner of a widening, each founder and a seated duty holder holds a joiner's binding before the row it signs. A duty holder holds no content key and receives no wrap. So the three flows of a binding also ride a sealed envelope addressed to one room key, outside any content-key wrap ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). The sealed invitation and its sealed return carry the flows between the inviter and the joiner. The same envelope, addressed to each cosigner, to each founder and to the duty holder, carries them before the admission row. Every flow is restartable from public state. The addressee keeps the pending secret on its device, and a lost one costs a fresh challenge. No model checks this carriage. A count of persons waits at a node that does not hold a binding, which is a stall at that node and never a fork.

**A count of persons waits for the bindings (normative).** A count of persons ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)) reads the bindings a node holds. Until a node holds the binding of every room key seated in the room, that count is missing at that node, and the node says which key it lacks. The count is held, `person_count_binding_missing`, with the room keys lacked as its detail. A withheld binding is a stall at that node and never a fork. Two nodes that hold the bindings reach the same count. A node that is no member's holds no binding, cannot count persons, and is not asked to.

**What travels, and what does not (normative).** A reply carries the row it answers to whoever receives the reply in that room, and that carriage of content is intended ([CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2)). What MUST NOT travel is proof of who said it or of who is in the room. A row of a private room that its own signer carries elsewhere shows that some room key signed it, and names no person.

**What a private room does not give (stated).** Deniability against a member who cheats in the exchange, under a post-quantum key exchange, is conjectured and not proved. A member who cooperates with an outsider while a binding is made can prove what it sees. A member can always say who is in the room and who said what: the room key removes the proof and never the witness. One signed row by a person outside the room, tying a room key to themself, makes that person's history in the room provable. A room whose rows were signed under identity keys stays provable. A member can deny being the person behind a room key. A room key cannot deny its MLS traffic, which the leaf's signature and the vouch tie to it ([CC 5.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.1)). The vouch names nothing of the person. A removed member keeps the bindings it was given. A custody claim and delivery still reach a node. A network observer learns which nodes receive a room's rows, unless delivery goes by the Anonymous Tier ([CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6)). A new key record appears when someone joins, so a holder of the rows sees that a joining happened and when. Erasure by person finds a person's rows in such a room only through that person's own devices, which keep the list of their room keys. A private room is out of reach of an order that names a person, except by testimony or by a member's device.

**The wire of a private room (normative).** The record of a room key, the commitment it carries, the `iss` of a row, the three flows of a binding, the wrap to a room key and the HPKE parameters are those of [CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11). The commitment is a hash over the room, the room key, the person and fresh random bytes, and the binding carries the opening. The binding is two encapsulations and no signature. One is a challenge that only the person's identity can open: an encapsulation to the person's binding key. The other is a confirmation that the recipient could also have produced: a seal to the addressee's room key, keyed also by the challenge's secret. The confirmation's AEAD authenticates the opening under both shared secrets, so a separate MAC adds no property. The person's claim, the challenge and the confirmation ride inside the sealed plaintext of a room-key wrap, which is a `key_grant` row. Those wraps already flow in each direction between two members, so a binding adds no row. No flow is a cleartext member of a row, and none rides an MLS Welcome. A wrap's own encapsulation is never the confirmation. An identity keeps a key pair for bindings that is distinct from its content-KEM pair ([CC 3.3.6.1](#3.3.6.1)). A wrap for a member is made to the KEM half of the recipient room key's own record. The addressee challenges first, and one exchange is made for each room key with a fresh challenge. The invitation is sealed to the invitee, so the proposal names the room key only after the invitee returns it.

#### 3.1.3.3 `custody` — `custody:*` — which of a cohort's own devices hold a blob, and which hold none (normative)

**The rule.** A family needs to see how many copies of its content exist — "only one copy, back it up" before a phone dies — without weakening encryption or outsider invisibility.

- (1) Within-cohort custody discovery is consistent with [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2): structural invisibility, and the "wire discovery: none" of the `self` / `family` tiers ([CC 4.4.3.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.4)), mean invisibility to those **outside** the cohort.
- (2) The report is its own leaf, `custody:ack:v1`, and it is the **one** holding claim at every tier, placed at the content's own scope, so no row shape exists that could advertise a bounded cohort's holdings to outsiders.
- (3) **"No copy here is a receipt (node responsive, no copy)"**: a device's signed `none` is a custody fact in its own right, the counterpart of a [CC 5.3.3.11](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.3.11) delivery receipt.

**Registry row (CC 3.1.7 R1).**

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custody:{kind}` | Within-cohort custody reports. `{kind}` ∈ `ack` — closed; wire `custody:ack:v1`. One report per device per blob: the blob's address digest, `custody_state` `here` \| `none`, and the signer-stamped instant; `here` also carries the blob's `size`. Placed at the blob's own `cohort_scope` and replicated only within that cohort. | positive-only | **Yes — holder self-report:** `attesting_key_id` is the device the report is about; nobody reports custody for another device |

**Scope and invisibility (normative).** A custody report is placed at the content's own `cohort_scope` by rule (1) below, and reaches only the audience of that scope ([CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2)). It carries nothing about the blob beyond its address, size and the device; the blob's name and format stay in the sealed descriptor ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13)). An outsider learns nothing it did not learn before.

**One holding claim at every tier (normative).** `custody:ack:v1` is the holding claim of the mesh, at every tier. A row typed with the retired `holds_bytes` token ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4)) is refused: the row-type slot admits only the five. Five rules. **(1) Scope is the content's.** A report is placed at the `cohort_scope` of the blob it is about: `self`, `family`, `community` or `affiliations` for a bounded cohort, **`federation` for Commons and `public` content**. A report waits for the content it names, and where that content's scope is not the report's, the report concludes nothing. An emitter never chooses a scope constant. **(2) Audience follows from the one rule.** Who receives a report is the audience of [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2), resolved by [CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3): the cohort's roster, its members' claimed nodes under each owner's allow list. At federation scope that audience is everyone, and the `here` rows **are** the holder directory a consumer reads to find holders ([CC 5.3.2.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.2.1)); at a bounded scope they are the within-cohort custody view and nothing else. **(3) A holding claim is never a content binding.** It says where bytes are, not that they may stay: a withdrawn or tombstoned blob is not live because a device still reports holding it ([CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3) bytes plane). The bytes-plane fold MUST read liveness from the content's own rows only. **(4) Retracted by its signer alone.** A device ends its own report by re-acknowledging `none` or by `withdraws`; nobody withdraws another device's report, and a takedown is the [CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3) tombstone path, not a withdrawal of holders. **(5) Freshness is the row's.** The 72-hour window below is the claim's `expires_at`; no second TTL exists. With these, "holding claims at every tier, bounded to the cohort" ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)) is true at every tier with no exception clause.

**A holding claim in a private room (normative).** For content of a private room ([CC 3.1.3.2](#3.1.3.2)) a holding claim is signed under the room key the holding node keeps for that room, and never under its node key. The claim then names no person to whoever holds it. It does not hide the holder from the network that carries the bytes.

**Freshness (normative).** A report is **live for 72 hours** from its instant, and a responsive device re-acknowledges about **daily**. A report older than 72 hours reads as *unknown*: a lost device stops counting within three days, while a phone that is off for a weekend still counts. A device that drops a blob re-acknowledges `none`.

**What a cohort member sees, per device.**

- **here** — a live `here` report;
- **received** — a [CC 5.3.3.11](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.3.11) delivery receipt with no later live report;
- **none** — a live `none` report;
- **unknown** — no live report.

The count of *here* is the number of known copies; a UI MUST NOT present *unknown* as *none*, nor a lapsed `here` as a copy.

**No possession challenge yet (stated).** A `here` report is trusted as signed by the device: nothing on the wire yet asks the device to prove it still holds the bytes. Possession challenges for custody reports are not yet defined. The residual is named: a device that lies, or a device whose storage has silently rotted, is counted as a copy until its report lapses or it is challenged once challenges exist. CC 6.1.5's **N6** is unchanged and still governs a holding claim counted toward an item's rarity: until a challenger exists a holding claim weighs by what backs it (possession verified 2, signature only 1, unverified 0). No challenger is defined in this edition. A custody report is a separate, within-cohort count and is not thereby a possession-bound claim.

#### 3.1.3.4 `files` — `file:*` and `collection:*` — files, and directories of them (normative)

**The rule.** A file is one row per file placed in a cohort, with name and type sealed ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13)). Directories are objects in their own right, so a directory can be promoted, moved, renamed, withdrawn and shared as one thing.

**Registry rows (CC 3.1.7 R1).**

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file:{version}` | A file: one row per file, placed at a `cohort_scope`, its bytes addressed by digest and described by the [CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13) Source struct, name and format inside the sealed descriptor. Wire `file:v1`. | positive-only | **Yes — author-emitted:** the file's author (or a device that author acts through) |
| `collection:{kind}` | A collection of files that is an object in its own right. Canonical kind `directory` (wire `collection:directory:v1`); `{kind}` open per [CC 4.5.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.1.1), leaving room for albums or playlists. Its name and its own `parent` live in its sealed descriptor, exactly as a file's do. | positive-only | **Yes — author-emitted:** the collection's creator; an amendment (rename, move) is its author's, or the cohort's under its `consensus_protocol` where the cohort's rules say so; a row that is the cohort's act is counted ([CC 2.6.1.9](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.9)), and every other row is authored |

**Identity and membership (normative).** A directory's identity is the attestation id of its creating row, carried forward by `supersedes` under the [CC 3.5.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.5.1) stable-id grouping; renaming or moving it is a `supersedes` of that row. A file's or a directory's membership in a directory is **`parent`, carried inside its own sealed descriptor** — the containing directory's stable id, sealed with the name. There is no edge row: the tree's shape is sealed at every scope, including `community`, so no holder learns how many items a directory holds. With no edge row, moving a file is one write — the child's row re-sealed with a new `parent`. Placing one's own file in a directory needs no one's leave but that file's author.

**Promotion is one intent, executed as N crossings (normative).** Every widening is an act on specific bytes: [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2) emits on the new Contribution, and promotion is the federation-emit moment ([CC 5.3.2.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.2.6)). The perceptual-hash tripwire fires at a promotion into the Commons and at a post into a `public` room, and never inside a private cohort ([CC 1.13.3.4](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.3.4)). A collection-level crossing would be the one way to publish bytes without that tripwire, so none exists and no folder key is ever minted. Promoting a directory is a `supersedes` of the directory row at the wider scope — the intent. The promoting author's node carries out that intent as one ordinary promotion per file that author owns, each with its own emission, reporting any it did not widen and why. A crossing that enters the Commons or a `public` room has its own tripwire.

**A directory's scope is a default, never a floor (normative).** A file placed in a directory is placed at the directory's scope at that instant, by its author's own act. A file its author pinned narrower stays narrower, and widening the directory never drags it. Narrowing a directory is forward-only: it changes the default for later placements and MAY withdraw the author's own wider copies; it un-publishes nothing.

**No consent for anyone else's files (normative).** A directory promotion widens **only the promoting author's own files**. No collection act stands in for an author's revocation authority over their own rows ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1) rule 1, [CC 5.3.2.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.2.5)) — the principle [CC 3.1.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.2) states for membership. Another author's files in a shared directory receive a widening **request**, which that author's node acts on only on that author's acceptance. Every per-file gate still binds: a non-author subject's consent ([CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3), [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1)) and the minor protections of [CC 3.4.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.13). A directory act inherits every gate and bypasses none.

**Custody at the directory tier** is a query over the per-file custody receipts of CC 3.1.3.3, filtered by `parent`; it needs no row of its own.

### 3.1.4 `transport-delivery` — CIRISEdge — transport, delivery, reachability

**Steward**: the transport. Substrate-self-reports per [CC 3.4.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.3).

Canonical leaves: `transport:{kind}`, `delivery:{class}`, `peer_reachability:{network}`, `key_boundary:{scope}`. Polarity: signed. See [CC 8.1](part_8_appendices.md#8.1) Edge leaf glossary.

Edge also emits on the one `system:*` family registered at [CC 3.1.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3), under its own `identity_type` ([CC 3.4.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.3)).

`delivery_ack:{stream_id}` is Edge's too, and is registered here rather than left to [CC 3.4.6](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.6) prose: subscriber-emitted, membership-gated, **not** a substrate-self-report. Polarity: signed. Emitter rule and the validated-not-adjudicated discipline: [CC 3.4.6](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.6).

#### Transport-capacity leaf (registry row)

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capacity:relay_delivery` | A consuming node's **measurement** of a relay's delivered-versus-claimed A/V throughput over a window, keyed to the relay's own `SignedRelayCapacity` claim `(advertiser_key_id, stream_id, epoch)`: the envelope `score` is the fulfilment ratio, never a verdict. Subject = the relay (`attested_key_id`), attester = the consumer (`attesting_key_id`), `attestation_type: scores`, wire `capacity:relay_delivery:v1`. Edge names the leaf and owns its semantics; the honesty score proper is LensCore's, composed fleet-wide with multi-observer corroboration. **A measure the subject cannot contest is an accusation:** a row of this leaf carries standing against a relay only when it binds the relay's own countersignature over the window measured, or a commitment to the chunks it covers, so that two colluding parties cannot mint a score and a relay cannot choose its auditors by withholding its grant; a row without either is a consumer's note and weighs nothing. | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)**: the `capacity:` stem's two gates, no-self-emit and consent-before-scoring |

**A `capacity:` leaf owned outside LensCore (normative).** Three things this row settles. *Leaf ownership and family policy are different things.* The component that owns the measured mechanism names the leaf (edge owns the A/V delivery vocabulary). Both [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5) gates bind the leaf regardless of owner: `attesting_key_id ≠ attested_key_id`, and admission only over a subject holding a live grant whose `scope` names `analyze`. *It is not a factor of the capacity score.* `capacity:relay_delivery` is a transport-plane leaf about a node. The leaf is never one of the five factors of [CC 3.1.8.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.8.1) and MUST NOT enter `capacity:composite`, whose `min` runs over exactly `C, I_int, R, I_inc, S`. *The consent addressee at a pair.* CC 3.4.5 addresses the `analyze` grant to the scoring community. A relay and its consumer are a pair, and here the grant covers the attesting consumer — the relay's `consent:state:granted` with scope `analyze` resolving `Granted` for that consumer through the substrate's one scoped-consent fold. That is the same predicate a node re-checks before it serves the row, and the emitter withholds on (a named withhold, never a silent drop). This is not the accountability case. Because the measurement is taken against a claim the relay itself signed, it could be argued to be *accountability*, which [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5) says consent never gates. It is not that case, because the row is filed as a `capacity:*` score about the relay and feeds LensCore's fleet-wide honesty composition, which is consensual reputation. A further reason is that one leaf carved out of the family's gate would be the ungated transmission principle the reservation exists to close. A mesh whose relays have not yet minted their `analyze` grant on latch therefore emits nothing on this leaf, by design (the plane opens when subjects open it) ([CC 3.4.5](#3.4.5)).

#### MLS leaf vouch (registry row)

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mls:leaf_vouch` | **A member's vouch for the MLS leaf key of one of its devices ([CC 5.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.1)).** The member's device key signs one row that names, as blinded elements, the leaf key, the room and the suite for each room it vouches in. It states `valid_from` and a required `valid_until`. The row's type is `scores` and its wire leaf is `mls:leaf_vouch:v1`. It is catalogued here because the transport owns the MLS group, its leaves and the door that reads the vouch. | positive-only | **Yes — self:** the signer is the member whose leaf it is, under that member's own key on the device; nobody vouches for another member's leaf, and a node key never vouches |

#### Rendezvous route leaf (registry row)

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rendezvous:route` | **A receiver's published route for targeted delivery through the Anonymous Tier ([CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6)).** A federation-scope row whose attester and subject are one **rendezvous key**: a fresh hybrid key pair for each rotation period, unlinkable to the receiver's identity because it is fresh (ML-DSA has no blinding). Its `key:record:v1` row travels inline in the payload, so a sender holding only this row can verify it; the key's `identity_type` is `rendezvous`, and it has no occurrence and no standing: a key plane refuses a rendezvous key offered as an identity with `federation_rendezvous_key_not_an_identity`. Payload: `format` (`"outfox-xwing-v1"`), `period` (`floor(unix_seconds / 3600)`), `valid_from` (the period's start), `valid_until` (the period's end plus one grace period), `rendezvous_node_key_id` (the layer-3 serve seat whose mailbox holds the receiver's packets; it MUST be a seat), `route_blob_base64` (the reply header for the receiver's three hops, sealed per hop to that period's hop keys), `rendezvous_key_record` (the inline key record). A route whose `rendezvous_node_key_id` names a key holding no serve seat is not used, since a seat stands only by the consents that place it. **Reach:** everyone, as on the bootstrap planes, because no sender is Rooted with a key that lives for one period. **Retention:** the current period plus one grace period; each period's row stands alone under its fresh key and supersedes nothing, since `supersedes` is by the same attester ([CC 2.4.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1)); a row is purgeable after `valid_until`; never a `hard_case`, never a durable item. **One route per period, used many times:** each relay can count the packets addressed to one rendezvous at its layer, which the rendezvous node sees anyway; the `format` member leaves room for a single-use variant. | signed | **Yes — self:** attester = subject = the period's rendezvous key; reach is federation-wide |

### 3.1.5 `accord-agent` — CIRISAgent — Accord principles + DMA + conscience + apophatic bounds

**Steward**: the agent runtime. This is where M-1 enters the namespace directly: the six principles, the four decision-making algorithms, the four consciences, and the apophatic bounds all become attestable dimensions.

#### Autonomy + explainability wire families (registry rows)

`consent:*` is `autonomy:` at the wire — the subject's own grant, scope and revocation over a Contribution about them; it **governs routing**, so leaving it unreserved would leave the transmission principle open. `trace:*` is `fidelity:explainability_sla:` at the wire — the artifact an `l2_reasoning_trace` / `l3_full_dma_chain` / `l4_attested_chain` commitment actually delivers.

| Prefix | Description | Polarity | Reserved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `consent:{kind}` | Subject-side consent authority over Contributions naming the subject in `subject_key_ids`, plus the producer-side and substrate-side leaves that close its lifecycle. Leaf catalogue, per-leaf polarity and the emitter class of each leaf: [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1); the directed node→peer grant `consent:replication:{version}`: [CC 3.3.7](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.7). **Open in its parameters, closed in its leaves** — the `{kind}` positions *within* a catalogued leaf are open vocabulary per [CC 4.5.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.1.1); a new leaf is admitted only once [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) catalogues it with an emitter class. | per-leaf ([CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1)) | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** |
| `consent:state:{stance}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the subject's stance on a Contribution, semantics at [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1). `{stance}` ∈ `granted` \| `revoked` \| `expired` — closed; `expired` is the one substrate-emitted value. | enumerated | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:stream:{kind}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); pre-packaged stream bundle, canonical kinds at [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1). | enumerated | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:deletion_sla:{days}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); the producer's time-to-delete-after-revoke commitment, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1). | signed | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:deletion_complete` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); producer's eviction attestation, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1). | positive-only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:decay:{stage}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); a decay-protocol stage, emitted by the party running the protocol, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1). | enumerated | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:partnership_grant` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); subject side of a bilateral grant, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) / [CC 4.4.3.28](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.28). | positive-only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:partnership_accept` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); producer side of a bilateral grant, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1). | positive-only | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
| `consent:scope:{kind}` | Catalogue row (CC 3.1.7 R1); a descriptive scope row — the scope of a grant is the `scope` envelope member of `consent:state:granted` ([CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1)). | enumerated | **Yes — [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5)** per-leaf emitter class, [CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.1) |
