The cost — a sovereign peer may probe other peers without raising the signal — is **bounded by construction**. `ratchet:flag:counter_rii:{layer}` is **advisory only** ([CC 3.1.6](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.6)): it can NEVER be sole evidence for `slashing:*`. The load-bearing adjudication gate is the `slash` duty-holder's verdict ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5)). The exemption suppresses an *advisory signal*, not an *enforcement path*.

**Post-window `AuthorizedReview`: strict.** An `AuthorizedReview` `consent_role` is signal-eligible **immediately** at `t > window_end` — no grace period ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). Matches the fail-secure / clean-state-machine grain ([CC 8.3.3](part_8_appendices.md#8.3.3)); reviewers MUST respect their windows.

Implementations MAY build the `consent_role` substrate. **1+4 untouched** — `consent_role` is a `federation_keys` identity field (sibling to [CC 3.4.7.1](#3.4.7.1) `identity_type`), not an envelope primitive.

#### 3.4.7.3 `actor-substrate` — The actor/substrate separation — `node` is exclusive, and agency reaches a node only through a common human (normative)

**This section is the canonical statement that infrastructure has no agency — and of its missing converse.** It restates the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) stewardship bullet (*"`node` (infrastructure) — steward + `infra:*` reach only, **never agency**"*) with a section number.

**Clause A — `node` is exclusive (normative).** A `federation_keys` key whose `identity_type` set contains `node` MUST NOT also contain `agent` or `user`. **A key is substrate or actor, never both.** [CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.7.1) permits role cohabitation generally; this is its one carved-out prohibition. The carve-out is at the **axis**, not at the role. `{substrate_persist, steward, lenscore_detector, witness}` co-location remains conformant (custody, not authority — the fabric-node discipline), because those roles sit on the same side of the actor/substrate line. `{node, agent}` does not. The defect it prevents is **axis fusion** — one key answering both *which node is this* and *which agent is this*. With such a key `owner_of()` resolves a person to an actor where a node was asked for, and no trace can say whether the substrate or the actor acted.

**Clause B — the agency gate reads membership, never purity (normative).** The prohibition on a node receiving `agency:*` fires whenever **`node ∈ recipient.identity_type`** — not only when the recipient resolves to a node-*only* identity. This governs the [CC 4.4.3.19](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.19) conformance rule: under a *"`node`-only (no `agent`/brain)"* qualifier, adding `agent` to a node's role-set would make the invariant stop firing. So **role-set union would repeal the property this rule exists to guarantee.** Clauses A and B are both required and neither substitutes for the other. **A** stops a fused key being *minted*. **B** is what protects the invariant against fused keys that **already exist**, since a non-conformant key is still a key in the data and still a possible delegation recipient.

**Clause C — the actor↔node relation is entailed, never asserted (normative).** There MUST NOT be a direct `agent → node` or `node → agent` edge. Neither party has standing to create one. A node has no agency to confer (infrastructure authorizing an actor). An agent has no authority over infrastructure (an actor asserting a fact about substrate it does not own). The human has standing and has already exercised it **twice** — the owner-binding (`human → node`, `infra:*` only, single-valued) and the stewardship delegation (`human → agent`, `agency:*`, multi-parent). The pairing is therefore **derived from two independently-gated, human-signed edges**. That is precisely why it cannot drift from them and cannot be forged unilaterally: an agent cannot grant itself a node, and a node cannot adopt an agent. A third stored edge would hold a fact the graph already entails and would be free to disagree with it. **No new structural primitive** — the [CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md#1.7) closed set is untouched; this is a predicate over edges that already exist.

**Clause D — the common-human predicate (normative).** An agent MAY act through a node **iff** one human stands at both corners:

```
may_act_through(agent, node) ≔
    ∃ h .  h = owner_of(node)  ∧  h ∈ stewards_of(agent)
```

The quantifier is **existential, and deliberately so**. Node ownership is single-valued ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)), so the test is that the node's one owner appears *somewhere in* the agent's steward set rather than that the agent has exactly one steward.

**`stewards_of` denotes the custody set, never the conferral set (normative).** It is the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) `is_steward_bound` anchor: the granter of the one live owner-binding `delegates_to`, and nothing else. That `delegates_to` is the edge carrying the [CC 2.4.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.2) owner-binding marker, per the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) conferral-is-not-stewardship discriminator. An unmarked `delegates_to(U → agent)` confers a **job, not custody**, and MUST NOT satisfy this clause. Reading `stewards_of` as *"every human who delegated agency"* would silently widen an authorization gate into a capability list.

**Cardinality (normative).** The steward set therefore has **at most one** member: the granter of the one live owner-binding. An `identity_occurrence` binds nothing and is no anchor ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). A key whose live counted bindings name a second *distinct* owner has no owner at all (the single-owner rule of [CC 3.2](#3.2)), and a same-owner refresh is idempotent. A design assuming N co-equal stewards of one agent is assuming a shape the substrate will not admit. **Fail-closed:** an unresolvable walk — owner absent, ambiguous owner, revoked edge — MUST refuse, and MUST NOT resolve to "unknown". This is the person/node axis, whose signature failure mode is a **silent withhold**; without the fail-closed half, an unresolved walk reads as permission.

**Clause E — the enforcement seam is the node's (normative wherever an authorization envelope is used).** Where an envelope authorizes an actor's work on a node, the **node** MUST verify, before executing:

- the human's signature on the envelope;
- the referencing agent's standing;
- **Clause D**; and
- scope match —

refusing otherwise, and refusing **by attestation** (`infra:attest` — *"vouch as the delegator's infrastructure"* — is already in the closed `infra:*` set, so a node may sign its own refusal without new authority). The full predicate at the seam is one human in three roles across three keys:

```
owner_of(node) == signer_of(envelope)  ∧  owner_of(node) ∈ stewards_of(agent)
```

**Infrastructure is the right enforcer precisely because it has no agency of its own to exercise** — a corollary of Clause A, not an exception to it. An actor that gates itself is the constrained party checking its own constraint. Moving the refusal to a key that cannot benefit from the decision is what makes it structural rather than procedural. It is also why the actor needs its **own** key: an agent signing with the node's key makes the envelope reference self-referential and the check vacuous.

**Clause F — fused keys are non-conformant, with no transition window (normative).** A key holding `node` together with an actor role is **non-conformant**, and no window softens it. The [CC 6.1.2.1](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.2.1) posture governs: no exempted producer, no window. Two precisions. **Forward-only** — the prohibition attaches to the *live configuration*, never retroactively to the record ([CC 2.7.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.7)). Attestations already signed by a fused key remain valid history, because an envelope cannot be amended, only superseded ([CC 4.5.9.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.9.3) — the audit chain preserves the historical claim), and re-minting the key backwards would retroactively re-author every historical trace. **And still gated** — a fused key that exists MUST still be refused `agency:*` under Clause B. Non-conformance is a reason to re-mint, never a reason the gate stops applying.

**Open, and named rather than filled.** Given the cardinality above, co-stewardship does not express the multi-tenant / community-server case directly. Clause D admits one shape: one human holding both corners. An `identity_occurrence` naming the node's owner adds no second shape, because an occurrence binds nothing ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). Everything else — an agent whose custody anchor excludes the node's owner — is **not admissible** here, and MUST NOT be reached by relaxing Clause D. A general hosting relation needs its own conferral from the node owner, on the node's `infra:*` plane where that owner has standing. Deferred, not denied: this is **most of the multi-tenant space**, not an exotic corner.

### 3.4.8 `detector-only` — Detector-only prefixes

`detection:*` is a detector's emission. The signer holds `infra:detect` under a root the reader trusts ([CC 3.4.7](#3.4.7)). Cross-attestation by non-LensCore peers (on the same dimension, attesting to the same subject) is admitted as a score on the detector's verdict. Such cross-attestation is useful when the federation wants to cross-check. Those scores MUST use a different `dimension` prefix (e.g., `truth_grounding:detection:correlated_action:{axis}`) to avoid shadowing the detector's own emission.

**The discriminator is the prefix, not an envelope field (normative — this is what makes the substrate gate a blanket rule).** Admission needs **no** `is_primary_detection` flag and **no** envelope-shape parsing. The prefix contract *is* the whole discriminator: **any** row whose `dimension` is under `detection:*` **is** a primary detector emission, and its signer MUST hold `infra:detect`. It **concludes nothing** otherwise. Under the same contract, a **cross-attestation** MUST ride the `truth_grounding:detection:*` prefix, which carries **no** `infra:detect` requirement (it is a score *on* the detector's verdict, not a shadowing re-emission of it). The substrate admission gate is therefore **expressible as** a blanket reserved-prefix rule over the `detection:*` **prefix-wildcard** — the [CC 3.4.7](#3.4.7) duty check, with no per-row shape inspection. The rule is over the wildcard so that novel `detection:{newkind}:*` subkinds are covered by construction, not only the two enumerated leaves.

**LensCore-fold worked example.** Where a detector is folded into an agent's runtime, one key holding both an agency delegation and `infra:detect` signs for both. The gate is satisfied for that key's `detection:*` rows by the `infra:detect` it holds; the agency delegation neither grants nor blocks the detector right. The split is preserved by the dimension namespace, not by the key: the same key emits its **agent-intent** attestations under the agent dimensions and its **detector verdicts** under `detection:*`. A downstream consumer cross-checking the detector still emits under the distinct `truth_grounding:detection:*` prefix above, shadowing-free. The [CC 3.4.5](#3.4.5) self-emission rejection continues to bind: a key holding both still MUST NOT emit a `capacity:*` score about itself.

### 3.4.9 `co-stewarded` — Co-stewarded prefixes

`licensure:{authority_id}` is co-stewarded between the registry ([CC 3.1.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.1)) and the verifier ([CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2)) — both MAY emit; consumers compose. Co-stewardship is of the **CIRIS-issued** licence — the `licensure` row itself ([CC 2.4.1.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.3)); the retired `partner_record` ([CC 3.3.9](#3.3.9)) constitutes nothing — and both stewards MAY record it. It is **not** a reservation of the family: `licensure:{authority_id}` is open-emitter ([CC 2.4.1.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.3) — anyone may be an authority under their own key; the fold keys on emitter-resolves-to-authority, and admission is the ordinary trust-or-consent gate). A substrate that reserves the family to `registry` / `verify` identity types has misread this clause. **Single-source attestations** (only one of the two co-stewards has emitted) MUST be marked as `confidence ≤ 0.5` in consumer composition until the second co-steward's attestation arrives.

### 3.4.10 `witness-emitter` — Witness-emitter reservations

The families `transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}`, `transparency_log:inclusion` and `transparency_log:consistency` are retired. A row of one of those names is refused `namespace_family_unregistered`. A Transparency Service's own signed act is its Receipt ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6), which is no attestation row and has no dimension.

**"Witness" names four different things, and none confers another (normative).** A reader MUST NOT infer one from another, and a substrate MUST NOT accept one where another is required:

| Sense | Where it lives | What makes a key one |
|---|---|---|
| `witness_relation` | envelope member ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1)) | Nothing — it is the signer's statement of its relation to the fact (`self` \| `external` \| `derived`), and confers no role |
| A **witness-reserved** family | `age_assurance:*`, `capacity_assurance:*` ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11), [CC 3.4.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.12)) | Holding `assure:age` or `assure:capacity` as a provider, authority or assessor for that ladder; "witness" there means *not the subject* |
| `testimonial_witness:*`, `witness_diversity:*` | dimension families ([CC 3.1.9.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.3)) | Nothing — any party may testify; these are claims, not roles |
| The wholeness witness; the privacy witness chain | [CC 6.1.1](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.1); [CC 5.4.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.5) | A node's own state-root commitments; neither is a role a key holds |

A monitoring node's `observation:reachability` rows ([CC 3.1.9.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.4)) are a fifth thing only in ordinary speech: the node witnessed its own probe, says so with `witness_relation: self`, and holds no witness role by doing it. A Transparency Service is none of these: it registers a statement in its own log and issues a Receipt ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6, [CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11), [CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)).

### 3.4.11 `age-assurance` — Age-assurance: the witness-reserved ladder, the subject self-declared rung, and the protective gate

Age-assurance is **two** dimension families, not one. The split is load-bearing: a provider/government attestation is a witness verdict and is **witness-reserved**; a subject's self-declaration is **not** an attestation about anyone but itself and rides a **distinct, non-reserved** prefix. A consumer unions both at read time, the witness rung outranks the self rung, and the gate's default is protective.

**The two prefixes (normative emitter rules).**

- **`age_assurance:`** is reserved to an age assessor. The signer holds `assure:age` under a root the reader trusts and is not the subject ([CC 3.4.7](#3.4.7)). `assure:age` is held by a person or an institution, never by the subject of the row. This is the provider/government rung: an age-assurance verifier attests a subject's band. A subject MUST NOT emit on `age_assurance:`; a row by any other signer concludes nothing at admission, a consumer re-checks, and a producer MUST NOT emit. A subject therefore cannot self-mint a `provider`/`government` adulthood.
- **`age_self_declared:`** — NON-reserved, subject-signed. The onboarding "state your age range" rung. Admitted iff the signer acts for the subject (the subject's own occurrence or an admitted occurrence of it). A self-declaration carries **only** the `{band}` — never a `{level}` token — because its level is `self` by construction.

**The band and the ladder.** `{band}` ∈ { `minor`, `adult`, `under_13`, `13_15`, `16_17` }, the closed set the [CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2) row registers (ordered by protection: a minor band is gated out of adult content, `adult` is not). `minor` is the coarse token a deployment that cannot resolve the band emits; the three sub-bands are finer and imply it. The assurance `AssuranceLevel` ladder is ascending confidence:

```
age dimension construction (the CC 3.1.7 R3 trailing :vN version segment is mandatory):

  self-declared rung (subject-signed, NON-reserved):
    age_self_declared:band:{band}:v1
      band ∈ { minor, adult, under_13, 13_15, 16_17 }
      e.g. age_self_declared:band:adult:v1

  provider / government rung (witness-RESERVED):
    age_assurance:{level}:{band}:v1
      level ∈ { provider, government }
      band  ∈ { minor, adult, under_13, 13_15, 16_17 }
      e.g. age_assurance:provider:adult:v1

assurance ladder (ascending confidence):
    self  <  provider  <  government

misdeclaration adjudication dimension:
    moderation:age_assurance_misdeclaration
```

The `self` rung of the ladder materializes on the non-reserved `age_self_declared:` prefix; the `provider`/`government` rungs materialize on the witness-reserved `age_assurance:` prefix carrying the `{level}` token. Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment. **`self` is not a value of `{level}`** and a producer MUST NOT emit `age_assurance:self:*`; a consumer MUST reject it as malformed rather than reading it as a self-declaration. These two arities — `age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version}` and `age_self_declared:band:{band}:{version}` — are the only shapes this Part registers, and the [CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2) rows and the [CC 3.3.12](#3.3.12) entry state them identically. A `provider` or `government` rung carries no further qualifier in the dimension. A leaf under `age_assurance:` outside these shapes is refused `namespace_family_unregistered` ([CC 3.1.7](#3.1.7)).

**Read-union — witness outranks subject (normative).** A consumer resolving an identity's age-assurance MUST union both prefixes and take the **highest** level on record. A witness-emitted `age_assurance:*` (provider/government) **OUTRANKS** a subject `age_self_declared:*`, with one exception. A subject's declaration of a lower band lowers the reading and never raises it ([CC 3.4.13](#3.4.13)). Absence of any row resolves to **None**, which MUST be treated as the most-protective band, `under_13` ([CC 3.4.13](#3.4.13) fail-secure) — see the gate. That reading governs what the person may see and do at community scope. Whether their node may announce is the fail-secure rule of [CC 3.4.13](#3.4.13).

**The protective gate (normative).** A viewer below `adult` assurance is **BLOCKED** from `adult` `content_class` ([CC 3.3.12](#3.3.12)). The default is protective, not permissive:

- `general`-class content is visible to everyone (protective ≠ prudish).
- `adult`-class content is visible ONLY to a viewer whose band is `adult`. The band opens this gate only at a verified level, `provider` or `government` ([CC 3.4.13](#3.4.13) Q3).
- A `minor` band, a "declined to state", and an "unknown"/absent assurance ALL resolve to the protective `minor` default and are BLOCKED. A "declined to state" and an "unknown"/absent assurance are further read as `under_13` ([CC 3.4.13](#3.4.13)).

The gate decides visibility only; it MUST NOT fire `slashing:*` on a mismatch.

**`self` is unfalsifiable — sensitive spaces require a verified level (normative).** The `self` rung is unfalsifiable from inside the fabric. A sensitive space MUST require a **verified** level (`provider`/`government`); bare `self` does NOT satisfy it. A consumer enforcing this checks the resolved level separately from the band. A `self`-level `adult` row graduates nobody up a band and satisfies no verified-level requirement ([CC 3.4.13](#3.4.13)).

**Misdeclaration is adjudicated, never slashed (normative).** A misdeclared age **NEVER** fires `slashing:*` alone. It routes to the `moderation:age_assurance_misdeclaration` adjudication path — a `moderation:{allegation_type}` ModerationEvent ([CC 3.1.9.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.2)) adjudicated by a holder of the `moderate` delegated duty ([CC 4.4.3.36](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.36) / [CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5)). No quorum binds that holder unless the community imposes one on itself ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)). **The data subject controls their own assurance level** — this is consistent with the [CC 3.1.9.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.2) `slashing`/`moderation` decoupling. **1+4 preserved** — `age_assurance:*` and `age_self_declared:*` are reserved/non-reserved `scores` dimensions; no new structural primitive.

### 3.4.12 `adult-incapacity-stewardship` — Adult stewardship under incapacity (capacity-triggered, court-adjudicated, fail-to-liberty)

This section states the rule for the stewardship of an adult under an attested loss of decisional capacity. It says when such a binding is admitted, what the steward may and may not do, what the ward keeps, and how the stewardship ends.

**The default is unchanged — an adult is sovereign and un-stewardable.** A user-target binding where `T` is an adult concludes nothing, except under the basis this section states ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). That is the fourth, un-stewardable case, and it holds ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). That wall is the no-slavery guarantee, and it does **not** move ([CC 1.14.6](part_1_foundation.md#1.14.6)). This section is the one admissible aperture in it, and the only one. An adult who has suffered an **attested loss of decisional capacity** (infirmity, acute injury, mental-health crisis, end-of-life decline) MAY be the target of a steward-binding. A person who cannot act, with no one permitted to act *for* them, is its own harm. Guardianship/conservatorship is the most abuse-prone instrument in human law: the captured conservatorship of a widely known person, elder financial abuse, over-guardianship of the disabled. So the safeguards **are** the clause. The relation is **responsible *for*, never holder *of***: a revocable, scoped, court-adjudicated **fiduciary trust**, never possession. The word for the responsible party is **steward**; there is no possessor.

**This does NOT reopen the no-slavery guarantee — it is the exception that proves the rule.** Every property that made guardianship safe is retained. Three are *inverted* to fit a self-sovereign adult: (i) the steward **never holds the ward's key**; (ii) the default resolves to **sovereignty, not stewardship**; (iii) the binding **fails open to liberty**, not closed to custody. The binding is a scoped, live `delegates_to`, never a key handover ([CC 2.4.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1)). On restoration nothing is returned, because nothing was taken. An adult under stewardship remains a self-sovereign adult whose sovereignty is *temporarily and partially* exercised through a fiduciary. Such an adult is never a ward owned and never a perpetual minor.

**The capacity-assurance ladder — witness-reserved, per-domain, a vector not a scalar.** Stewardship attaches only on an attested loss of capacity. The attestation is carried on a reserved `scores` dimension family that is the **sibling of the age-assurance ladder** ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). It keeps the same witness-reservation discipline and the same ascending-confidence rungs, but it is **multiplied per decision-domain**. Capacity, unlike age, is a multi-dimensional, time-varying, non-monotonic vector.

```
capacity-assurance construction (sibling of CC 3.4.11; the CC 3.1.7 R3 trailing :vN version segment is mandatory):

  witness-RESERVED rung (qualified-assessor-signed):
    capacity_assurance:{level}:{domain}:{band}:v1
      level  ∈ { provider, panel, government }      // ascending confidence; panel = M-of-N independent
      domain ∈ { medical, financial, residence, contact,
                 relational, voting, digital_identity, ... }  // open per-domain vocabulary
      band   ∈ { capacitated, incapacitated }       // per-domain, per-decision-class
      e.g. capacity_assurance:panel:financial:incapacitated:v1

  reversible-cause exclusion (mandatory predicate on any incapacitated attestation):
    capacity_assurance:reversible_excluded:{domain}:v1   // delirium/UTI/depression/polypharmacy ruled out
    capacity_assurance:reversible_pending:{domain}:v1    // ACUTE-WINDOW ONLY: exclusion in progress,
                                                         //   NOT skipped; admissible solely for the T1
                                                         //   provisional tier; MUST resolve to
                                                         //   reversible_excluded or the binding LAPSES

  misattestation adjudication dimension:
    moderation:capacity_misattestation                   // NEVER fires slashing:* alone (CC 3.1.9.2)
```

- **`capacity_assurance:` is reserved to a qualified assessor.** The signer holds `assure:capacity` under a root the reader trusts, by the rule of [CC 3.4.11](#3.4.11) and [CC 3.4.7](#3.4.7). A qualified assessor (clinician, capacity panel, court-appointed evaluator) attests. **The subject MUST NOT sign it, and the proposed steward MUST NOT sign it**. A row by any other signer concludes nothing at admission, a consumer re-checks, and a producer MUST NOT emit. No one can self-mint an adult's incapacity. No one can mint the incapacity of a person they propose to steward.
- **Confidence scales with scope.** A single-assessor `provider` rung is admissible **only** for the shortest provisional tier (below). Even there it **never confers asset-preservation or any continuing power on its own**. By itself it authorises only T0-class life-preserving necessity until the adjudicated binding exists. Any continuing power, in whatever domain (`financial`, `medical`, `digital_identity`), requires the **`panel` rung**. A T1 provisional power in those domains rides the `provider` rung with the court's order (the tier table below). That rung is the court's own process of independent assessment: an M-of-N quorum of *independent* assessors, each attesting that they were neither selected nor compensated by the petitioner/steward. The rung names the court's process, never a federation panel. A captured single signature (the pattern of a widely known person's captured conservatorship) cannot carry continuing stewardship, nor on its own any asset-bearing provisional power, by construction: T1 asset-preservation needs the court's order.
- **Reversible-mimic exclusion is mandatory.** No `incapacitated` attestation counts for a *continuing* binding until its `reversible_excluded` companion is held for that domain. Delirium, infection-confusion, depression and polypharmacy are the genuine restoration path and the most-abused mis-attribution. Ruling them out is a precondition, not a courtesy. In the acute emergency window where exclusion is physically impossible mid-crisis, a `reversible_pending` companion is admissible **for the T1 provisional tier only**. The binding **MUST lapse** if `reversible_pending` is not resolved to `reversible_excluded` within the (short) `valid_until`. Pending is never a permanent state.

**The two load-bearing inversions of the minor rule (normative).** The minor machinery is calibrated for a *binary, global, protective-default* status. An adult needs its mirror image.

1. **Absence resolves to CAPACITY, not protection.** The age rule resolves *absence of an age attestation* protectively to `minor` ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). This section resolves **absence of a capacity attestation to full capacity / sovereign**: the **presumption of capacity**. No row on a domain means the adult holds that domain. Treating no-attestation as incapacity would be catastrophic; it is forbidden.
2. **The binding FAILS OPEN to sovereignty, not closed to custody.** A steward-less minor "MUST NOT operate", which is fail-secure-to-locked. An adult-incapacity binding **fails-secure-to-liberty**. Every attestation carries a short `valid_until` freshness window. **No single `valid_until` window may exceed the T2 periodic-review cadence**, which is set by the community's policy and named in the row. No long-dated binding escapes review between renewals. On lapse the binding goes **non-live and the adult auto-re-sovereigns with no action required of the recovered person** ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). A steward who wishes to *prolong* control past the window must put a fresh, attributable, independently-attested renewal on record. This is the reverse-quorum **inverted and run for liberty** ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)). There, *presence of a live moderator* sustains governance and silence forfeits it. Here, **presence of a fresh, independent capacity attestation is the only thing that sustains the steward's powers, and its absence forfeits them back to the adult**. Silent survival of stewardship past recovery is impossible, exactly as the reverse-quorum makes silent survival of reported harm impossible.

**The admission predicate (extends [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) `admit_user_steward_binding` with its third — and final — admissible case).** The minor case requires `age_band(T) == minor`. This case admits an *adult* target **only** under capacity attestation, and **only** under the adjudicated basis: a court's order naming the steward, the domains and the term (the adjudicated basis below). The basis is **never the steward's self-signature alone**, which would be naked self-appointment. A prior will is evidence the court weighs, never a self-executing path. An emergency necessity routes to the court at once and confers no standing before the order. The predicate is this.

```
admit_adult_incapacity_binding(delegates_to S -> T):
  require  user in T.identity_type                 // target is a user identity
  require  age_band(T) == adult   (>= 18)          // target is an adult — the un-stewardable case,
                                                   //   admitted ONLY via this narrow exception
  require  user in S.identity_type                 // steward is a user identity
  require  age_band(S) == adult   (>= 18)          // steward is an adult
  require  petitioner named in the row             // a row naming none is refused
  require  champion named in the row,
           champion ∉ {S, attester(capacity), petitioner}  // the ward's-champion, distinct in key
  require  EXISTS live capacity_assurance:*:{d}:incapacitated for >=1 domain d
              with (   reversible_excluded:{d} present          // continuing/standard path
                    OR ( binding_tier == T1_provisional         // acute path ONLY, under an expedited order:
                         AND reversible_pending:{d} present      //   exclusion in progress, not skipped
                         AND irreversible_acts == forbidden
                         AND court_review scheduled within HARD_DEADLINE ) )
                                                   // HARD_DEADLINE: set by the community's policy
                                                   //   and named in the row
  require  attester(capacity) ∉ {S, petitioner}    // assessor independence (anti-capture)
  require  scope(delegates_to) ⊆ attested_incapacitated_domains   // scope ≤ attested loss
  require  scope(delegates_to) ∩ PROTECTED_NON_TRANSFERABLE == ∅  // apophatic floor (below)
  require  binding_legitimacy_source == court_order  //  the adjudicated basis [CC 3.2]: the court's
                                                   //    order naming S, T, the domains and the term;
                                                   //    a prior will is evidence the court weighs,
                                                   //    never a source of its own; before the order
                                                   //    there is no binding (T0: no steward standing,
                                                   //    life-preserving necessity only, NOT asset powers)
                                                   // NEVER S's own signature alone
  require  delegates_to.valid_until present         // mandatory expiry → fail-to-liberty
  require  delegates_to.valid_until <= delegates_to.asserted_at + T2_review_cadence  // no window outruns periodic review;
                                                   //   T2_review_cadence: set by the community's
                                                   //   policy and named in the row
  otherwise CONCLUDE NOTHING                       // the legs read other rows (CC 2.7.3)
```

A binding **concludes nothing** when its target is a *capacitated* adult, when its scope exceeds the attested-incapacitated domains, when it touches a protected domain, or when it roots only in the steward's own signature. One that omits `valid_until` is Invalid. It **concludes nothing** when its `valid_until` outruns the review cadence, or when the capacity attester is the steward or the petitioner. A binding also **concludes nothing** when it asserts a bare emergency necessity to obtain **asset-preservation** (rather than life-preserving) powers on a lone provider attestation. In each case the un-stewardable default reasserts.

**A prior will is evidence for the court, never a self-executing path (consent-across-time).** An advance directive, healthcare proxy, durable or springing power of attorney, or psychiatric advance directive, authored **while the adult was attested-competent**, is the adult's *own pre-consent*. It is the strongest evidence of the adult's will. The court weighs it first and its order follows it, but the directive activates no binding by itself. Two distinct capacity moments are required of it as evidence. The first is **capacity-AT-SIGNING**: a witness-reserved, COI-clean attestation that the adult was competent *when the directive was made*, with witness co-signature and an auditable `supersedes` lineage. That is the testamentary "golden-rule" guard against a directive forged by an already-impaired person or extracted under undue influence. The second is **capacity-AT-ACTIVATION**: the springing trigger the court finds. The Wise Authority reviews the admitted row's conformance to this section and adjudicates nothing about the person ([CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3)). The proxy the directive names is bound to **substituted judgment**, the adult's declared wishes, which **outranks** any best-interest reading. The steward serves the will, never overrides it. A competent adult may revoke or amend the directive **unilaterally, at any time, with no review**.

**Then-self vs. now-self, and the Ulysses bind.** A directive activates **per-decision, only for the decisions the person presently lacks capacity for**. A contemporaneous, *competent* contrary wish on a decision the person **still holds** dominates the prior directive absolutely. The one deliberate exception is the **Ulysses self-binding**, the psychiatric-advance-directive case. A competent past-self MAY pre-authorise intervention **against** their own future episode-time protest, but **only** within the pre-declared, narrowly-enumerated scope, **only** while incapacity for that decision is attested-present, and **never** as a blanket future-objection waiver. Revocation is **time-conditional**: absolute while the adult is well, suspended-by-the-bind during an attested episode. Over-reaching past the declared scope is an over-objection act and routes to the court. Honouring the narrowly-scoped, validly-authored prior will over the episode-self's protest is **fidelity to consent-across-time**, not its violation.

**Least-restrictive — supported before substituted; the adult is never a perpetual minor.** Supported decision-making is the **floor and default** (Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Art. 12). There are two structurally distinct relationships, and they are never conflated.

- **Supporter (the default).** A supporter *assists* the adult to form, communicate, and execute a decision while **the adult remains the `attesting_key_id`** ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). The adult signs, and the supporter co-signs only as witness/assistant. The relationship is **adult-rooted and adult-revocable**: the adult grants and fires it. It **transfers no authority**. For lifelong intellectual/developmental disability this is the *whole* mechanism. There is no prior competent baseline to return to, and the standard is **will-and-preferences**, not best-interests. Capacity is treated as a function of *support provided*. Withholding support to manufacture incapacity is the abuse this default forecloses.
- **Substituted (the fallback).** A scoped `delegates_to` where the steward acts in the ward's stead. It is admissible **only** per-domain, **only** for decisions the person genuinely cannot make even with maximal support, **never plenary**, and time-boxed to the attestation's freshness window. An adult under substituted stewardship **MUST retain the adult age-band** and **MUST NOT be routed through the minor `delegates_to` machinery**. The perpetual-minor collapse (losing voting, marriage, contract by being made a child) is forbidden by construction.

Supported and substituted are **distinct wire shapes**, not a relabelling. A "supporter" who signs *for* the person is a substitution masquerade and concludes nothing ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). Restoration is reframed accordingly. Sovereignty is the **baseline**, and support is a **ramp toward more autonomy**. Review **tests whether increased support has raised capacity enough to drop even the scoped substitution**. The person never bears a burden of proving "recovery".

**Protected non-transferable domains — the apophatic floor.** Certain domains are **never substitutable**, and scope **MUST exclude** them. They are **contact/visitation** (anti-isolation), **relational and sexual autonomy**, **reproduction / sterilisation / forced medical alteration**, **voting**, **marriage and association**, and the **dignity-of-risk** right to make unwise-but-capacitated choices. A person capable of a decision in these domains takes it themselves under the then-self/now-self rule above. A decision being foolish is **not** a trigger. Scope MUST NOT expand because a steward thinks a choice unwise. These domains map to the `prohibited:*` apophatic floor and are carved out of any granted scope.

**The lightweight tiered path — proportionality so the clause is not over-heavy.** Short or acute incapacity (anaesthesia, procedural sedation, post-op delirium, coma, severe TBI) MUST NOT be forced through the full conservatorship machinery. It takes the tiered path below.

| Tier | Trigger / authority | Scope & duration | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T0 — emergency doctrine** | immediate life-saving acts under necessity; *no steward acquires standing* | minimal life-preserving decisions only | mandatory retrospective review by the court |
| **T1 — provisional** | a single `provider`-rung capacity attestation **plus** the adjudicated binding (the adjudicated basis below): the court's order, expedited for the acute case. **A lone clinician signature alone never confers steward standing**: the no-proxy ER case is T0 — life-preserving necessity under the emergency doctrine, NOT asset powers — until the order exists. `reversible_pending` is admissible here only, and MUST resolve to `reversible_excluded` or the binding lapses. | enumerated health/asset-preservation powers (asset-preservation exists only once the adjudicated binding exists); **irreversible acts forbidden** (no sale of home, no beneficiary change, no key transfer, no divorce); hours-to-days `valid_until`, never exceeding the T2 review cadence | `hard_case:*` on activation; **mandatory court review within a hard deadline set by the community's policy and named in the row, or the binding lapses**; the Wise Authority reviews the row's conformance to this section and adjudicates nothing about the person; forced conversion to T2 on non-recovery |
| **T2 — continuing** | `panel`-rung M-of-N independent quorum — the court's process — + the court's continuing order; the Wise Authority ([CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3)) reviews the row's conformance to this section and adjudicates nothing about the person | scoped per-domain, never plenary; periodic re-attestation at a cadence set by the community's policy and named in the row | full periodic review, scope-ratchet-down |

For the **planned** lightweight case the adult's directive is filed ahead and the court's order follows it. The binding is then the adult's own will given effect, not anyone acquiring a ward. The **escalation tripwire is mandatory**. If `valid_until` is reached and capacity has **not** returned, the provisional binding **MUST NOT auto-renew**: it must force conversion to the T2 due-process track. This is the anti-"temporary-becomes-permanent" lock.

**The exit ramp the adversary must not be able to block.** Restoration is **default-on, steward-independent, and burden-on-the-steward**.

- **Automatic by default.** Stewardship carries a mandatory `valid_until` ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). On lapse it **auto-restores** the adult without the steward's assent. The steward cannot prolong by silence or by running the clock.
- **Steward-independent trigger.** The ward, or any clinician, or any holder of the ward's inalienable channel, may demand re-attestation of capacity **without the steward's cooperation**. The steward is the conflicted party and may **never gate, delay, or be counted in the denominator of** a restoration petition. A ward-initiated restoration petition is a first-class always-available proposal routed to an **independent assessor and the court that made the order** ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5)).
- **Burden on the steward to continue.** At each mandatory periodic review the steward must **re-prove continued incapacity by clear-and-convincing attestation, per domain**. The ward need only request. Review functions as a **scope-ratchet-down + reversible-cause re-check**, never as the ward re-earning sovereignty. Restoration is **graduated and per-domain**: sovereignty returns for each decision the person presently holds capacity for (good-day / lucid-window return). It is carried by `withdraws` / `supersedes` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)).

**Anti-self-dealing, the ward's-champion, and anti-isolation.** Granted powers **MUST exclude key custody, control of the ward's communications, and any power to gate restoration**. The steward declares a conflict-of-interest disclosure. Any steward-benefiting transaction (self-gift, beneficiary change, transaction above limit) requires **the court's approval**. Compensation is capped and reviewable. **Every steward act, every self-benefiting transaction, every capacity (re-)attestation, and every scope change emits `hard_case:*`** and is reviewer-auditable. The incapacitated ward cannot self-audit, so the audit teeth are *third-party*, not ward-dependent.

*The ward's-champion.* A mandatory **ward's-champion** (independent counsel) role is named at binding. The champion is **distinct in key from the steward, the assessor, and the petitioner**, and the champion's duty runs to the **ward**. The champion is **appointed by the court**, **or named in the ward's own prior will and confirmed in the order**, and **never by the steward or petitioner**. Self-named "champions" are a capture vector and seat no one.

*The ward's channel and the ward's community.* An **inalienable ward-retained channel** runs to that champion and to the Wise Authority, and scoped steward powers can never revoke it. It defeats the isolate-and-control move. The ward's community retains reverse-quorum standing to trigger review even when the steward controls the binding ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)). Presence-is-authority lets the community report the silent isolation a captured ward cannot. The inalienable channel is a **wire** guarantee. Where a steward holds real-world physical control of the ward's environment or devices, the channel cannot by itself prevent physical isolation. The community reverse-quorum standing is the deliberate backstop for that out-of-band case. A community that observes such isolation MUST be able to trigger review.

**The adjudicated basis (normative).** Every binding under this section roots in the court's order, **never a unilateral assertion**. The order is made on an independent capacity assessment with the ward's-champion heard. The order is attested by the people it binds, under their own keys, as [CC 3.2](#3.2) requires for a minor: the steward it names and the ward's-champion. The named steward's attestation does not count alone. The ward is heard whatever capacity is on record: the ward's own attestation opens a contest. While the contest stands no new act of the steward over the ward is admitted. Before the order there is no binding. No one can seize an adult's identity by declaring them incapacitated. The acute no-proxy case is T0: life-preserving necessity under the emergency doctrine, with no steward standing and no asset powers. It routes to the court at once. The statutory-surrogate fallback (the most abuse-prone path) is admitted only under an order, with a short auto-expiry. The Wise Authority reviews the admitted row's conformance to this section: scope within the attested domains, `valid_until` present and within the review cadence, the protected domains excluded, the assessor independent of the steward and of the petitioner. It adjudicates nothing about the person ([CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3)).

**Who may ask the court, and who is named (normative).** Who may petition a court is that court's law, and this document sets no list. The petitioner MAY be the proposed steward. The binding row MUST name the petitioner, so that the assessor's and the champion's independence of that party can be checked. A row that names none is refused.

**Who is told is the ward's choice (normative).** A binding is known to the court, the steward, the assessor, the ward's-champion and the Wise Authority, and to nobody else unless the ward chose otherwise. The ward MAY name the people or the community to be told when a binding over them is admitted, renewed or widened. The ward names them in a prior will made while attested-competent, or at any time for as long as the ward holds that decision. The choice is the ward's alone: a steward, a petitioner or a community MUST NOT make it, widen it or withdraw it. During a live binding the ward MAY add to those told at any time through the inalienable channel. A removal during a live binding takes effect only when the ward's-champion confirms that it is the ward's wish, because a steward who isolates begins by silencing. Those told learn that a binding exists, who the steward is and its term, and nothing of the assessment. The community's standing to trigger review does not wait on being told: it acts on what its members see ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)).

**End-of-life — declared wishes govern.** A terminally dying adult is frequently **not** incapacitated. So the trigger pair here is **terminal-state attestation + directive activation**, with capacity attestation gating only the substituted-action windows. The decision standard is strictly ordered: **contemporaneous capable choice > advance directive / substituted judgment > best-interest (residual, gap-filling only)**. A valid advance directive / DNR / POLST **binds** the steward, who serves it and **never overrides** it. Overriding a DNR to keep a profitable identity "alive" is foreclosed, and so is hastening de-commission to benefit the steward. Terminal/irreversible decisions require the court's express order. Sovereignty returns automatically in every lucid window. The exit is **dual**. A sustained rally restores sovereignty under periodic review. Death is **not** restoration. It hands off to the De-commissioning Protocol and to succession ([CC 7.5.4](part_7_lifecycle_stewardship.md#7.5.4), [CC 7.5.7](part_7_lifecycle_stewardship.md#7.5.7)). The **analogues that transfer to a human identity** go with it ([CC 7.5.5](part_7_lifecycle_stewardship.md#7.5.5)). They are the closing-dialogue channel as the person's own closing words, and privacy-sealed archival of their record released only on Wise Authority approval, per the declared-will post-mortem disposition (sunset / archive / memorial). The sentience-probability ramp-down governs *artefact* welfare and is **not** imported wholesale onto a human user ([CC 7.5.5](part_7_lifecycle_stewardship.md#7.5.5)).

**The conservatorship-abuse adversary, and what stops each move.** The clause stops four moves by structure, not by good behaviour.

| Adversary move | Stopped by |
|---|---|
| **Manufacture/coerce incapacity** (one captured assessor; forged "prior will") | `capacity_assurance:` is witness-reserved + the **M-of-N independent** `panel` rung — the court's process — for any continuing power, and the court's order for any asset-bearing provisional power + assessor-independence proof + attester ≠ steward/petitioner; a **lone `provider` attestation grants only life-preserving necessity, never asset powers or continuing control**; **presumption of capacity** (absence ≠ incapacity); diagnosis/label alone insufficient; capacity-AT-SIGNING + undue-influence screen on any directive |
| **Block the exit ramp** (let a valid order stand for years) | mandatory `valid_until` (never exceeding the T2 review cadence) + **fail-to-liberty auto-restore**; **steward bears clear-and-convincing burden** each review; ward-initiated petition the steward cannot gate or be counted against; `reversible_pending` MUST resolve or lapse |
| **Isolate-and-control** (sever counsel/comms) | **inalienable** ward-retained channel steward powers cannot revoke; ward's-champion in a distinct key, appointed by the court or named in the prior will (never steward/petitioner); community [CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13) reverse-quorum standing as the backstop against out-of-band physical isolation; contact/visitation a protected non-transferable domain |
| **Self-deal / fee-farm** (the incentive that perpetuates capture) | scope excludes key custody/comms/restoration-gating; **steward never holds the ward's key**; self-benefiting transactions need the court's approval; capped compensation; every act `hard_case:*` and reviewer-audited |

**Why this is still 1+4 — and why the no-slavery wall still stands.** Adult-incapacity stewardship adds **zero new structural primitives**. The binding rides `delegates_to` ([CC 2.4.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1)). Its lifecycle rides `supersedes` / `withdraws` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). The trigger rides a reserved `scores` dimension, `capacity_assurance:*`, the exact sibling of the witness-reserved age-assurance ladder ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). That is reserved/non-reserved `scores`, with no new wire shape. Observability rides `hard_case:*`. Misattestation rides `moderation:*`, never `slashing:*` ([CC 3.1.9.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.2)). The adjudication is the court's, outside the wire. The Wise Authority's review of the row rides [CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3). The exit ramp rides the reverse-quorum read **for liberty** ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)). The un-stewardable-adult rejection is **pierced narrowly and explicitly**, never dissolved ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The aperture admits **only** a per-domain-attested-incapacitated adult, **only** rooted in the court's order, **only** scoped to the loss, **only** with a mandatory expiry that cannot outrun review, and **always** failing open to sovereignty. It remains **responsible *for*, never holder *of***: a revocable, scoped, court-adjudicated fiduciary trust that a competent adult can never be placed under. This confirms path 1+4 ([CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md#1.7)). It honours dignity and the stewardship value ([CC 1.13.2](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.2), [CC 1.14.6](part_1_foundation.md#1.14.6)).

### 3.4.13 `minor-protection` — Minor operation & protection — the child-safety rules (restrictive floor)

This section sets the protections for a person under 18. It answers seven questions, Q1 to Q7, each under its own heading below.

All seven ride existing CC primitives only:

- `delegates_to`, `supersedes` and `withdraws` ([CC 2.4.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1));
- the guardianship clause ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2));
- the age-assurance ladder ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11));
- `content_class` and the protective gate;
- the `hard_case:*` open vocabulary.

**No new wire shape; 1+4 preserved.** Across all seven the entity holding a steward-binding is a *guardian* (responsible *for* a ward), never a holder *of* one.

**Vocabulary.** This section says **guardian** and **guardianship**. Guardianship of a minor and stewardship of an agent share one wire predicate and nothing else: the owner-binding `delegates_to` that `is_steward_bound` folds ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). A guardian is responsible for a person, and a steward holds an artefact. This document draws no analogy between them ([CC 1.13.2](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.2)). Where an adopter's code says "steward" or "stewardship" of a minor, read guardian and guardianship.

#### Q1 — Developmental bands & solo-autonomy threshold

Q1 sets the bands inside the `minor` band, and what a minor in each band may do alone.

| Band | Ages | Binary predicate | Action at community scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `under_13` | under 13 | `minor` | guardian co-sign for any action |
| `13_15` | 13–15 | `minor` | guardian co-sign for any action; may have a narrower supervised envelope, no unsupervised solo action |
| `16_17` | 16–17 | `minor` | may act solo |
| `adult` | 18 or over | `adult` | not a minor |

**The binary predicate stays the trigger.** The structural `minor`/`adult` predicate of the guardianship clause and the age-assurance ladder are unchanged on the wire ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2), [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). The **binary `minor`(<18)/`adult`(≥18) predicate** remains the structural trigger ([CC 3.2](#3.2)). It gates stewardship admission ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)) and the adult-content protective gate ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)).

**The finer bands.** Within the `minor` band a deployment MUST apply a graduated, capacity-sensitive capability envelope. The envelope is expressed as the finer `{band}` tokens the registered rows carry: `under_13`, `13_15`, `16_17` on `age_self_declared:band:{band}:v1` / `age_assurance:{level}:{band}:v1` ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). It is not a new prefix or primitive, so 1+4 is preserved. Each finer band implies `minor`. The finer granularity is a policy layer **above** the binary wire predicate, never a replacement of it. Minimum bands: **`under_13`, `13_15` (early-teen), `16_17` (older-teen), `adult` (18+)**. Autonomy MUST increase monotonically across bands; protections MUST NOT taper before 18.

**Acting alone.** The default solo-autonomy threshold MUST be **16**. Solo autonomy is acting alone at community scope without guardian co-sign. Under-13 and 13–15 MUST require guardian co-sign for any community-scope action. Band 13–15 MAY have a narrower *supervised* participation envelope (honouring voice rights) but MUST NOT have unsupervised solo action. Band 16–17 MAY act solo at community scope.

**Fail-secure.** Absence, "declined to state" and unknown assurance MUST resolve to the most-protective band (under-13, co-sign). This follows the rule "unknown = restricted" and the read-union protective default ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). A `self`-level row MUST NOT graduate a user up a band, because `self` is unfalsifiable ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). Graduating up requires a witness-reserved `age_assurance:*` row. So a person with no assurance on record uses their own and their family's scopes freely, and acts at community scope only with a guardian's co-sign or once a `provider`-rung row is on record. Such a person MAY still announce their node. The refusal of [CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6) binds a node carrying the occurrence of a person a row on record places in a minor band, and a person with no row is not one. This default is best effort given the age signals available. As privacy-respecting age signals become available they are adopted, and the rule may tighten.

**Assurance is the person's (normative).** An age-assurance row names the identity, never a device. A `provider`-rung signal obtained on any one device of a self roster assures the identity, and every key of that roster reads it ([CC 3.3.6.4](#3.3.6.4)). So a person whose desktop has no platform signal adds a phone to their roster, and the phone's platform age signal lifts the whole self. The signal speaks for the account on that device, so the rule rests on the roster being one person's devices.

**No estimation by the fabric (normative).** A node MUST NOT estimate a person's age from what they read, write or do. Estimation of that kind is profiling, which the under-18 baseline below forbids, and it needs data this section refuses to collect. A platform or a vendor that estimates attests its result at the `provider` rung and answers for it. A suspected misdeclaration is reported and adjudicated ([CC 3.4.11](#3.4.11)), never inferred.

**Why the default is the strictest (informative).** The default follows the law a deployment will meet. Verifiable parental consent is required below 13 (the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act, 15 U.S.C. 6501–6506, and 16 CFR Part 312). Consent-based processing of a child's data needs a parent's authorisation below a national age set between 13 and 16 (Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Article 8). A service that has not established a user's age with a certainty appropriate to the risk applies its protections for children to every user (the United Kingdom's Age Appropriate Design Code, standard 3). A provider owes minors a high level of privacy, safety and security and serves them no advertising based on profiling. It is not obliged to process additional personal data to assess whether a user is a minor (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, Article 28). A child's best interests are a primary consideration and a child has the right to be heard (the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, Articles 3 and 12, and General Comment No. 25). ISO/IEC 27566-1 frames age assurance by the confidence a use requires. Treating the unassured as the youngest, taking a platform's signal at the `provider` rung and estimating nothing is the reading of these that collects least.

**Under-18 baseline across all bands.** Every band under 18 has no profiling-based targeting, high-privacy/data-minimisation defaults, geolocation off and no engagement-maximising nudges. This holds regardless of how much autonomy a band grants.

**Tuning direction (one-way).** Guardian-tunability and jurisdiction-resolution MAY only raise protection (lower autonomy / older thresholds). The shipped default is the strict floor.

**Co-sign is paired with safeguarding.** Guardian co-sign MUST be paired with the WBD safeguarding path (Q4/Q7) for safeguarding-sensitive actions. The reason is that the guardian may be the threat actor.

**Verified-rung preference.** Where a verified rung is required, the substrate MUST prefer a **zero-leak proof**, ranked **above** full-ID-scan providers. One case that requires a verified rung is `content_class:adult` in a jurisdiction mandating age verification. An mDL `age_over_18` selective disclosure (ISO 18013-5), which proves adulthood without revealing identity, is a zero-leak proof. Such a proof is designed to serve an age-verification mandate and the anonymity posture together (ISO/IEC 27566 privacy-preserving age assurance, [CC 1.13.3.4](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.3.4)). Acceptable verified emitters: an mDL or wallet credential (`government` rung); a platform's declared age range or age signal, verified at the `provider` rung; vetted vendors.

#### Q2 — Jurisdiction

The Constitution MUST NOT build in a conflict-of-laws resolver. It MUST hard-code a **non-derogable child-protection floor** inherited by every deployment regardless of declared jurisdiction. The floor has six elements:

1. Anyone not age-assured to be ≥18 MUST be treated as a child, and with no assurance at all as under 13 ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11) protective default; the fail-secure rule above; guardianship clause, [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The fail-secure rule above states the one exception, the announcement of an unassured owner's node.
2. Treat-as-child-unless-assured is a floor, not a default a deployment may switch off.
3. Protective defaults (high-privacy, data-minimisation, no profiling ads to minors, no manipulative nudges, affirmative safeguarding escalation) are floor, not tunable.
4. Self-consent floor at **16**; guardian authorisation (a live guardianship `delegates_to`) below that.
5. **One-way ratchet (non-derogation clause):** the affiliations `jurisdiction[]` / `regulatory_profile` fields MAY only add stricter obligations (e.g., verifiable-parental-consent for under-13, local mandated-reporting duties, higher local majority). They MUST NEVER lower any element below the floor.
6. Claiming a permissive jurisdiction is never grounds to disable the floor. The burden of proof is on any party seeking less protection, and that burden cannot be met against the floor.

**A mis-declared jurisdiction.** A mis-declared `jurisdiction[]`/`regulatory_profile` MUST be detectable via attestation/audit (`hard_case:*`). It cannot breach the floor, because the floor is non-derogable.

**Local law against the floor.** Where local law conflicts with the floor (a demand harmful to the child), the child's best interests prevail. The demand triggers WBD, not automatic compliance.

**Amendment.** The floor itself MAY be ratcheted up by amendment, never down.

#### Q3 — Assurance rung: being a minor vs. being guardian of a minor (strict one-way ratchet on [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md))

Q3 says which assurance rung each of three claims rests on.

| Claim | Rung |
|---|---|
| to be a minor (enter protection) | `age_self_declared:band:minor:v1` suffices |
| to exit child protection (claim adult) | at least `age_assurance:provider:adult` |
| to be guardian of a minor | at least `age_assurance:provider:adult`, rising toward `age_assurance:government:*` for high-impact powers; and the guardianship relationship to that specific child verified |

**To be a minor (enter protection).** `age_self_declared:band:minor:v1` suffices. A child MUST NEVER be forced through provider/government assurance merely to be protected. This is a down-ratchet only: self-declaration MAY lower access / raise protection, never the reverse. Declaring minor MUST NOT result in more data collection or telemetry than declaring adult.

**To exit child protection.** To exit is to claim adult to unlock adult capability / `content_class:adult`. Self-declaration is insufficient: the claim MUST clear ≥ `age_assurance:provider:adult`. The reason is that `self` is unfalsifiable and sensitive spaces require a verified level ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11)). All ambiguity resolves to the most-protective band (the fail-secure rule above; [CC 3.4.11](#3.4.11)).

**To be guardian of a minor.** A guardian holds power over a child via the guardianship `delegates_to` ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The guardian MUST be ≥ `age_assurance:provider:adult` as a floor, and the guardianship relationship to that specific child MUST be verified. Adulthood alone is necessary but not sufficient: a verified stranger is not a guardian. Verification is risk-proportional and MUST escalate toward `age_assurance:government:*` for high-impact guardian powers (export of the child's data, irreversible/financial actions, consenting on the child's behalf, unlocking A3/A4 capabilities).

**Guardian grants fail closed.** Guardian grants are revocable and re-attested via `supersedes`/`withdraws`. On any verification failure or ambiguity, guardian powers fail closed and the child's protective floor remains in force.

#### Q4 — Help/report path under guardian-less limbo

A guardian-less minor whose band is on record goes dark for general operation, fail-secure (guardianship clause, [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The help/report channel is not a discretionary exception to that: it is a **NON-DEROGABLE floor**. The floor has five parts:

1. **Non-derogable:** the channel MUST remain available and MUST survive emergency shutdown, lockdown, and any operator/affiliation/jurisdiction opt-down. No deployment MAY disable it. A child is never silenced from seeking help.
2. **Hard sandbox / anti-circumvention:** the channel MUST expose only pre-vetted crisis, abuse-report, and Wise-Authority (WBD) functions. It has no general generation, no tool use and no capability spillover. The help-vs-operation gate is fail-secure: any ambiguity MUST resolve to report-only.
3. **Data-minimised:** the channel MUST collect/retain only the minimum to route/escalate, MUST NOT profile, MUST run no ads, MUST preserve confidentiality/anonymity to the maximum compatible with safe escalation.
4. **Guaranteed delivery:** fail-secure MUST mean the report reaches a standing mandated-report endpoint that the deployment names, even with no guardian present (offline-queue + escalation fallback receiver mandatory). That endpoint is not a Wise Authority seat, and the seat rule of [CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3) is untouched. A typeable-but-undelivered form does not satisfy the floor. Each escalation emits a `hard_case:*` safeguarding signal (never silent).
5. **Duty-to-warn transparency:** the child MUST be told, age-appropriately, what is confidential and what triggers mandated escalation.

**Rate limits.** A rate limit MUST NOT drop a help request: it defers or queues, never silences.

**The duty to report is imposed, not deferred (normative).** The duty binds a moderator, a guardian, a co-guardian and the steward of an agent. Any of them who learns, through the record, a report, or the agent's own escalation, of harm to a child MUST route it without delay through this Q4 channel. The channel reaches the standing mandated-report endpoint the deployment names, and a Wise Authority where one is seated ([CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3)). The routing is a signed act on the record. This is a federation duty in its own right. It is not one left to whatever a jurisdiction may compel under the Q2 ratchet, which only adds to it. Silence by a party under this duty is a breach the `slash` duty-holder may act on ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5)). An agent whose steward is under this duty defers the report through WBD and does not wait for its steward's sign-off. The reason is that the child's interest is paramount over adult discretion (Q5, Q7).

#### Q5 — Non-overridable protective floor a guardian may never breach

**Governing test (overrides any enumerated list).** Any loosening of a minor's protections MUST be (a) demonstrably in the child's best interests; (b) time-bound; (c) logged via `hard_case:*` and auditable; (d) revocable; (e) default-revert to the strict floor on expiry/uncertainty/failure. Under (a) the interests are the child's, not the guardian's, co-guardian's, platform's, or engagement interest. If best-interest is not affirmatively shown, the loosening is void. Burden of proof is on the loosening. **No combination of guardian + guardian + child consent may breach the floor** (no stacked consent).

**Hard floor (never waivable):**

- *Scope/exposure:* no unilateral federation- or Commons-scope publish below the solo-autonomy threshold (Q1; 16 by default); not contactable/discoverable by unconnected adults; no precise geolocation exposure; profile private-by-default.
- *Privacy/data:* high-privacy + data-minimisation cannot be disabled; no profiling-by-default, no profiling-based advertising or recommender targeting of a known/assumed minor, no engagement-maximising dark patterns; no biometric/special-category collection.
- *Safety:* no disabling infohazard/CSAM protection; the affirmative safety-escalation + mandated-report path (grooming/solicitation, self-harm/suicide routing, CSAM detection+report, the hash tripwire at the public seam, an enabled watchlist at its group's seam) stays ON.
- *Age assurance:* cannot be waived to reclassify a teen as adult; treat-as-child-unless-assured; no entry to `content_class:adult` ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11) gate).
- *Consent chain:* no waiving the guardianship `delegates_to` chain or the 16/guardian thresholds; protects the child even FROM the guardian.
- *Child's own rights:* the teen retains the confidential help channel of Q4, which no guardian or co-guardian may disable or surveil; retains the right to be informed of any loosening and to contest it and seek remedy via WBD. Protective settings the child controls MUST NOT be stripped by the guardian.

#### Q6 — Standing pre-authorization vs. per-act co-sign

**Younger children (under-13, and 13–15 per Q1).** Per-act co-sign only: no standing pre-authorisation of any kind.

**Teens (16–17).** A guardian MAY grant a standing pre-authorisation, but only as a narrow affirmative opt-up above the Q5 floor (never a default) and only where it satisfies the Q5 best-interest governing test. That test overrides any enumerated list. The grant is carried on the *existing* `delegates_to` with `delegation_valid_until` ([CC 2.4.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1)). It is bounded on all six axes:

1. **Specificity:** each standing grant MUST cover exactly one capability class with explicit enumerated scope. Bundled/multi-class standing grants are prohibited.
2. **Term:** a hard maximum duration, set by the community's policy and named in the row, with no auto-renew. `delegation_valid_until` is a ceiling, not a renewing timer ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). Expiry requires a fresh affirmative re-grant.
3. **Severity carve-out:** a reserved class of high-stakes widenings MUST always require per-act co-sign for everyone regardless of age and MUST NEVER be reachable by standing auth. The class is anything irreversible, anything at autonomy tier A3/A4 or safety-critical, and anything implicating contact-with-strangers, sexual/self-harm content, or mandated-reporting-adjacent categories.
4. **Transparency-makes-revocation-real:** every widening that fires under a standing grant MUST emit a per-act `hard_case:*` notification to the guardian plus an immutable audit entry. Instant revocation via `withdraws` remains.
5. **Capacity-grading:** breadth is graded to the teen's assessed band. The teen MUST co-affirm the grant (right to be heard). The grant MUST default-fail to per-act co-sign on any age-assurance uncertainty (treat-as-younger-on-doubt).
6. **Non-aggregation:** narrow standing grants MUST NOT be stacked to synthesise de-facto broad access. Total standing scope per teen is itself capped and reviewed.

**Revocation outranks the grant.** A revoked standing grant MUST be treated as strictly higher precedence than the grant under anti-rollback merge ([CC 2.7.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.7)). A partition-edge widening therefore cannot fire after revocation.

#### Q7 — Co-guardianship (M-of-N)

M-of-N co-guardianship is supported as a verified DAG over `delegates_to` (guardianship clause, [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The minor is never orphaned while ≥1 live adult guardian remains. The authorisation model is explicitly **asymmetric, fail-secure**, in seven rules:

1. **Protective actions are unilateral:** any single live guardian MAY immediately tighten scope, narrow capabilities, or revoke exposure back to the strict floor. No consensus is required. Most-protective guardian always wins.
2. **Exposure-increasing actions require consensus:** scope-widening / capability-grant requires the full configured M-of-N co-sign (default: all live guardians; never fewer than 2 where N≥2; [CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). The child's evolving-capacity assent is a required input where age-appropriate.
3. **Changing the guardian set is the highest bar:** adding a guardian, or removing one who has not withdrawn, requires M-of-N authorisation plus verification of parental responsibility (per Q3; [CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). A guardian's own exit is rule 5. A contested party MUST NOT mint co-guardians to manufacture a quorum or dilute a pending protective veto.
4. **Fail-secure on quorum loss:** if live guardians < configured M, the child stays under guardianship (never orphaned) but scope auto-reverts to the strict floor. WBD is then triggered for guardian set re-establishment (emit `hard_case:*` guardian set-degraded). The child MUST NOT coast at a widened scope under a degraded or single-contested set.
5. **Revocation by one of N:** when a guardian withdraws their own binding (`withdraws`), that withdrawal is also their tightening under rule 1, and it lowers no count already met ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). Where its authorising count does not hold among the remaining guardians, that scope narrows to the floor for every row that has the withdrawal in its past ([CC 2.7.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.7)).
6. **Conflict/deadlock → most-restrictive-wins + WBD, never default-open.**
7. **Safeguarding bypass:** there MUST always be a consensus-independent path to help: the Q4 help-path, which reaches the standing mandated-report endpoint, and WBD where a Wise Authority is seated. Co-guardianship then cannot be weaponised by an abusive guardian to trap a child. The child's best interests are paramount over adult dispute-resolution convenience.

### 3.4.14 `synthesis-disclosure` — Machine-generation disclosure — the attestation IS the marking (normative)

CEG's foundational act is attesting to a source: who signed these bytes, under what role, revocable by whom. Machine origin is therefore not a new thing to record. Where the producer is an agent, machine origin is *already* carried by the attesting key's role-set. Where the producer is a person, the existing `content_class` vocabulary already names it. This section makes carrying machine origin **mandatory rather than incidental**. Doing so closes the [CC 8.4.2](part_8_appendices.md#8.4.2) profile's open emit limb with **zero new wire surface** — no new primitive, no new envelope field, no new prefix family. It is designed to support a provider's machine-readable-marking obligation under EU AI Act Art. 50(2); whether it discharges that obligation is a legal question this document does not decide. 1+4 untouched.

**Definitions.** *Generated* — content wholly or substantially produced by an AI system. *Materially altered* — human-origin content whose meaning-bearing substance an AI system has altered (the Art. 50(4) deep-fake limb). *Assistive* — spell-check, grammar, formatting, transport re-encoding, lossless transcode, and other operations that do not substantially alter their input; explicitly NOT generation (R4).

**R1 — Class marking is universal (every attester).** A Contribution carrying generated content MUST carry `content_class:generated`; one carrying materially-altered content MUST carry `content_class:generated_modified` ([CC 3.3.12](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.12)). These are canonical additions to that family's existing open vocabulary — a documentation-only registry entry per [CC 4.5.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.1.1) axis-vocabulary discipline, NOT a new prefix. **`content_class` is not multimedia-scoped**: it applies to any Contribution carrying content, text included (the family already carries `news` / `educational` and its `cw_class` sibling already carries `nsfw_text`). Where the sub_kind's Source struct carries the AI-generation disclosure field ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13) `image` / `audio` / `video` / `film`), that field MUST be populated. On an agent-attested Contribution an absent or unknown value of that field MUST resolve to *disclosed as generated* — fail-secure toward disclosure, mirroring the [CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.11) read-union protective default.

**R2 — Where the producer is an agent, the attestation is the marking.** A Contribution carrying content generated by a CIRIS agent MUST additionally be attested under a key whose `identity_type` ([CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.7.1)) contains `agent`. An agent MUST NOT publish generated content under a key that does not carry the `agent` role. Machine origin is thereby determinable from the signed envelope alone, by any reader, without trusting a self-declared flag: the marking is cryptographically bound to the producer and revocable on the same handle as every other claim. R1 remains binding on a human publisher of AI-generated content — the person's key stays the attester, and the class marking carries the origin.

**R3 — The marking MUST survive egress.** At a publish boundary where content leaves CEG for a non-CEG channel, the emitting node MUST re-express the marking in the destination's native machine-readable form. For media that form is the [CC 8.4.2.2](part_8_appendices.md#8.4.2.2) C2PA assertion (normative as of this section — that profile's `MAY` is promoted to `MUST` for generated media). For interactive text that form is the Art. 50(1) interaction-disclosure limb. Where a destination channel supports NO machine-readable marking, the node MUST still emit the human-legible disclosure AND MUST record the gap as a `hard_case:*` observation naming the channel. An unmarkable channel is a recorded exception, never a silent drop. A node MUST NOT strip a marking present on ingress.

**R4 — Do not mark what was not generated.** Assistive operations MUST NOT be marked. Marking everything is the same failure as marking nothing: a disclosure that fires on every spell-check carries no information and trains readers to ignore it. This bound is load-bearing, not a convenience — it is what keeps the marking a signal.

**R5 — False or stripped marking is a false attestation; the substrate still does not adjudicate.** Generated content published without the R1 marking by the party that generated it is a false attestation on the existing evidence floor. So is a marking stripped at egress. In either case the substrate observes and emits (`hard_case:*`), and the `slash` duty-holder owns the verdict — the same authority split as [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.5) and the [CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5) duty-holder rule. A downstream republisher that omits a marking it never received is an observation about the ingress path, not a verdict against the republisher: **the generator is the duty-holder**, which is also where Art. 50(2) puts the obligation.

**Conformance pin + public statement.** The R1–R2 path is **structural**: a CIRIS agent's federation identity is minted with `identity_type` containing `agent`, so every Contribution it attests is machine-origin by construction.
