In a private room the room key signs a row of one entry. The entries are blinded so that a room sees its own entry and no other. No fold or admission of the row reads an entry, and the leaf's door reads the one presented to it ([CC 2.6.1.10](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.10)).

**The door of a leaf (normative).** The LeafNode's credential carries the vouching row and that room's disclosure. The row is presented only inside the MLS group of the room it discloses. It is placed at that room's scope and reaches that room's audience. A row that vouches for several rooms is placed at `self`, and each room sees only its presentation. A presentation discloses exactly one entry, and a row presented with none or with more than one is refused at that room's door, `leaf_vouch_presentation_invalid`. Every Add, Update and Commit path checks the vouch under the member's device key. It refuses a leaf whose vouch is absent, ended, for another room, for another leaf key, or under a key that is not the member's. The five refusals are named in that order: `leaf_vouch_absent`, `leaf_vouch_ended`, `leaf_vouch_other_room`, `leaf_vouch_other_leaf` and `leaf_vouch_not_by_member`. The vouch names the room and not the epoch. It covers that room's MLS groups, the chat group and its call groups, with the same vouched leaf key. A door recomputes from a group's id that the group is of the room the vouch names ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). A renewal's vouch names a fresh leaf key, installed by the same Update: the old leaf key signs the Update, and the new LeafNode carries the new key. A lapsed leaf's signature is accepted on exactly an Update that replaces it. Its application messages are refused, not held. Members MAY remove a leaf that stays lapsed. The group's exporter keys scope two things and only two.

| What the exporter keys scope | The keys |
|---|---|
| **addressing** | the record secret and the destination secret of [CC 5.4.1](#5.4.1) and [CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6) |
| **live call media** | the stream DEK seed exported under `ciris-stream-dek/v1`, then the HKDF over the label ‖ `stream_id` ‖ `u64_be(epoch)` above |

**Content at rest** is chat bodies, files, and kept or recorded streams. It is sealed under content DEKs carried by a flat per-recipient `key_grant` cascade on three axes ([CC 3.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.2)).

| Axis | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `key_grant:epoch:v1` | the community epoch DEK, rotated by an epoch bump on removal |
| `key_grant:stream:v1` | one DEK per stream and epoch, for chunk DAGs and kept audio and video |
| `key_grant:content:v1` | self and family whole blobs |

The MLS group never keys a chat body. Which mechanism applies is fixed by the content's class and is not a deployment setting. The tree's advantage is one-to-many commit aggregation among live members. The flat cascade is one grant per recipient over whatever delivery the transport offers. Neither displaces the other. The split is **wire-invisible**: tree position rides the opaque `key_grant` payload, and there is no schema migration.

**Forward secrecy** is forward-only by default, by rotation on departure ([CC 4.5.12.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.12.1)). **Post-Compromise Security (PCS)** is **not provided by default**. A deployment MAY enable it by requiring periodic TreeKEM key-updates (member self-updates). A compromised current member then heals on the next commit. A deployment that does not enable it stays forward-only.

**Catch-up bound**: `min(operator depth cap, chunk-eviction horizon)`. The depth cap is an operator setting, not a substrate constant. Operators MUST ship the depth cap **with** the cascade. Without it the per-rekey Contribution count is unbounded: 10⁶ for a million-recipient roster. Three distinct windows are NOT conflated: the chunk-eviction horizon, grant durability, and the holding claim's 72 h liveness ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)). A catch-up request against an evicted epoch returns **`ContentMiss` — fail-honest, no silent gap** (the fail-honest invariant).

## 5.2 `family` — Structural invisibility — no holding claim leaves a bounded cohort

Every row has an **audience**: the nodes it may reach ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). A row is served to a node in its audience and to no other, and a node holds a row only when it is in that audience. This is one rule at every tier, and only the roster changes size: `self` and `family` are not a special case but the audience rule applied to the smallest rosters.

| `cohort_scope` of the row | Its audience | What a node outside the audience learns |
|---|---|---|
| `self` | the owner's own nodes | nothing, not even that the content exists |
| `family` | the nodes of the family's current members | nothing, not even that the content exists |
| `community`, `affiliations` | the claimed nodes of the roster's members | nothing of the content, of the roster or of who holds it |
| `community`, in a public room ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)) | the claimed nodes of the roster's members | the listing, the holding claims and, by asking a member's node, the content and the roster |
| `species`, `biosphere`, `federation` (the Commons) | every node | everything: the holding claims here are the holder directory ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)) |

**What a row carries (normative).** A row carries its audience to the rows it names, when it is concluded, sits in the same room as the row it names, and its signer is already in that row's audience. So a joiner holds the rows its own admission names, and a reply carries the row it answers to a later joiner. A row leaves its room only by its own signer's act: a row that names it from elsewhere carries it only when the same key signed both. No member carries another member's signed row out of a room ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). Since a row waits for what it names ([CC 2.7.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.3)), what a reply carries to a reader follows from the reply and the rows that reader is already served.

Within every cohort, holding claims, custody reports, target replication and anti-entropy run exactly as at every other tier ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)). Carrying a sealed frame for someone else is not being in its audience; who may carry is the rule of [CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6).

**Which of a member's nodes.** A node is in a cohort's audience only through its owner's membership, and the owner chooses per node which of their cohorts it serves ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)). A node with no owner is in no cohort's audience.

**A row about a party reaches that party.** A row that names a node, or a grant issued for it, is always served to that node ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)). A row placed at `family`, `community` or `affiliations` may name only keys within its audience, and one that names a key outside it concludes nothing, with the reason `subject_outside_audience` ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1)). So at those scopes the person a row is about is always in its audience. What a duty-holder's record shows the person it names is the rule of [CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.5). The one row about a person that does not reach them is the author's own `self` note, the last boundary case below.

**No holding claim leaves a bounded cohort (normative).** When a Contribution carries `cohort_scope: self` or `cohort_scope: family`, the substrate MUST NOT emit any holding claim observable outside the cohort ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). The `custody:ack:v1` report is placed at the content's scope and replicated to members only ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)). The bytes are delivered to admitted members of the self-collective ([CC 3.3.6](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6) `identity_occurrence`) or the family ([CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.4)) through the at-rest encryption flow, never through the public holder-discovery directory. The holding claims of `community` and `affiliations` content reach the roster's members only, in the same way. The Commons' holding claims are at federation scope and are the holder directory.

**What an outsider cannot do.** The privacy property is structural, not policy:

- A non-member peer cannot issue `ContentFetch` for the bytes because no holding claim it can observe names a holder ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)).
- A non-member peer cannot discover that the bytes exist through the substrate: the only attestations that refer to them are scoped to the cohort and never federate beyond it ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)).
- This is **structural invisibility**: the privacy comes from what the wire format can carry, so no operator of a node outside the audience can switch it off. It is no operator's policy and no legal undertaking. A node inside the audience holds the rows it is served, a hosted member's node included ([CC 1.13.3.3](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.3.3)).

> **Scope (normative):** structural invisibility buys **content-holding confidentiality only** — it is NOT relationship-existence, metadata, traffic-analysis, or unobservability privacy. The bounding non-goals are stated canonically at [CC 1.13.3.1](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.3.1); do not represent CEG as providing the stronger properties.

**What moves to a peer (normative).** Being in a row's audience means the row may be served to a node, not that it is sent. A row moves to a peer when it is requested or required, and appropriate ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). It never moves because it is federation-tier: that tier means a row can be shared and may be public, not that it is copied to everyone.

| A row is | when |
|---|---|
| requested | the peer itself pulls for a subject or a dimension ([CC 5.3.2.9](#5.3.2.9)); an automatic diff is not a request |
| required | the peer must hold it to seal, address and take part: the consent-free set of [CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6) and the rows of the cohorts it belongs to |
| appropriate | its audience names the peer: it is addressed to the peer, is about it, or is placed in a cohort it is in, the family's replication tier and audience deciding ([CC 3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1), the family model) |

A `consent:replication` grant ([CC 3.3.7](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.7)) names the class it moves and moves that class and nothing else; it does not make a peer a mirror of the grantor's corpus. Anti-entropy over the commons is what serve seats do among themselves. A seat offers a person's node only what is required or appropriate for it, and the rest waits on a pull ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). A node with no owner is offered no more than that. It holds what it must to seal to and address the peers it dials, and what it was asked to hold, which is what a peer referred to it asks of it ([CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6)). It is never a copy of the mesh. What is required moves before any walk, so a fresh grant or a contact's own row never waits behind history. What is offered unasked is the live state, and a superseded row moves on request.

**Substrate enforcement**:

```
On admission of a Contribution C with cohort_scope ∈ {self, family}:
    # (1) STRUCTURAL INVISIBILITY — UNCONDITIONAL:
    substrate MUST NOT emit a holding claim for C's evidence_refs bytes outside the cohort
    substrate MUST NOT propagate C beyond the self-collective / family scope
        via any other directory or discovery surface
    # (2) AT-REST ENCRYPTION — the CC 4.4.3.16 cascade, always on (CC 4.4.3.15):
    recipients := if cohort_scope == self:   all current identity_occurrences of C.attesting_key_id whose node's allow list names the cohort (CC 6.1.5.3)
                  if cohort_scope == family: all current occurrences of the members of family per C.family_id whose node's allow list names the cohort (CC 6.1.5.3)
    FOR each recipient r:
        kem := resolve_encryption_keys(r.key_id)    # current occurrence's encryption_pubkeys (CC 3.3.6.1)
        IF kem is None OR kem.ml_kem_768 invalid:
            # FAIL-SECURE: no valid v2 wrap target ⇒ EXCLUDE r from the grant.
            # MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or to wrap_algorithm v1.
            # NOT SILENT: emit hard_case:recipient_excluded:{scope_key_id}
            #   (CC 3.4.4, which defines the closed reason-set) INTO the self/family
            #   scope — recipient r, reason, + the skipped Contribution's envelope
            #   ref. Scoped to the cohort; never federates beyond it (CC 5.2
            #   invisibility preserved).
            skip r   # content stays encrypted + unreachable to r until r registers encryption_pubkeys
        ELSE:
            substrate MUST wrap C's DEK via key_grant (CC 4.4.3.16, wrap_algorithm v2)
                to kem.{x25519, ml_kem_768}
```

**Two layers, not one.** (1) **Structural invisibility** — holding claims that never leave the cohort + non-propagation beyond scope — is the **unconditional** guarantee: no discovery attestation federates. (2) **At-rest encryption** — the CC 4.4.3.16 DEK cascade — is **defense-in-depth** (against local-disk forensics, the host operator, or the cloud-substrate operator). It is always on: a body written at a self, family, community or affiliations tier is sealed by the substrate, and no operator switch turns that off. It uses `wrap_algorithm: v2` (hybrid PQC, CC 4.4.3.16), never v1. At those tiers the only plaintext bodies are those of authorized infrastructure communities and public rooms, which [CC 4.4.3.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.4) places at federation scope, holding claims included.

**Composition with the at-rest encryption flow**: the store wraps the DEK (`wrap_algorithm: v2`) to every current recipient occurrence ([CC 4.4.3.16](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.16), [CC 2.7.8](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.8)): the owner's occurrences at `self`, and every occurrence of each member at `family`. An occurrence whose own key a live allow list names, and whose list does not name the cohort, receives no wrap ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.3)). New occurrence / new family-member admission triggers retroactive `key_grant` emission for all extant `cohort_scope: self|family` content (the "I bought a new phone and want my history" / "I added Carol to the household" flows from CC 3.3.4 worked example).

**Recipient encryption-key resolution + fail-secure exclusion.** The wrap target is **not** a recipient's signing key. `wrap_algorithm: v2` needs the recipient's `{x25519, ml_kem_768}` **content-KEM** keys, which the recipient self-certifies via its `identity_occurrence.encryption_pubkeys` ([CC 3.3.6.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6.1)); the substrate resolves them by `resolve_encryption_keys(key_id)` = the recipient's current (non-superseded, within-`valid_until`) occurrence → its `encryption_pubkeys`. Because this layer **mandates v2**, a recipient whose current occurrence carries **no valid ML-KEM-768 key MUST be fail-secure *excluded*** from the grant, and the content remains encrypted and unreachable to it. The substrate MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or to `wrap_algorithm: v1`. To be an at-rest-encryption recipient, an identity MUST have an occurrence carrying `encryption_pubkeys` that the sealer holds. This is the non-maleficence / fail-secure default: a missing key denies access, never downgrades the protection.

**Exclusion MUST NOT be silent.** A bare `skip` makes a fail-secure exclusion indistinguishable from "the family went quiet" — a soft-censorship vector for a buggy or malicious substrate, and a contradiction of the spec's own `hard_case:*` attestability grain. On every fail-secure skip the substrate MUST emit **`hard_case:recipient_excluded:{scope_key_id}`** ([CC 3.4.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.4), which defines the closed `reason` set) **into the affected self/family scope itself**, carrying the excluded recipient's `key_id`, a `reason`, and the skipped Contribution's envelope ref. This is so that the excluded member (who still sees cohort-scoped attestations) has something to audit and remediate. The event is cohort-scoped: it MUST NOT federate beyond the self/family (the CC 5.2 invisibility promise is preserved; the *fact* of the family's content is not leaked by its exclusion events).

**A write its own author cannot open is refused (normative).** A sealer MUST NOT seal a write where its author has no wrap target among the write's recipients: no current occurrence of the author, and no node the author owns, is wrapped to ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The rule covers every write sealed at rest under a cohort's content key, a chunk and a stream's segments among them. It does not cover a message sealed to one named recipient, such as a contact request, an invitation or a key grant. The sealer refuses the write and stores nothing, `write_author_has_no_wrap_target`. The check is the sealer's own, made over the roster and occurrences it holds when it seals. It is no verdict about the row, and no other node repeats it. Where the author has a wrap target and another recipient has none, the write is sealed and that recipient is excluded as stated here.

**Locality dividend**: `cohort_scope: self|family` content is the bulk of daily activity (family photos, personal notes, in-household device chatter), and that bulk never federates. Operators do not configure this; the wire format enforces it.

**Boundary cases**:

- A `cohort_scope: self` Contribution that is later promoted via `supersedes` to `cohort_scope: community` emits its holding claims at the new scope, on the NEW Contribution, at promotion time. The original `cohort_scope: self` Contribution's bytes remain structurally-invisible at federation; only the promoted scope's bytes propagate.
- `cohort_scope: self` content with `subject_key_ids` containing a non-self party (e.g., a private note Alice writes ABOUT Bob) is admitted and stays in Alice's self-collective. Bob does NOT receive a key_grant unless Bob is also in Alice's self (not the case for two distinct identities). Bob's [CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3) subject-side revocation authority over the note still composes, but the bytes never reach Bob without Alice's explicit re-emit at a higher cohort_scope including Bob.

## 5.3 `endpoint` — Endpoint shapes

This section specifies the endpoint shapes below for the discovery and transparency surfaces. Wire-format consumers read these.

### 5.3.1 `witness` — Transparency Services and Receipts

Transparency keeps a producer from showing one history to one party and a different one to another. It follows SCITT ([RFC-9943], [RFC-9942]). A Transparency Service keeps its own append-only log, registers Signed Statements in it and issues a Receipt for each. No service signs over another party's root, and no directory of witnesses exists.

**What a service does (normative).** A service is offered a Signed Statement, a `COSE_Sign1` of this form ([CC 2.6.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1)). It registers the statement's deterministic encoding, with an empty unprotected header, as one leaf of its own log ([CC 2.7.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.11)). It answers with a Receipt: a `COSE_Sign1` under the service's own key that carries an inclusion proof of that leaf ([RFC-9942]). The Receipt states the service's identity, the subject of the registered statement and the service's own instant of issue. It rides in the statement's unprotected header, label 394, and no signature of the statement covers it ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). A service keeps one log under one identity.

**What a Receipt says.** A Receipt says that the named service registered the statement, and when. It confers no standing and adds no authority. A Receipt that does not verify is ignored, and it is never a fault of the statement. Anyone MAY run a service under their own key ([CC 2.7.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.11)). The audit log a node keeps of its own rows is no Transparency Service: it issues no Receipt and takes none.

**The services of a lineage (normative).** A lineage's charter MAY name `transparency_services` ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6). The services a charter names in `transparency_services` register the lineage's heads. The member is a set of at least two identity references, each to a composite key. `receipt_quorum` is exactly ⌊n/2⌋ + 1 of the n services named. `receipt_cadence_secs` is how often a named service issues a Receipt again for an unchanged head. The three members are present together or not at all ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). A charter that carries none of them names no services. Its head is then current when the holders have counted it and it descends from a head the reader holds out of band, the pinned bundle ([CC 5.3.4](#5.3.4)).

**Naming a service binds nobody.** A charter that names a service confers no standing on it and places no duty on anyone ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). The service's part is its own signed act, the Receipt, and no ceremony of acceptance exists ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). A named service that issues no Receipt does not count, and nothing else follows.

**Independent.** A service is **independent** of a lineage when it is none of that lineage's holders or seats and none of them owns it. Only an independent service counts for a lineage, so a lineage's own services never count for itself.

**A head and its registration (normative).** A lineage's head is the bundle in force ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). `lineage_key_id` is the bundle's `family_key_id`, and a head's position is the bundle's `version`. A holder's statement over the bundle is the Signed Statement a service registers. A service's first registration for a lineage is the lineage's first bundle, or a head that descends from it. Each later one is a head that descends by `prev` from the head the service last registered. On the way each bundle counts on its predecessor's holders. A service registers one head for each lineage and position. It MUST refuse a second head at a position it has registered, and it keeps both heads as evidence. So a fork gets no Receipt from a service that registered the other head.

**Receipted and fresh (normative).** A head is **receipted** when Receipts for it from `receipt_quorum` distinct independent services are held. The services are those the charter of the head's predecessor names, and for a first bundle its own charter. They are never those of the head's own charter, which a fork head chooses. A head is **fresh** at an attaching edge when its newest counted Receipt was issued within `attach_window_secs` before that edge's own signed instant ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T4a). No node's clock enters that reading. Each named service MUST issue a Receipt again for an unchanged head at least once per `receipt_cadence_secs`. So a stable lineage stays attachable with no act of its holders.

*Fork attempt.* A head that the lineage's holders counted and that does not descend from the lineage's receipted head is a **fork attempt**. A node that holds one MUST record it once per `(lineage_key_id, fork point)` and raises `hard_case:lineage_fork_attempt` ([CC 3.4.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.2)). The fork point is the nearest ancestor on the receipted chain. The node counts and does not store further attempts off the same point. So a holder of those keys can file one fork off a point and show a different fork off it to a reader at its first view. A node that recorded the first holds a count of the second and not its head, and only the reader that was shown it holds it. A fork attempt never freezes anything.

*Equivocation.* Two heads of one lineage at one position that each hold a receipt quorum are **equivocation**, `hard_case:lineage_equivocation`, and freeze head adoption under T6. Because the quorum is a strict majority of the services named, at least one service registered both, and its two Receipts name it.

*Silence.* A lineage whose newest counted Receipt is older than its charter's `receipt_cadence_secs` is *silent*. It is reported on the trust surface as a liveness signal under [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T4, never a validity leg. Its effect is on *attaching* (T4a), where a silent lineage becomes unattachable once `attach_window_secs` lapses and attachable again on the next Receipt. `attach_window_secs` is the charter's attach window ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T4a), distinct from `receipt_cadence_secs`, which is the services' cadence and the liveness signal.

**Where a head is served.** `GET /v1/trust-root/lineage-head` serves a lineage's heads with the Receipts held for each ([CC 5.3.4](#5.3.4)). No route of this section takes a cosignature. The tree-head cosignature of the earlier form, over `ciris.sth_cosign.v1`, and the route `POST /v1/transparency/sth/cosign` that carried it are [CC 8.11.26](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.26).

#### 5.3.1.1 `consistency-proof` — Receipts and their proofs (normative)

A Receipt means something only where the log behind it is append-only. A service's log is the SHA-256 tree of [RFC-9162], whose hashing is that of [RFC-6962]. Every root a service issues a Receipt under MUST be consistent with every root it issued one under before. The consistency check is the service's own, over its own log. A service checks no other party's tree, and no party signs over a service's root.

A lineage's head needs no consistency proof: it descends by `prev`, and a service checks that descent before it registers ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)). A stream's log is its producer's. A stream's head after the first is offered to a service with a consistency proof from the head that service last registered for the stream. The proof is submission material beside the statement ([RFC-9942], label 396), never a payload member ([CC 5.3.3.8](#5.3.3.8)).

### 5.3.2 `transport` — Transport substrate for byte-level content

Wire-format Attestations carry claims; they don't carry bytes. When a claim's `evidence_refs[]` cites a SHA-256-addressed blob (e.g., an installer binary, a config file, an adapter package per `agent_files:*` per [CC 3.1.7 / CC 3.1.10](part_3_the_namespace.md)), the bytes travel via Edge transport substrate: `MessageType::ContentFetch` + `ContentBody` + `ContentMiss`. Holder-discovery via the `custody:ack:v1` `here` rows at the content's scope ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)); node-mode peers serve the bytes. Attestation envelope shape unchanged; SHA-256 in `evidence_refs[]` becomes universally resolvable to bytes through the substrate.

**The durable trace (normative).** The substrate's duties for an agent's reasoning trace follow the anchor rule of [CC 1.13.6](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.6): a trace is durable only when it is anchored on the record of an act. Every execution path that produces an external effect — every utterance, every tool call, every adapter-mediated emission — MUST close with a terminal result row (the closing action record of the agent's pinned trace schema, [CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.5)). The trace that row anchors is carried as `trace:complete:v1` ([CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.5)) or its post-scrub `trace_summary:{kind}`. An in-flight trace that reaches no terminal row is working state, not a record. The substrate MUST purge such a trace after a declared, bounded age (the orphan sweep) and MUST export a count of the traces it purges. The count is exported so an auditor can see how much is discarded while the contents stay, by design, unavailable. A substrate MUST NOT be read as having lost evidence when an unacted deliberation ages out. The orphan sweep can never erase evidence of a consequential act, and if it ever did the defect lies in the action-emission path, never in the purge. Until the totality of the terminal row over effect-producing paths is tested, the invariant MUST be represented as a named wager wherever the control is claimed, and the register carries its status. An operator needing interrupted-path forensics MUST enable a bounded, privacy-scoped incomplete-receipt plane as an explicit opt-in; it is not the default, and this document does not claim one exists on every surface.

#### 5.3.2.1 `holder` — Holder directory TTL + ContentMiss feedback

A `custody:ack:v1` `here` report is live for **72 hours** from its instant ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)); after that the holder reads *unknown*. Consumer policy MUST attempt at most 2 holders in parallel and accept the first successful full-SHA verification. On `ContentMiss` (holder does not hold the blob) the consumer MUST NOT withdraw the holder's report: only its signer retracts a holding claim ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3) rule 4). The consumer records the miss and downweights the holder in its own holder resolution. The holder's own next acknowledgement reports `none`.

**The cap binds the whole-object fetch (normative).** "At most 2 holders in parallel" bounds the fetch in which each holder returns the whole object and parallel attempts duplicate the download. A chunked object ([CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1)) is fetched chunk by chunk, each chunk verified by its own seal and committed root, and the same rule applies at chunk granularity: no chunk is requested from more than 2 holders in parallel. How many distinct chunks a consumer keeps in flight with one holder is the implementer's, and the `ContentMiss` downweight above applies per holder on either path.

#### 5.3.2.2 `consent-revocations` — Consent revocations are NOT local-tier-eligible

A user's withdrawal of consent is the one signal federation peers rely on to stop propagating that user's data, so it MUST NOT rest unsigned and invisible to them. It MAY be in transit, unsigned, for at most the window below. The rule is **local-tier signature deferral** — self-attestations skip the composite signature path ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)) locally and only sign at federation-tier promotion. This is sound for **producer-only-authority self-attestations**. **The discriminator is *whose act the row is*, NOT whether `subject_key_ids` is empty**: a row is local-tier-eligible iff it is the producer's own act under its own authority. Such a row MAY name a subject in `subject_key_ids` per [CC 2.3.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3.1) and remains local-tier-eligible, because the row is the producer's own act. Examples are `observed:user:{hash}:*`, `epistemic:about:{key}:*`, an agent's own `consent:partnership_accept`, or the [CC 2.3.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.3.4) self-`identity:current` with `subject_key_ids=[self]`. Every listed subject keeps its withdrawal authority over the row under [CC 2.4.1.1 rule 2 or 3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1). A listed subject's later `withdraws` or `consent:state:revoked` is that subject's **own signed Contribution**, never a durable local row. The single carve-out is below: a **subject's own revocation** over a Contribution that names it.

**Consent revocations from subjects MUST NOT use the local-tier deferral path.** The rule covers a Contribution that carries non-empty `subject_key_ids`. Any subsequent `consent:state:revoked` emission OR `withdraws` admitted under [CC 2.4.1.1 rule 2 or 3](part_2_the_grammar.md) from a subject in that set MUST promote to federation-tier within **the window (24 hours by default, operator-tunable)**.

**Rationale**: subject-side revocation is the wire-format observability primitive that federation peers depend on to honor consent. If a user revokes consent in the local-tier scope of one agent's substrate, and that revocation is unsigned + unpromoted for an extended window, other federation peers continue propagating the user's data — exactly the failure mode this closes.

**Substrate emission**: substrate MUST emit `hard_case:consent_revocation_promotion_overdue` when a subject-side revocation has been local-tier for longer than the window without federation-tier promotion. LensCore composes `detection:consent:promotion_delay_pattern` on top (operator monitoring; not a slashing trigger on its own).

**Composition with the self-attestation pattern**: the CEG-native agent's `consent:partnership_accept` self-attestation (the producer-side half) MAY ride local-tier; the user's `consent:state:revoked` against the agent's stance Contribution (subject-side) MUST NOT. This preserves the cardinality win of deferral while closing the leak window.

**The consent tail: transit, not rest.** The "no local subject-revocations" rule and the consent-SLA promotion gate above are the **same invariant viewed from the two gates**, not a contradiction. A subject-side consent revocation — a subject-emitted `consent:state:revoked`, or a `withdraws` admitted under [CC 2.4.1.1 rule 2/3](part_2_the_grammar.md) from a subject named in the target's `subject_key_ids` — is **federation-tier by classification**. It MAY *transit* the local-tier write path while in flight (the producing occurrence's substrate accepts the unsigned envelope before promotion), but it MUST NOT *rest* there: a subject revocation is **never a durable local row**. Its only conformant terminal state is *promoted* (federation-tier, hybrid-signed per CC 5.3.2.7); *overdue-flagged* is a recorded breach of the window, not a resting state, and *settled local* is never reached. The substrate MUST drive it to federation-tier promotion within the window; the local tier is a momentary staging buffer for it, not a resting place.

**The overdue emission records the breach.** When the window lapses without federation promotion, the substrate MUST emit `hard_case:consent_revocation_promotion_overdue` (as required above). This emission is not merely observability — it is the signal the consent-promotion path keys off: the consent-promotion gate and the CC 5.3.2.7 `local ⟹ caller is the producing occurrence` read-gate read the **same** overdue state. Because both gates key off one shared signal, a subject revocation can never be simultaneously (a) invisible to federation peers under the local read-gate and (b) un-flagged by the consent-promotion gate. Keeping the two gates reading one state is exactly what closes the de-synced-gates case (CC 5.3.2.7).

**What the record shows when the substrate is at fault.** The overdue event is emitted by the substrate that holds the revocation. A substrate that drops a revocation it accepted unsigned emits nothing. The subject then holds no signed row, and the record shows no breach.

#### 5.3.2.3 `merge` — Cross-region merge intents — CEG-declared per subject_kind (normative)

With operational data joining the CEG-native replication stream ([CC 3.3.9](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.9)), the substrate runs **more than one merge policy**. The policy is a **normative property of the subject_kind, declared here** — the substrate reads and dispatches on the declaration; it MUST NOT infer policy per record type (the substrate enforces declared merges; it does not invent policy).

| subject_kind(s) | Merge intent | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `organization`, `org_membership` | **`lww_skew_bounded` + `withdrawal_forward_only`** | Stable-id grouping ([CC 3.3.9](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.9)); an admitted `withdraws` (deactivation) is forward-only — a later non-withdrawn write does NOT resurrect; else, among one attester's own writes, latest `asserted_at` wins; tie-break smallest `attestation_id` ([CC 3.5.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.5.1)). The forward-only here is the **lightweight authz flag**, NOT the [CC 4.4.3.15](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.15) DEK-cascade crypto path — Commons tier, no DEK exists. |
| the licence (`licensure:{authority_id}`, [CC 2.4.1.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.3)), written under the affiliation record's M-of-N quorum ([CC 4.4.3.12](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.12), [CC 3.3.9](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.9)) | **`monotonic_quorum`** (the revocation merge below, on `license_id`) | A write with a lower `revision` than one held never wins the merge. Then the `MergeBallot` comparator: the greater `quorum_weight` stands, a weight being a count. At equal weight the more restrictive state stands: `revoked` > `suspended` > `active`. Two writes equal on both give one state, so no further step is needed. No signed timestamp and no content hash ranks two writers. |
| `revocation` + the three membership-revocations | **`monotonic_quorum`** (the original instance) | No revocation is refused for another, and none is withdrawn. A revocation has one state, so no comparator picks among the revocations of one subject: every admitted one stands. For `key:revocation:v1` the effective bound is the minimum `revoked_after` over all of them ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)). `key:revocation:v1` merges on its subject `sub`, the revoked composite key's thumbprint ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)): the per-subject anti-rollback keys on the digest. The three membership revocations merge on the member `key_id`, since roster rows are addressed by `key_id`. |
| keys / attestations / occurrences / families / communities / location_proofs | Content-addressed idempotent admission | Same content → same `envelope_hash` → dedup; two rotations of one key are both kept, and a reader reads them as [CC 2.7.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.7) rule 2 states. |

**Skew-bounded admission (normative).** For every subject_kind merging by `lww_skew_bounded`, the substrate MUST reject at admission any envelope with `asserted_at > now + tolerance`, where `tolerance` is the [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.7) clock-skew bound (±5 minutes; the existing `CLOCK_SKEW_VIOLATION` error class). Without this, a signer with a forward-skewed clock future-dates `asserted_at` and wins LWW indefinitely; with it, a forward-dated write can win for at most the skew window. This matters precisely because `org_membership` carries `role: OrgAdmin` — unbounded LWW on authz data is a role-escalation surface.

**The two quorums (restated from [CC 3.3.9](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.9) — different layers, different stewards):** the **steward-signature admission quorum** is NOT the **region merge quorum**. The first is an M-of-N set of statements over one payload ([CC 2.6.1.9](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.9)): the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) founder-quorum machinery at admit, Verify's layer. The second is `quorum_weight`, the `MergeBallot` tier-1 ordering above: the substrate's layer. The substrate's merge logic never counts steward signatures; Verify's admission check never orders merges.

#### 5.3.2.4 `attestation-tier` — The attestation tier model — local-tier write, query, promotion (normative)

Pins the **shared attestation surface** every implementation of the row store and the relay writes, queries and promotes through, so it is analyzable + modelable as one contract. The substrate exposes the *methods*; CEG pins the *wire/conformance semantics* every implementation MUST agree on. **No change to the 1+4 surface** ([CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md#1.7)) — a "tier" is recorded state on an attestation, not a new primitive. The tier split serves the same fail-secure cost discipline as streaming: cheap, unsigned writes stay private and local until the costly hybrid signature is paid exactly once, at the moment authority actually crosses to the federation.

#### 5.3.2.5 `authority-local` — Local-tier eligibility — the discriminator is *whose act the row is*, not subject-set emptiness

A write is local-tier-eligible iff **it is the producer's own act under its own authority** ([CC 5.3.2.2](#5.3.2.2)). The discriminator (*whose act the row is*, NOT empty `subject_key_ids`), the producer's-own-act-with-named-subject examples, and the single carve-out are defined canonically at [CC 5.3.2.2](#5.3.2.2). The carve-out is a listed subject's own `withdraws` under [CC 2.4.1.1 rule 2/3](part_2_the_grammar.md) or subject-emitted `consent:state:revoked`. That row is the subject's own signed Contribution and MUST go signed / promote within the CC 5.3.2.2 window, never a durable local row. Tier-specific addition: `witness_relation` MUST be `self` for any local-tier write.

#### 5.3.2.6 `local` — Promotion — `local → federation` (the deferred-signature moment)

Promotion computes the hybrid signature and flips the row federation-visible. It is **idempotent** (promoting a `federation` row returns it unchanged). At the promotion instant the tiered-scope promotion ([CC 4.4.3.14](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.14)) and the holding claim at the new scope ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)) fire exactly as for any federation write — **promotion *is* the federation-emit moment** ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)).

**Signed bytes — the deterministic payload of [CC 2.6.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.2):**
- The signature MUST cover the payload the producer committed, in the deterministic encoding — the **identical** bytes any natively-federation row signs. A promoted row is therefore **byte-indistinguishable on the wire from one born federation-tier**; there is no "was-promoted" marker in the signed bytes.
- **Substrate columns are NOT in the signed bytes.** `tier`, `promoted_at`, and any other storage bookkeeping are substrate state, never part of the payload. Only the [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1) envelope member set is encoded.
- **The CC 2.6.1.2 omit rule is load-bearing here.** Promotion MUST encode the **exact member set the producer committed at local-write time**. A field *omitted* at local write MUST NOT be materialized at promote, and vice-versa, or the encoded bytes diverge from what the producer committed and the signature fails. The substrate serializes the stored row → the committed payload → the deterministic encoding → sign; it MUST NOT re-default.
- Registry owns the exact envelope member set ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1) + the logical names of [CC 2.6.1.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.4)); the verifier verifies the bytes it received. Do NOT use the verifier's internal length-prefixed `signing_bytes` framing — that is for verify-to-verify primitives that never cross the four-impl boundary as a row; a promoted attestation is the opposite.

#### 5.3.2.7 `two` — The two tiers

| Tier | Signature | Federation-visible | Read-visibility | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `local` | MAY be absent (deferred per CC 5.3.2.2) | **No** | **only the producing occurrence** (self-read); every other caller — even an authorized family/community peer — sees nothing | local-tier write |
| `federation` | composite signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)) **present** | Yes | per [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1) `cohort_scope` + the CC 5.2 invisibility rule | direct signed write OR `local → federation` promotion |

**Invariant (substrate MUST enforce):** `tier = federation ⟹ hybrid signature present`. Nothing crosses to federation-visible unsigned. A `local` row is **labelled** local and MUST NOT be served as federation-authoritative (fail-honest). The read-gate is **orthogonal** to `cohort_scope`: it is an additional filter (`local ⟹ caller is the producing occurrence`), composing with the audience rule of [CC 5.2](#5.2) and [CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5). The three failures this closes: a local row leaked to a non-self caller, an unsigned local row served as authoritative, the two gates de-synced.

#### 5.3.2.8 `admission-pqc` — The PQC half is MANDATORY at admission — no classical-only, no hybrid-pending accommodation (normative)

The CC 5.3.2.7 invariant `tier = federation ⟹ hybrid signature present` is **enforced at the admission gate**, and "present" means **verified**. Every federation-tier admission gate MUST check **both** halves. The two halves are those of the composite signature of [CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7), which never verifies on one half. An earlier-form row's halves are those of the bound hybrid of [CC 8.11.12](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.12). Every federation-tier admission gate MUST **reject** a federation-tier Contribution that carries only the classical half. This invariant binds **all operational-authority admission gates**. Those gates explicitly include `operational_admit` (key_grant / partner / org-membership / license writes), the [CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6.2) `transport_destination` binding, and the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) founder-quorum gates, under which the affiliation record's licences are written ([CC 4.4.3.12](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.12)).

**This is an immediate requirement.** There is no opportunistic-acceptance window and no fleet-floor or calendar trigger. The rationale is exactly the threat hybrid exists to defend: an adversary holding a future Ed25519 break could forge a grant / binding / licence and have it admitted if the classical half alone sufficed. There is **no `require_hybrid: false` posture** — a verifier's hybrid-required check is always-on, never an operator toggle. The only conformant state for a federation-tier key is "carries a valid ML-DSA-65 half". A key that has not completed PQC wiring is **not conformant for federation-tier emission** and is confined to local-tier (self-read, [CC 5.3.2.5](#5.3.2.5)) until it does. The mandate is at the **federation admission boundary only** — the single place authority crosses; local-tier rows MAY still defer the signature per [CC 5.3.2.2](#5.3.2.2).

**The mandate binds the durable store + replication path, not only the authority gates.** "Federation-tier" means **every** federation-tier attestation, including the bulk **per-trace / store-and-replicate** path — not merely the operational-authority gates enumerated above. A federation-tier trace written to the durable, content-addressed, replicated corpus MUST carry (and a verifier MUST check on ingest) the ML-DSA-65 half exactly as a `key_grant` does. There is **no "operational authority vs testimony leaf" exemption** (federation root and the trace leaf are bound by the same rule). **Content-addressing is NOT a defense against forge-later:** a CRQC-era adversary who breaks Ed25519 mints a backdated trace under a historical key and hashes **their own** forgery. The content hash matches by construction, so the address proves nothing about authenticity. Because the trace store is *kept for posterity* (it outlives the classical primitive), the per-trace signature is the single most forge-exposed surface in the federation — the crux of a store kept at scale. The PQC half is therefore mandatory there for the same forge-now / harvest-now-exploit-later reason as the at-rest DEK cascade ([CC 5.1](#5.1) / [CC 4.4.3.16](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.16)). A substrate persisting/replicating a federation-tier row whose envelope signature lacks a valid ML-DSA-65 half MUST reject it at the ingest gate ([CC 2.7.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.3)) — store-then-quarantine is non-conformant.

#### 5.3.2.9 `persist-query` — Query — open-prefix dimensions, bounded operators (normative)

The uniform read filters on `(dimensions[], valid_at, confidence_floor, subject_key_id?, scope)`.
- **`dimensions[]` is an OPEN-vocabulary set of prefix strings, matched by hierarchical prefix — NOT a closed enum.** Per [CC 4.5.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.1.1) axis-vocabulary discipline, dimension prefixes are open vocab (new families — `consent:*`, `detection:community:*`, `settlement:*` — ship continuously). A closed enum would force a substrate redeploy per CEG namespace addition and break forward-compat. A query for `detection:*` matches `detection:correlated_action:bribery` etc.; an exact string matches exactly.
- **The bounded surface is the *operator set*, not the *vocabulary*.** The apophatic discipline (a fixed, named surface — not an OLAP/graph engine) is preserved by the **closed set of five predicates** above + no caller-composed SQL/projections — NOT by closing the dimension vocabulary. *Open data, closed operators.*
- `valid_at` filters `asserted_at ≤ valid_at < COALESCE(expires_at, ∞)`; `confidence_floor` filters `confidence ≥ floor`; `scope` applies BOTH the audience rule of [CC 5.2](#5.2) AND the CC 5.3.2.7 tier gate ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). Write-side reserved-prefix emitter gates ([CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.7.1)) are unaffected — read is gated by scope, not by dimension authority.

#### 5.3.2.10 `holistic` — For holistic analysis + modeling (informative)

The tier model is the *same KEM-then-symmetric placement* the streaming model uses ([CC 5.3.3](#5.3.3)), applied to attestations. The **expensive op (hybrid sign) is on the cold path** (promotion, at federation-emit), while the **hot path (local self-attestation write) is O(1) and unsigned**. Cost shape for a node:
- **local write**: O(1), no asymmetric crypto — the agent's steady-state memory/config/consent/identity churn.
- **promotion**: one composite sign ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7); the CC 5.3.3-model per-op cost) + the deterministic encoding — only at the federation-emit moment, never per local write.
- **query**: the [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1) scope-filtered read; cost is the predicate + index, independent of tier.
- **observability for modeling**: `local` row count, promotion rate, and `hard_case:consent_revocation_promotion_overdue` count are the three measurable signals; the CC 5.3.2.2 window is the one tunable. A model of a federation's attestation load is therefore *(local-write rate, promotion rate, query rate)* with promotion carrying the only asymmetric-crypto cost — the dual of the streaming model's epoch-rekey tail.

#### 5.3.2.11 `full-sha` — Full-SHA verification before consumption (normative)

A CEG-Conforming Consumer (CCC) MUST verify the full SHA-256 of received bytes against the value in `evidence_refs[]` BEFORE handing the bytes to any consumer (Agent loader, Portal renderer, etc.). A holding claim names the blob by its address digest ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)); the consumer MUST verify the full SHA of the received bytes regardless of how it found the holder. Bytes that fail the full-SHA check MUST be discarded and the holder MUST be reported per consumer policy (a negative score on the holder; never a `withdraws` of another device's holding claim).

**Every blob cited through a descriptor carries its size, and size is checked first (normative).** A descriptor that cites a blob from `evidence_refs[]` — installer, config, adapter package, media, any bytes — carries the blob's byte length alongside its digest. A producer always knows it at creation time. **Where the size lives:** an `evidence_refs[]` entry is a content hash ([CC 2.6.1.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.4)) and carries no size. The size rides the **descriptor** whose canonical shape this document already defines. The descriptors are the multimedia Source struct's `{digest, size}` ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13)), the live-stream chunk-descriptor list (same section), and the per-artifact entries of `SkillImportManifest` and the build manifest. The `build` descriptor of a build-manifest Contribution is one too, and carries `manifest_size` beside `manifest_hash` ([CC 3.1.2.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2.1)). This rule binds every blob cited **through** such a descriptor. A blob cited only by a bare `evidence_refs[]` string has no declared size, and a consumer fetching it enforces the cap of [CC 2.6.1.6](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.6) instead. The consumer MUST NOT invent a size field on the envelope, which would be a wire change. A producer that needs the size check on such bytes cites them through a descriptor. The consumer MUST compare the received length to the declared size **before** computing the digest: a mismatch is a refusal without reading the rest, and the descriptor alone lets a receiver enforce caps and refuse a `ContentFetch` that would overrun. Size is not a substitute for the digest, only the cheaper check that runs first. The one descriptor with no total size is a **live stream in progress** ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13) `live_stream`): each chunk and the init segment carry their own, and the recording, once the stream ends, is an ordinary blob with one.

#### 5.3.2.12 `render-tier` — The render tier is receiver policy, computed from verified, sniffed bytes (normative)

A CCC MUST decide whether and how to render a blob from the **verified bytes and its own policy, never from a claim in the descriptor**. After [CC 5.3.2.11](#5.3.2.11) verification the consumer MUST sniff the leading bytes and require the sniffed essence to **equal** the declared `format` ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13)); a mismatch is a **refusal, not a correction**. Where the description is sealed (`sealed_descriptor`, [CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13)), the sniff runs where the bytes decrypt, by the party that opened them, against the `format` inside the seal. A holder that cannot open the bytes does not sniff and does not claim to. The declared `format` / `codec` are inputs to that comparison and to capability checks, never authorisations. This is what makes the set below a property of the *receiver* that a malicious sender cannot widen.

**Recommended renderable set (recommended CCC policy — not normative).** The intersection of what the widely deployed messengers *emit*, what the common mobile and browser platforms all decode, and what has a memory-safe decoder. A CCC MAY adopt a narrower set; a wider one is its own risk to own, and this Part does not endorse it.

| `format` (sniffed) | Tier | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| `image/jpeg`, `image/png` (APNG as PNG), `image/gif` | **A — render** | ≤ 16 MB, ≤ 33 Mpx; GIF ≤ 921,600 px + frame cap; reject bytes after `IEND` / `FFD9` |
| `image/webp` | **A — conditional** | ≤ 10 MB; node runs a WebP sanitizer; re-encoded on ingest |
| `text/plain` | **A** | valid UTF-8, ≤ 1 MB, bidi controls rendered visibly |
| `video/mp4` | **A — conditional** | `codec` present and `avc1.*` (≤ L4.1) + `mp4a.40.2` only; ≤ 100 MB, ≤ 8,294,400 px; node runs a hardened MP4 sanitiser (for example `mp4san`); receiver rejects unlisted tracks |
| `audio/mp4` (`mp4a.40.2`), `audio/mpeg` | **A** | ID3v2 ignored — never decode `APIC` |
| AVIF, HEIC / HEIF, JXL, WebM, MOV, MKV, Ogg / Opus, FLAC, WAV, ADTS, Markdown | **B — sender converts to a Tier-A form before hashing; raw arrival = C** | not decoded natively by the common mobile and browser platforms; no memory-safe decoder is assumed |
| `image/svg+xml` | **C for the bytes — never a client renderer or WebView.** A node MAY emit a PNG rendition (`derived_from`) from a hardened rasteriser (for example `resvg`: no file-href resolver, no system fonts, caps) in an isolated process; that PNG is Tier A | scriptable, with external references and font resolution; no client renderer is admitted. The [CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.13) rendition rule dissolves the B-or-C question: the SVG is C, the node's PNG is A |
| `application/pdf` | **C — download**; node MAY rasterise pages to attested PNG in an isolated process | JS / Launch actions / embedded fonts; viewer escapes recur |
| `model_3d` (glTF, USDZ, FBX, splats) | **C — download**; node MAY rasterise a PNG poster in an isolated process | scene-format parsers fail on memory safety recurrently, and a glTF text field can carry script into a 3D viewer |
| HTML, Office, fonts, archives, TIFF, PSD, BMP, ICO, everything else | **C — refuse** | generic card, external handoff, dangerous-extension block on save |

**Where enforcement lives.** The ingest pipeline that makes Tier A enforceable belongs on the **node**, so every client renders only bytes the node's safe encoder produced. The pipeline is size ([CC 5.3.2.11](#5.3.2.11): checked first) → full-SHA → sniff (only on verified bytes, [CC 5.3.2.12](#5.3.2.12)) → memory-safe demux / decode → canonical re-encode → strip metadata → emit rendition + descriptor. Decoders for every Tier-A format MUST be memory-safe. Images, SVG and audio decode entirely in memory-safe code; video is "memory-safe code validates container and elementary stream, hardware decodes".

### 5.3.3 `transport-streaming` — Streaming transport, per-stream logs & delivery receipts

This is the **delivery axis** — the third orthogonal envelope concern alongside visibility (`cohort_scope`) and revocability. [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4)'s 1+4 primitive set is untouched; this is an endpoint + envelope + composition extension, NOT a grammar change.

**Bifurcation**:

| Half | Cardinality |
|---|---|
| **Observer-share / directed delivery** (single Contribution → subscriber-set; no `stream_id`; rides [CC 3.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.2) `key_grant` + [CC 4.4.3.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.3) Policy M membership) | N=1 typical; per-subscriber `key_grant` |
| **Media / streaming multicast** (`live_stream` chunk-DAG; per-`(stream_id, epoch)` keys; specified by CC 5.3.3.1 / CC 5.1 / CC 5.3.3.11) | N>1; live media keyed from the group exporter, kept epochs carried by flat per-recipient `key_grant:stream:v1` wraps ([CC 5.1](#5.1)) |

#### 5.3.3.1 `stream` — Chunk seal + STREAM nonce (normative)

Per-chunk content sealing **uses SFrame's per-frame AEAD construction** ([RFC 9605](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9605), normative) with the binding and nonce pinned here. The construction is the per-frame AEAD model with a `(KID, CTR)` header, here bound as `KID = stream_id` and `CTR = counter`, AEAD = AES-256-GCM, keys derived per MLS epoch (the canonical SFrame+MLS composition, CC 5.1). The STREAM nonce below is CEG's binding profile of SFrame's per-sender nonce derivation. Per-chunk content sealing uses AES-256-GCM (NIST FIPS 197 + SP 800-38D). The 12-byte (96-bit) nonce follows the **STREAM** layout (Hoang, Reyhanitabar, Rogaway, Vizár — *Online Authenticated-Encryption and its Nonce-Reuse Misuse-Resistance*, CRYPTO 2015):

```
nonce[12] = prefix[7] ‖ counter_be[4] ‖ last_flag[1]
```

- **`prefix[7]`** — derived, NOT transmitted: `prefix = HKDF-SHA256(epoch_dek; info)[0..7]` where the HKDF `info` is the **byte-exact** concatenation: `info = b"ciris-stream-nonce/v1" ‖ stream_id_utf8 ‖ epoch_be8`, with `stream_id_utf8` = the UTF-8 bytes of the stream's id in its own form, `av-` or `file-` followed by the lowercase hex of the 32 bytes the chunk header carries, 67 or 69 bytes, and **`epoch_be8` = the `u64` epoch as 8-byte big-endian** (`epoch.to_be_bytes()`, consistent with `counter_be`). **This encoding is normative and MUST be byte-identical across producer, substrate, and every consumer**. Every consumer recomputes this exact nonce to *open* chunks, so any BE/LE/ASCII disagreement on `epoch` yields a different `prefix` → different nonce → GCM auth-tag failure (silent whole-stream decryption failure), the same hazard class `counter_be` already guards. No length-prefix on `stream_id` is required. The tag prefix has a fixed length, the id's own first bytes say which of its two forms it has, each form has one length, and the `epoch` suffix is 8 bytes. So the parse is unambiguous, and distinct `(stream_id, epoch)` pairs always yield distinct `info`. A realtime data stream ([CC 5.3.3.4](#5.3.3.4)) takes the `av-` form, which names a stream id and claims nothing about media. The bare 64-hex form names only an inline blob's one-leaf log and seals no chunk ([CC 5.3.3.8](#5.3.3.8)). Matches the **`KEY_GRANT_V1_INFO`** versioned-context HKDF pattern (`b"cewp-key-grant/v1"`). Per-`(stream_id, epoch)` unique; verifiable by any holder of the epoch DEK
- **`counter_be[4]`** — 32-bit big-endian; hard ceiling 2³²−1 chunks per epoch. Substrate MUST force an epoch roll before wrap. Recommended operational cap: **`MAX_CHUNKS_PER_EPOCH = 2²⁴`** (~16.7M chunks/epoch) to keep per-epoch state + proof sizes bounded (operator-tunable)
- **`last_flag[1]`** — `0x01` on the final chunk of an epoch; `0x00` otherwise. It is set by the epoch terminator and is not a header field: like `prefix`, every holder derives it, from the epoch's seal, and never reads it off the chunk. The distinct nonce on the final chunk gives **truncation + append resistance**: an adversary cannot drop the final chunk and pass off a short stream, nor append past a sealed segment

**Cross-epoch counter reset is nonce-safe (normative reasoning)**: GCM's catastrophic case is reuse of a `(key, nonce)` pair. On epoch roll the DEK changes, so a reset counter lives in a different keyspace — `(DEK_e, nonce=0)` and `(DEK_{e+1}, nonce=0)` are distinct pairs. The enforced invariant is therefore only within a single epoch: counter strictly monotonic, never wraps (guaranteed by the forced roll). Across epochs, reset is free.

**Single-sender-per-`(stream_id, epoch)` invariant (normative — nonce-collision safety; as in SFrame/MLS)**: the `counter_be[4]` space of a `(stream_id, epoch)` is owned by **exactly one** sender — the `stream_id`'s producer. Two distinct senders MUST NOT seal chunks under the same `(stream_id, epoch)` DEK, or their independently-incremented counters could collide into a reused `(DEK, nonce)` pair (GCM-catastrophic). In **group video** ([CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2)) each participant emits their **own** `live_stream` with their **own** `stream_id`, so the nonce prefix `HKDF(epoch_dek; "ciris-stream-nonce/v1" ‖ stream_id ‖ epoch)` is per-sender-unique by construction. This avoids the same hazard SFrame avoids with per-sender keys, here by per-sender `stream_id`. Substrate MUST reject a chunk-append whose `(stream_id, epoch, chunk_seq)` collides with an existing sealed chunk (the replay and forking guard).

#### 5.3.3.2 `composition` — Realtime group communication — composition

The delivery axis was framed for 1:1 observer-share and 1:N broadcast multicast ([CC 5.3.3](#5.3.3)). Realtime **group communication** — group video, voice, desktop/screen sharing, text chat, and topic-scoped channels with sub-channels — is the **same primitive set at N↔N cardinality**. It composes entirely from `community` ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)) + `live_stream` (the CC 5.3.3 streaming surface) + `chat_message` + member/transport resolution ([CC 4.4.3.8](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.8)). **Zero new structural primitives** ([CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md#1.7)): the whole realtime-collaboration surface is composition.

**The composition map (all generic — no new wire):**

| Surface | Composes from |
|---|---|
| **1:1 / group video call** | each participant emits a `live_stream` (their A/V) scoped to the channel `community`; each subscribes to peers. N↔N = N simultaneous bidirectional streams over a small roster |
| **Voice channel** | identical to group video with an audio-only codec; same `live_stream` wire |
| **Desktop / screen sharing** | a `live_stream` whose source is a screen capture (1→N within the channel); same chunk-seal + epoch-DEK wire |
| **Text chat** | `chat_message` at `cohort_scope: community`, `community_id: <channel>`; threads via `refs.answers` ([CC 3.3.11](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.11)) |
| **Channel** | a `community` (persistent) — its roster gates who can join the call / read the chat |
| **Sub-channels** | nested `community` membership ([CC 4.4.3.9](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.9) multi-level pattern): a parent "space" community whose members admit child channel-communities; sub-channel members are a subset of the space roster |
| **Presence ("who's here")** | the reachable set ([CC 5.3.3.9](#5.3.3.9)) — node-local, never an attestation, never logged |
| **Invite / join / leave** | community admission ceremony ([CC 4.4.3.6](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.6)) — invite = membership proposal (`membership:proposal:v1`); join = admitted member, by a membership widening **on the invitee's own `membership:acceptance:v1`** ([CC 3.1.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.2)); decline = `membership:decline:v1`; leave = the member's own `membership:resignation:v1` |

**Transport profiles (normative — extends CC 5.3.3.10):**

| Profile | Topology | Transport |
|---|---|---|
| Broadcast (1:N, large N) | asymmetric | pull-only `ContentFetch` (CC 5.3.3.10 E2); no relay tree |
| **Realtime small/medium group** (calls, huddles, ≤ ~50) | symmetric mesh | **direct Reticulum Links between participants** (low-latency push; no relay tree needed at small N) |
| Realtime large group (≫50 in one A/V room) | fan-out | push through the member relay tree ([CC 6.1.6](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.6)), only the layers asked for ([CC 5.3.3.9](#5.3.3.9)); `ContentFetch` (CC 5.3.3.10 E2) for a missed chunk |

The low-latency realtime profile (direct Reticulum Links) needs no relay tree for small/medium rosters — RNS Links give encrypted low-latency point-to-point natively. The wire is identical to broadcast (chunk-seal CC 5.3.3.1, per-`(stream_id, epoch)` epoch DEK CC 5.1, per-stream head CC 5.3.3.8); only the transport profile + roster size differ. A live chunk and a stored chunk are the **same sealed object**. So "record a call" is retention policy over chunks that already exist as a DAG, "VOD" is the puller at offset zero, and a licence is a `key_grant` the owner chooses to issue over the same bytes. **PQC is unchanged and mandatory** — epoch DEK wrapped `wrap_algorithm: v2` (X25519+ML-KEM-768) at rest, hybrid KEX in transit ([CC 5.1](#5.1)).

**A member relays for a member (normative).** Where two participants of a call cannot link directly, another member of the same room MAY forward the sealed chunks of one to the other. That is a member relay ([CC 5.3.3.10](#5.3.3.10) E1), whatever the size of the room. It forwards sealed chunks only, and it holds no key it does not hold as a member. A member device relays, and is relayed for, whether or not its owner has announced it. Neither the serving rule of [CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6) nor the relay duty of the onion tier reaches a member relay.

**Ephemeral vs persistent rosters**: a persistent channel is a long-lived `community`; an ad-hoc call is an **ephemeral `community`** (short `valid_until`, torn down on last-leave). Same primitive, different lifetime — no special-case "session" primitive.

The breadth confirmation: a full realtime group-communication platform — group video, voice, screen sharing, chat, and channels-with-sub-channels — requires **no addition to the 1+4 structural set** beyond the CC 5.3.3 delivery axis and the `community` membership machinery of [CC 4.4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3).

#### 5.3.3.3 `namespace-realtime` — `codec_id` namespace — realtime A/V chunk codec discriminator (normative)

[CC 5.3.3.4](#5.3.3.4) makes the realtime chunk payload codec **application-defined and opaque to the substrate**. For realtime **A/V at scale**, a fetching node asks a serving peer for one layer, and the peer sends that layer, **without** either side decrypting the chunks — so the codec's layer-numbering semantics must be a **clear (non-AEAD) discriminator**; no relay reads it. CEG defines a 1-byte `codec_id` namespace so every implementation reads the same meaning. **This is a namespace on the transport-layer chunk header, not a change to the [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) attestation envelope** — the frozen 1+4 surface and its canonicalization are untouched.

**Wire position (normative).** `codec_id` (1 byte) + `ChunkLayer { spatial: u8, temporal: u8, quality: u8 }` (3 bytes) = a **4-byte additive block** at `SealedAvChunk` header offset **48..52**, after the 48-byte fixed header. **Clear metadata, NOT inside the AEAD** — a fetching node asks for, and a serving peer sends, one layer by `codec_id`/`ChunkLayer` without touching the inner epoch-DEK seal; no relay reads it ([CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1)); tampering causes mis-decode or drop, never a crypto break. No length-prefix is needed — the block is fixed 4 bytes at a fixed offset.

| Hex | Codec | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `0x01` | **AV1 SVC** | Scalable Video Coding — 3 spatial × 4 temporal × N SNR layers; base layer required to decode anything. Production default (WebRTC-native, royalty-free). |
| `0x02` | JPEG XS (layered) | Low-latency intra-only; broadcast use case. **Reserved.** |
| `0x03` | **Symmetric MDC** | Multiple Description Coding — any subset of chunks decodes at proportional fidelity, no base-layer floor. **The substrate design target** (below). **Reserved**; no production encoder is assumed; substrate is MDC-ready. |
| `0x04` | **Temporal-layered, one spatial layer** | For a codec with temporal scalability and no spatial layers (H.264, VP8, VP9 and their kind): `ChunkLayer { 0, t, 0 }`, base = `t = 0`, enhancements at higher `t`; the codec itself is named by the stream's binding, never by this id, which carries layer semantics only. For a device that cannot encode the production default in real time. |
| `0xFF` | Opaque | No scalable-coding semantics. `ChunkLayer` MUST be `{ 0, 0, 0 }`. Default for non-layered streams and for audio. |
| `0x05`–`0x7F` | — | **Reserved** for future standardized codecs (CEG-assigned). |
| `0x80`–`0xFE` | — | **Experimental / per-deployment** — no cross-federation meaning guaranteed. |

**What every client decodes (normative).** Every client decodes `0xFF`, which carries audio, so a call never falls silent for want of a video codec; every client decodes `0x01`, the production default; a client SHOULD decode `0x04`, and a publisher MAY emit it only where it cannot encode `0x01` in real time; a receiver that cannot decode a stream's video keeps its audio, and the client says so. Shedding reads the layer and never the id: the base of any layered stream is its `ChunkLayer` base, and an opaque stream is base. `codec_id` lets a receiver know whether `ChunkLayer { spatial: 2, temporal: 2, quality: 0 }` means "SVC base + 2 spatial enhancements" or "MDC quadrant" — without it, layer numbers are ambiguous across codecs. The substrate (Edge) never picks the codec — choice is upstream (agent/server tier); Edge needs only the namespace stable. The variable-depth `SubStreamPath` (MDC tree-path encoding) is reserved for amendment.

**MDC-primacy design intent (informative).** The user-facing contract the realtime A/V plane targets is *"any node can request a lower-bandwidth stream from peers — as simple as taking every other chunk, down to a blinking dot."* MDC (`0x03`) matches that **symmetrically**: drop any subset → decode the rest at proportionally lower quality, no coordination, no base-layer floor. SVC (`0x01`) is the production default but has a floor (base-layer bytes must arrive) and needs coordination for an "every other chunk" drop. The substrate is **MDC-shaped** (the `ChunkLayer` / `SubStreamPath` model is symmetric-drop-ready) while the production default is SVC; the MDC compression overhead against SVC at equal quality is the accepted cost of symmetric drop semantics.

#### 5.3.3.4 `realtime` — Realtime non-A/V data streams (normative scope boundary)

The realtime profile is **not media-only.** Any high-frequency mutable shared state rides the **same** CC 5.3.3.2 realtime transport (direct Reticulum Links; at scale, pull-only ContentFetch per [CC 5.3.3.10](#5.3.3.10) E2), with an application-defined payload codec in place of an A/V codec. At scale only a call's A/V chunks push through the member relay tree ([CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2)); a data stream's chunks are pulled. Such state includes multiplayer game ticks, collaborative-editing operations (CRDT/OT), live cursors/whiteboard strokes, remote-control input and high-rate telemetry. The wire is identical: per-`(stream_id, epoch)` epoch DEK (CC 5.1, `wrap_algorithm: v2` PQC), STREAM-nonce chunk seal (CC 5.3.3.1), per-stream head (CC 5.3.3.8). A data-stream chunk is just a chunk.

**Scope boundary (the explicit call):**
- **IN scope (transport):** ordered, sealed, authenticated, PQC-encrypted realtime delivery of arbitrary data-stream payloads — covered by CC 5.3.3.2, no addition.
- **OUT of scope (merge semantic):** the conflict-free / convergent-merge logic for shared mutable state (CRDT, Operational Transform, last-writer-wins, etc.) is **application-layer**, not a CEG primitive. This is consistent with the [CC 1.13.4](part_1_foundation.md#1.13.4) discipline ("the substrate stores; the wire transports; CEG describes the shape of the claim; consumer policy composes verdicts"). CEG carries the ops; the application converges them. A codified merge primitive, if one is ever added, routes through the [CC 4.5.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.1) amendment process; none is required, because a realtime collaborative application is buildable on the transport as it stands.

#### 5.3.3.5 `registry-wire` — `SealedAvChunk` wire layout (normative)

The realtime A/V chunk that lands on each RNS Link payload (and the broadcast pull path). **Byte layout (normative):**

```
offset  field                       encoding
0..32   stream_id                   32 bytes of the stream's id (a call stream: the binding's derivation;
                                    a chunked file: the file derivation of CC 5.3.3.8)
32..40  epoch                       u64 big-endian
40..48  chunk_seq                   u64 big-endian
48..49  codec_id                    u8  (CC 5.3.3.3 namespace)
49..50  layer.spatial               u8
50..51  layer.temporal              u8
51..52  layer.quality               u8
52..    double_sealed_ciphertext    remaining bytes
```

- `CHUNK_HEADER_LEN = 48` (the `stream_id`+`epoch`+`chunk_seq` fixed header); `CHUNK_CODEC_LAYER_LEN = 4` (the `codec_id`+`ChunkLayer` block).
- **The block is always present; no length-disambiguated compatibility (normative).** The 4-byte `codec_id` + `ChunkLayer` block is part of every chunk: the header is 52 bytes, and a wire shorter than 52 bytes, or whose ciphertext does not carry its AEAD tag, is refused as malformed. Length does not select a layout: a 48-byte wire carries no ciphertext and no tag and could never open.
- `codec_id` + `layer` are **clear metadata, NOT inputs to the AEAD** ([CC 5.3.3.3](#5.3.3.3)) — a fetching node asks for, and a serving peer sends, one layer by `(codec_id, layer)` without compromising the inner DEK; no relay reads it; tampering causes mis-decode or drop, never a crypto break.
- **One chunk, one link payload (normative).** A sealed A/V chunk rides the RNS Link whole, under the [CC 5.3.3.7](#5.3.3.7) outer seal (AES-256-GCM), itself inside the link's [CC 5.3.3.10](#5.3.3.10) E1 transit seal; it is never fragmented into symbols. The sender checks the chunk against the link's channel payload MDU before sending and refuses an oversize chunk as `ChunkTooLarge`, never splitting it. No symbol envelope, no XChaCha20-Poly1305 and no `K_symbol` ([CC 5.4.2](#5.4.2)) is on this path.

**Source authentication: the binding and the trailer (normative; part of the chunk format).** Every member of a room can derive every stream's epoch DEK ([CC 5.3.3.7](#5.3.3.7)), so the DEK proves membership, not authorship: without more, one member could mint chunks that open under another member's stream. The format therefore carries two more objects, and a chunk that lacks either is refused. **(1) The `StreamKeyBinding`** states that one ephemeral Ed25519 key signs one stream's chunks in one epoch, and what the publisher says of that stream. Its encoding is a fixed big-endian concatenation, no CBOR and no JSON, of these members in this order:

```
version     u8: 0x02
room        u16 len ‖ UTF-8, 1 to 1024 bytes: the community key id
publisher   u16 len ‖ UTF-8, 1 to 1024 bytes: the publisher's federation key id
join_nonce  32 bytes
stream_id   32 bytes: SHA-256("ciris-edge:call-stream:v3" ‖ u16 len ‖ room ‖ u16 len ‖ publisher ‖ join_nonce), each u16 the big-endian byte length of the field after it, join_nonce the fixed 32 bytes
epoch       u64: the room's MLS epoch
chunk_key   32 bytes: the Ed25519 public key
codec_map   u8 count (0..=8) ‖ count × ( class u8 ‖ u16 len ‖ token, ASCII, 1..=32 bytes )
            sorted by class, no class twice; a registered token sits under its own class
replaces    u8 0 | 1 ‖ (if 1) stream_id[32]
end         u8: 0 none, 1 Left, 2 Backgrounded, 3 Ended
final_seq   u64, present iff end ≠ 0 (u64::MAX: no chunk sealed)
kind        u8: 0 media, 1 share (an unknown value reads as media)
framing     u8: 0 none, 1 fragments (any other value is refused)
profile     u8: 0 best-effort, 1 accountable (any other value is refused)
signature   u16 len, which MUST be 3373 ‖ the composite signature of CC 2.6.1.7
```

`stream_id` MUST equal the derivation shown, and a registered codec token MUST sit under its own class. Each fixed length, the signature's included, is enforced at parse. The whole encoding is at most 8192 bytes and trailing bytes are refused. Every member before `signature` is the unsigned body, and the signing bytes are `"ciris-edge:av-stream-key:v2" ‖ body`. The composite signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)) is over those bytes, signed by the publisher's federation key. That is the publishing member's own key on the producing device, a person's roster key there or an agent's key, and never a node key, so two members on one node publish apart. A verifier checks it by verification, never by byte equality. **Who reads each member.** `codec_map` gives a receiver its decoder for each layer class, and an unregistered token makes its class locally undecodable. `replaces` swaps a stream in place, as for a codec or device change. `end` and `final_seq` are the only signed leave: a receiver acts on a leave only from them, never from an unsigned control frame, and drops chunks past `final_seq`. Call recovery reads `end` to tell a background from a leave. `kind` sets the tile layout for a share. `framing` says whether the 8-byte fragment marker is in use. `profile` says whether the stream is accountable, and the receipt guard of [CC 5.3.3.11](#5.3.3.11) reads it. **A receiver accepts a binding in this order:** parse; a binding already seen is known and not re-verified; the room equals the call's room; the stream id re-derives from the publisher and nonce; the publisher is in the room's MLS group; the composite signature verifies against the directory; then it is installed, a stream keeping its two newest epochs and a publisher its four newest streams; a binding whose epoch is older than both epochs a stream already holds is refused, and with one held an older one is accepted. Refusals are not cached. **The binding travels in parts** on the A/V link: each part is `"CSKB" ‖ 0x01 ‖ id ‖ index ‖ count ‖ payload`, the id being the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 of the binding's encoding, at most 64 parts, each payload the link's message limit less the 15-byte part header, reassembled per link (at most four in flight, the count equal in every part, a duplicate index ignored, the whole hashing to its id); a publisher never mints a stream id beginning `"CSKB" 0x01`.
