A part takes no outer seal and no hop sequence; the link's E1 seal covers it like every frame. **When it is sent:** on every new leg, after the transit KEX and the stream hello and before the leg joins the fan-out roster, so no chunk precedes its binding, and on that same new leg a member relay also sends every binding it holds except the dialled member's own, whoever it heard each from, once; at every epoch roll, in a fixed order under one lock (derive the new DEK, mint the new key and binding, roll, swap the key, remove departed members' legs, send the binding on every remaining leg), so the new binding precedes the new epoch's first chunk on every leg; and every ten seconds, to replace a binding lost to an overflow. **Bindings travel only on member-to-member legs:** a node dials only the room's MLS members at their derived call addresses, a departed member's leg is removed at the roll before the new binding is sent, and an inbound link from a non-member is closed before any frame is read. A member relay forwards a binding it has verified to every other leg, and only when the binding's publisher is the peer it heard it from, so a re-send passes along and cannot loop. A non-member forwarder ([CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6)) never receives, verifies or forwards a binding, which names the room and the publisher; it carries the sealed frames opaque. **(2) The trailer** is 72 bytes, `u64 source_ms ‖ signature`, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal. `source_ms` is the publisher's clock in UNIX milliseconds at sealing, signed so that a relay's latency meter reads a time no relay can forge. The signature is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature, not a half of a composite, since its key is ephemeral to one stream and one epoch and a composite signature binds it to the publisher. It is made by the bound chunk key over `"ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2" ‖ stream_id ‖ u64 epoch ‖ u64 chunk_seq ‖ codec_id ‖ spatial ‖ temporal ‖ quality ‖ u64 source_ms ‖ inner_aead`. `inner_aead` is the inner ciphertext including its 16-byte tag; the chunk header is unchanged. **A member relay verifies without the DEK:** parse the chunk, open the outer seal at the hop counter, look up the bound key for the stream and epoch (else `av_chunk_unbound`), take the last 72 bytes as the trailer (else `av_chunk_trailer_missing`), split it into `source_ms` and the signature, verify strictly (else `av_chunk_trailer_invalid`), and forward the unit byte for byte, re-sealing only the outer layer, only when the link's hello named the stream and the stream's binding names the verified publisher. A relay checks that publisher at every hop, never that the link's peer is the publisher. **A receiver** does the same and then opens the inner seal with the DEK; the frame's publisher is the binding's, never the hello's. No step reads the store and no step runs a hybrid verification. **The budget:** the frame's plaintext is the link's channel limit less 156 bytes (84 of chunk overhead and the 72-byte trailer): 244 bytes at the base link MTU of 500 and 1140 bytes on a punched direct link at MTU 1400; a frame over the budget is refused before sealing. **The refusal tokens**, one closed vocabulary identical at a relay and a receiver, each counted under its own name and one aggregate: `av_binding_part_malformed`, `av_binding_malformed`, `av_binding_other_room`, `av_binding_publisher_not_member`, `av_binding_stream_not_derived`, `av_binding_signature_unverified`, `av_binding_stale_epoch` (the aggregate `av_call_binding_refused`); `av_chunk_unbound` (`av_call_frame_unbound`); `av_chunk_trailer_missing`, `av_chunk_trailer_invalid` (`av_call_frame_forged`). **Known answers (normative; the vectors the release carries):** publisher `node-kat-a` with Ed25519 seed `01`×32 and ML-DSA-65 seed `54`×32, room `room-kat`, join nonce `07`×32, epoch 5, chunk key seed `0c`×32, DEK `42`×32, chunk 0 of codec `ff` at layer (0,0,0) with plaintext `kat-chunk-0`, source timestamp `1790000000000` ms, forger seed `0f`×32: `stream_id` `c7adfc999afbc7643b24eab3b57ca66540315d345e52bbb33cfa1d5dfb9c18d8`, chunk public key `0b513ad9b4924015ca0902ed079044d3ac5dbec2306f06948c10da8eb6e39f2d`, the publisher's composite public key with SHA-256 `b2cf9b1e41fec62e7807a9d7314b805c510f7502d6a17a1103ed382b1b2f3f30`, two bindings, their full bytes carried by the verification library: one with codec map `av1` under class `01` and `opus` under `ff`, replacing the stream of join nonce `08`×32, `end` 2 with `final_seq` 41, `kind` 0, `framing` 1 and `profile` 1, its 3561-byte encoding with SHA-256 `b18d2ec2fbbf2f46a0196e88e52d6149e39a1a59cf6483a151401e0abfa0ac70` and so part id `b18d2ec2fbbf2f46`; and one with codec map `opus` under `ff` alone and every later member 0, its 3515-byte encoding with SHA-256 `c7a6aaf092ef815490edae74db49543ba7bd1f52e8d1fceb80c7966899b0fa1a` and so part id `c7a6aaf092ef8154`; over the inner ciphertext `b3b432abd9ea536a45a933956e21b34dc01e4571e5196d0aa08396` the trailer `000001a0c4506c00` ‖ `cf846332…0a14ff09` verifying as `node-kat-a`, the forger's trailer refused `av_chunk_trailer_invalid`, the inner unit truncated to 20 bytes refused `av_chunk_trailer_missing`. **The post-quantum position.** The chunk key is classical and ephemeral, minted per stream and epoch; its authentication need hold only for the stream's lifetime, and the long-lived object that names it, the binding, is composite-signed. [CC 5.3.3.10](#5.3.3.10) E1's hybrid rule is about confidentiality and [CC 5.3.2.8](#5.3.2.8)'s about durable records; a live chunk is neither. The residual, stated: an adversary who breaks Ed25519 online within one stream's epoch, and who also holds that epoch's DEK, could forge chunks of that stream for that epoch; the residual is bounded to a member for one stream and one epoch. One further residual: between a member's removal from the MLS group and the node's next roll, at most one 250 ms watch tick, a re-announce may send the departed member the current binding, which it already held as a member of that epoch.

#### 5.3.3.6 `chunklayer` — `ChunkLayer` + `ReceiverLayerPolicy` — SVC layer model (normative)

`ChunkLayer` is the 3-byte SVC layer descriptor in the chunk header (`spatial`, `temporal`, `quality`, each `u8`). Each axis is **monotonic**: layer `0` is the base (lowest fidelity, always required); each increment is an additive enhancement. A receiver reconstructs from the prefix `0..=max_spatial × 0..=max_temporal × 0..=max_quality` of cells. The base cell `{0,0,0}` is the **"blinking dot"** — the minimum a participant can subscribe to. For `codec_id = 0xFF` (opaque) the layer MUST be `{0,0,0}` ([CC 5.3.3.3](#5.3.3.3)).

`ReceiverLayerPolicy { max_spatial, max_temporal, max_quality }` (each `u8`) is the per-receiver drop policy. It is **advertised over the existing `federation_session` / `key_grant` entitlement surface — NOT a new wire** — and the sender drops chunks above the cap without re-encoding. `admits(layer)` is the per-axis test `spatial ≤ max_spatial ∧ temporal ≤ max_temporal ∧ quality ≤ max_quality`; a chunk tagged `codec_id = 0xFF` MUST be admitted **unconditionally** regardless of policy (the fan-out filter short-circuits before consulting `admits`). Canonical policies: `BLINKING_DOT = {0,0,0}`, `UNCAPPED = {255,255,255}`. This composes with the inner-once / outer-N fan-out optimization: the inner seal runs once per chunk; the outer seal runs only for the `(receiver, chunk)` pairs the policy admits.

#### 5.3.3.7 `stream-double` — Double-seal + deterministic nonce derivation (normative)

`double_sealed_ciphertext` is **outer-AEAD( inner-AEAD( chunk_plaintext ) )** — two independent AES-256-GCM layers (12-byte nonce + 16-byte tag, standard ring layout each). The **inner** seal is end-to-end (the epoch-DEK content seal); the **outer** seal is the per-RNS-Link transit wrap (a relay sees the outer layer only, never plaintext — the [CC 5.3.3.10 E1](#5.3.3.10) two-layer posture). Both nonces are **deterministic** (no nonce is transmitted — every holder recomputes; collision-safety rides the [CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2) single-sender-per-`(stream_id, epoch)` invariant).

**One chunk seal (normative).** The inner seal **is** the [CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1) chunk seal: the STREAM nonce `prefix[7] ‖ counter_be[4] ‖ last_flag[1]`, with `counter` = the chunk's `chunk_seq` (the header's `u64` field carries it; it MUST stay below 2³² within an epoch, the 5.3.3.1 ceiling, with the forced epoch roll before wrap) and `last_flag` set on the epoch's final chunk. There is no second inner nonce, so a live chunk is stored as it was, a stored chunk can be served into a call, and [CC 5.3.3.9](#5.3.3.9)'s reconnect-then-pull works for a call. Live and stored chunks are one object model, differing only by subscriber offset. The **outer** nonce is:

```
outer_nonce = SHA-256( b"CIRIS-AV-OUTER-V1" ‖ link_id ‖ link_seq_be8 )[0..12]
```

The label bytes (`b"CIRIS-AV-OUTER-V1"`, ASCII, no terminator) are a **domain separator pinned by this section**. `link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per outer key on an RNS Link: one counter for each pair of link and outer key, and one outer key is never live for two streams (transit replay guard).

**Where the two inputs come from (normative).** Neither nonce input rides the frame. `last_flag` is set by the epoch terminator and is not a header field ([CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1)). `link_seq` is that pair's counter, kept by both ends and never carried in the frame. It starts at 0 for the first frame under a new pair and advances by one per frame; the sender advances it once per frame sealed; the receiver advances it only on a frame that authenticates. After loss, the receiver counts the frames it dropped before its sink and reports that count on its next frame, and the sender's hop tries, in order, `next + dropped`, `next`, and a bounded slack above that — in this edition eight counters, at most ten opens per frame — and never a counter below `next`, so a replay never opens. A frame is tried under at most ten counters, so a forger's chance on one frame and a receiver's work on a forged frame are at most ten times those of one open. Loss neither end observes is covered only by that slack; beyond it the hop ends loudly, and there is no in-band resync. **Conformance is proven by the vector set** for the outer nonce and `to_bytes`, published with the release; the inner seal's vectors are 5.3.3.1's. `codec_id` and `ChunkLayer` stay clear metadata outside both AEADs.

**Keeping a call (normative).** A call is live by default and nothing of it is held past forwarding. **Each stream is kept by its own publisher and by nobody else:** a participant's stream carries that participant's own voice and picture, so the one who may make it durable is its owner, as durability is the owner's per item ([CC 6.1.5.1](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.5.1)); the room's policy row MAY forbid keeping in that room, never require it; and every participant is told at joining whether streams in this room may be kept, before they publish ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13), the choice explained before it is made). A screen share is its publisher's stream and is kept the same way: what was on the publisher's screen is in it, the call's own window with the other participants in it included, and a room that forbids keeping forbids it for a share as for a camera. A kept stream is its sealed chunks held under the epoch keys they were sealed with, so **a later joiner reads a kept stream only from the epochs whose keys they hold**. An earlier epoch's key reaches a joiner only by the publisher's own wrap: by `history_on_join: full`, within the catch-up bound ([CC 5.1](#5.1)), or by a later grant. A publisher changes keep mid-stream in whole epochs, one DEK per stream per epoch: turning it on wraps the current and later epochs, turning it off stops wrapping from the next, and neither reaches an earlier epoch ([CC 5.1](#5.1)).

#### 5.3.3.8 `per-stream` — Per-stream log + stream-root (normative)

**A stream's id has one of three forms (normative).** The form says what the stream is, and no reader has to ask. An inline blob's one-leaf log is named by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits and nothing else: the hex of the blob's at-rest content address. That bare form is reserved for it. It names the log in a delivery ack and never in a head, since a `stream:head` row takes only the two forms below. An A/V stream is `av-` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits ([CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1)). A chunked file is `file-` followed by the 64 lowercase hex digits of a SHA-256. Its input is the 20 bytes `ciris:file-stream:v1`, the two-byte big-endian length of the producer, the producer, and a nonce of 32 random bytes. The producer is the opening member's identity reference as UTF-8 text, 1 to 1024 bytes. So the id commits to its producer as an A/V stream's does, and to nobody without the nonce does it differ from random bytes. The opener keeps the producer and the nonce with the stream. They travel beside a head as submission material and never in a payload. A node that holds no part of the stream recomputes the id from them and checks that the head's author is that producer. The holder that opens the stream mints that id before any key is registered or any chunk is sealed, since each chunk's seal binds it. A caller never supplies it, and the sealed manifest carries it. A node that receives the stream's chunks or its manifest takes its `file-` id as read, and checks only its form. A stream whose id has none of the three forms is refused. A file's id is not derived from its content: a reader holding a copy of the file could otherwise confirm that it is stored. So the same file put twice is two streams.

A stream is its own log, and its chunks are the leaves. The log is the producer's. It is what makes a producer accountable for what it streamed: each signed head commits the producer to a single chunk history. The root is the [RFC 6962](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6962) Merkle root over the first `tree_size` leaves. Each leaf is the chunk's SHA-256 in `seq` order, hashed under the `0x00` prefix, and each inner node is hashed under the `0x01` prefix.

**The head is a row (normative).** A stream's head is a signed row of family `stream:head`, wire `stream:head:v1` ([CC 3.1.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3)). Its author is the stream's producer, a member's key and never a node's, and nobody else writes a stream's head. Its `sub` is `stream:` followed by the stream's id in the `av-` or the `file-` form. The row that carries the head is a statement of [CC 2.6.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.1), signed as every row is, with one composite signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)). Its payload carries these members:

| Member | What it states |
|---|---|
| `author` | the producer's identity reference |
| `asserted_at` | the producer's signed instant |
| `epoch` | the stream's epoch at this head ([CC 5.1](#5.1)) |
| `tree_size` | the count of chunks the root covers, at least 1 |
| `root` | the Merkle root over the first `tree_size` leaves |
| `sealed` | optional, and true on the head that seals the stream |
| `refs.prev` | optional: the head this one follows |
| `room` | optional: the community key id of the room the stream is accountable in |
| `dimension` | `stream:head:v1` |

A head carries no list of witnesses and no proof. The consistency proof from an earlier head is submission material beside the statement ([RFC-9942], label 396), never a payload member ([CC 5.3.1.1](#5.3.1.1)).

**An inline file publishes no head.** An inline file is a log of one leaf, and no head is published for it. Its root is the leaf's own hash, the blob's SHA-256 under the `0x00` prefix, which every holder of the blob computes. A delivery ack over an inline blob is checked against that leaf ([CC 5.3.3.11](#5.3.3.11)), and the file's row carries no head.

**Best-effort and accountable (normative).** A head that carries `room` is **accountable**, and a head without it is **best-effort**. A best-effort head stands on its producer's signature alone: it registers with a service on the ordinary rules and is never counted as accountable. The heads of a stream whose binding's `profile` is 1 carry `room` ([CC 5.3.3.5](#5.3.3.5)). A reader that holds the binding checks that the head's `room` is the room the binding names, and refuses a head that differs, `stream_head_room_mismatch`.

**The services of a room (normative).** A room MAY name `transparency_services` and `receipt_quorum` in its record, for its accountable streams only ([CC 2.6.1.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.4)). The two members are present together or not at all. `transparency_services` is a set of at least two identity references, each to a composite key, and `receipt_quorum` is exactly ⌊n/2⌋ + 1 of the n named. The producer registers each accountable head with those services, and each answers with a Receipt from its own log ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)). An accountable head counts as **published** when `receipt_quorum` distinct services of the room have registered it. A service that the producer runs, or that the producer's owner runs, does not count. A room keeps no attach window, no cadence and no quorum of its own for its roster ([CC 4.4.3.7](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.7)). So a published head stays published, and no Receipt of it grows stale.

**Starting an accountable stream (normative).** A producer MUST NOT start an accountable stream in a room that names no services, or whose services that count are fewer than its `receipt_quorum`. The producer refuses by name, `stream_accountable_pool_below_quorum`, and never falls back to best-effort silently.

**What a service checks (normative).** A service registers one head for each stream and tree size. The first head it registers for a stream MAY name a `refs.prev` or none, and its Receipt says nothing of the stream's earlier history. Each later head is offered with a consistency proof from the head the service last registered for that stream. The service judges `refs.prev` only where it holds the head that member names. It refuses a head on any line of this table, and it keeps a refused head as evidence.

| Refusal | The fault |
|---|---|
| `stream_head_prev_not_last` | the head names in `refs.prev` a head the service holds that is not the one it last registered for the stream |
| `stream_head_equivocation` | the service has registered a head of the stream at this `tree_size` with a different `root` |
| `stream_head_repeated` | the service has registered a head of the stream at this `tree_size` with this `root`, and this head does not seal the stream |
| `stream_head_epoch_regressed` | `epoch` is below that of the head last registered |
| `stream_head_inconsistent` | the consistency proof from the head last registered is absent or does not verify |
| `stream_head_room_mismatch` | `room` differs from the room of the stream's binding, or from the `room` of the head last registered |
| `stream_head_after_seal` | the service has registered the head that seals the stream |
| `stream_head_interval_below_floor` | the stream states a head interval below 30 seconds |

Two heads of one stream at one tree size with different roots are the producer's equivocation, and both carry its signature. The quorum is a strict majority of the services named, so two such heads are never both published unless one service registered both. That is the **anti-equivocation guarantee**: a producer cannot show a different chunk K to different subscribers, nor rewrite mid-stream. It holds while the services check consistency before they register, and while no quorum of them colludes.

**Cadence (normative).** The producer signs a head at each epoch boundary ([CC 5.1](#5.1)) and at sealing. Between them it signs one head for every head interval or every 1024 chunks, whichever comes first. The head interval is the producer's and is at least 30 seconds. The stream's binding states it, and that member's bytes are an open encoding ([CC 2.6.1.12](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.12)). A best-effort stream MAY publish no head.

**Incremental verify.** A subscriber verifies chunk K's inclusion against the nearest held head at `tree_size` K or more, by an inclusion proof under that head's `root`. No commitment structure is needed beyond the chunks' own hashes and the stream's heads.

#### 5.3.3.9 `liveness` — Liveness invariant — entitled vs reachable (normative)

Two sets are NEVER conflated — the durable record of who is *allowed* in, and the ephemeral fact of who is *currently here*. Mixing them would turn presence into a logged, federated attestation, which the fail-secure posture forbids:

- **Entitlement roster** (the store's): signed CEG envelope, propagated by the transport, durable, logged. It's **evidence** — it MUST propagate + be auditable. Per [CC 4.4.3.3–4.4.3.12](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.3) Policy M community-membership composition
- **Live-reachability set** (Edge-owned): generalizes the holding claim's 72 h liveness ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.3)) down to seconds-to-minutes for live-multicast. Node-local presence tracker. **NEVER an attestation, never a holding claim, never replicated, never logged**

**Fan-out invariant: `fan_out(C) = entitled(C) ∩ reachable(now)`**.

**Layered multipath (normative).** A member MAY take each layer of a stream from a different parent of the member relay tree ([CC 6.1.6](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.6)). A chunk that a member's parent did not deliver, the member pulls from a sibling under the same parent before it asks the parent again. So a phone publishes a stream once, each first-hop peer carrying a layer and passing it on, and the stream reassembles wherever a member holds every layer it asked for. **The presence floor (normative).** Every `codec_id` class defines a floor layer, a presence tile of colour and a blink at one frame a second at a stated rate of a few tens of bytes a second. A receiver in a call of `N` senders subscribes each sender at the highest layer that fits its budget divided by `N`, and a relay forwards only the layers downstream asked for. So a call never excludes a sender for bandwidth: quality falls, presence does not. Neither needs a new wire shape: the layer header of [CC 5.3.3.3](#5.3.3.3), the tree and the pull of E2 are the mechanisms, and the tree's model states them with their numbers.

**Heartbeat-suppression discipline**: this is a **producer-side-refusal invariant** (same class as the [CC 5.2](#5.2) no-holding-claim-leaves-a-cohort rule). Missed (entitled-but-unreachable) members fall back to pull on reconnect — substrate does NOT keep retrying push, does NOT emit a "delivery_failed" attestation, does NOT log liveness state. The reconnect-then-pull catch-up rides CC 5.1 `history_on_join`; under the one chunk seal ([CC 5.3.3.7](#5.3.3.7)) the pulled chunks open with the same nonce as the pushed ones, so it works for a call.

#### 5.3.3.10 `transport-edge` — Transport — Edge layer (normative)

| Decision | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **E2 — pull-only** | Broadcast one-to-many delivery is **pull-only**: producer seals chunks under the epoch DEK → emits holding claims at the stream's scope → subscribers pull via the existing `ContentFetch` path. Broadcast has no relay tree. A call pushes, on direct links in a small group and through the member relay tree of [CC 6.1.6](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.6) in a large one; `fan_out` in E3 names the delivery set, never a relay topology. |
| **E1 — two-layer crypto (security-critical)** | Transit-key is a **hop-by-hop transport wrap around content already sealed under the E2E epoch DEK** (two independent crypto layers); the whole rule is stated as **E1, in full**, directly below this table. |
| **E3 — fan-out = entitled ∧ reachable** | **The store owns durable entitlement** (the roster: signed CEG envelopes, replicated, logged). **The transport owns reachability** via a node-local presence tracker. Fan-out targets the intersection. Reachability is NEVER an attestation, never a holding claim, never replicated, never logged — consistent with the [CC 5.2](#5.2) `cohort_scope: self\|family` structural-invisibility shape |
| **E4 — durable side rides existing federation-attestation path** | Durable entitlement (roster + epoch-key grants) rides the **existing federation-attestation Edge path** — just more `federation_attestations` rows. NO net-new Edge transport for the durable side. Net-new is only on CC 5.3.3.8 streaming-log endpoints |

**The KEM-authenticated handshake.** The per-link seal is a **KEM-authenticated handshake**, chosen over a signature-authenticated one: no party signs the handshake, so it gives no peer a transferable proof that two keys met (the link's identification frame is the stated limit below), which keeps reachability from becoming an attestation, and no identity key is an online signer on every link. The hybrid KEM is X-Wing, the one KEM of [CC 2.6.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1); each relaying node's long-term static is the X-Wing transit key its signed binding publishes, `transit_xwing_pubkey` ([CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6.2)), never a key reused under another combiner, and rotated by superseding the binding. **Two messages, one flight.** The initiator sends an ephemeral public key, an encapsulation to the responder's static, and its own identity sealed under the keys so derived; the responder answers with an encapsulation to the initiator's ephemeral, an encapsulation to the initiator's static where it holds the initiator's binding, and a key confirmation; the session keys derive from every shared secret present. **Known initiator, mutual:** both statics are used and both ends are authenticated by the handshake itself. **Unknown initiator, first contact:** the responder's encapsulation to the initiator's static is omitted, the link is sealed and forward-secret and the initiator is authenticated only by what the first-contact plane then admits ([CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6)), and a later encapsulation to the initiator's static on the same link promotes it to mutual once its binding is held; a node that publishes no transit pair, a client-only phone, is always such an initiator. **What this gives:** forward secrecy against the compromise of either static after the fact, authentication of both ends without a signature, and a handshake that fits one flight of thirteen frames at the Reticulum base size. **What it does not give:** full deniability while the link's identification frame remains a signature, which is stated. It does not keep the initiator's identity from a later compromise of the responder's static. The identity block of the first message is sealed under the encapsulation to that static alone, so a recorded first message then opens. Nothing here charges a shaped link's budget, since the handshake runs before shaping begins. The bindings and sealed invitations of a private room ([CC 3.1.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3.2)) use no signature either, under a key pair kept for bindings and never under the transit pair. The relay rule of E1 that binds a non-member's static against the initiator's ephemeral stands as written. Decapsulation at a responder runs outside any node-wide lock and behind the receiver rates (per-link, per-sender and node-wide, a set and not a sequence, as rule 9 of E1 states them), since a stranger's first frame is the cheapest way to make a node do expensive work.

**The wire (normative).** The suite is `transit_xwing_hkdf_sha256`: `XW` is X-Wing (public key 1216 bytes, ciphertext 1120, shared secret 32), `H` is SHA-256, `HKDF` is HKDF-SHA256, `MAC` is HMAC-SHA256 and `AEAD` is AES-256-GCM. Every length and integer is big-endian. `S_r` is the responder's static, `S_i` the initiator's static where it has one, and `E_i` the initiator's ephemeral. The transcript is a running hash bound to the link:

```
h0 = H("ciris-transit/v2" ‖ link_id[16] ‖ pk(S_r))
h1 = H(h0 ‖ pk(E_i) ‖ ct1)
h2 = H(h1 ‖ id_ct)
h3 = H(h2 ‖ flags ‖ ct2 ‖ [ct3])
```

**Message 1, initiator to responder,** carries the ephemeral, an encapsulation to the responder's static, and the initiator's identity sealed under it:

```
(ct1, ss1) = XW.Encaps(pk(S_r))
k_id       = HKDF(salt = h1, ikm = ss1, info = "ciris-transit/v2/identity", 32)
id_block   = u16 len ‖ initiator_key_id ‖ u8 has_static ‖ [H(pk(S_i))]
id_ct      = AEAD(k_id, nonce = 0^12, aad = h1, id_block)
msg1       = 0x01 ‖ u8 len ‖ "transit_xwing_hkdf_sha256" ‖ u16 len ‖ responder_key_id
                  ‖ pk(E_i)[1216] ‖ ct1[1120] ‖ u16 len ‖ id_ct
```

`responder_key_id` is in the clear, so the responder can pick its static. `H(pk(S_i))` commits the initiator to one static: the responder proceeds as mutual only when the initiator's binding it holds hashes to that commitment.

**Message 2, responder to initiator,** carries an encapsulation to the ephemeral, an encapsulation to the initiator's static when mutual, and the responder's key confirmation:

```
(ct2, ss2) = XW.Encaps(pk(E_i))
(ct3, ss3) = XW.Encaps(pk(S_i))     iff the initiator's binding is held and matches
flags      = u8: bit 0 = mutual (ct3 present); any other bit is refused
bound      = u8 len ‖ suite ‖ u16 len ‖ initiator_key_id ‖ u16 len ‖ responder_key_id
prk        = HKDF-Extract(salt = h3, ikm = ss1 ‖ ss2 ‖ [ss3])
k_i2r      = HKDF-Expand(prk, "ciris-transit/v2/initiator-to-responder" ‖ bound, 32)
k_r2i      = HKDF-Expand(prk, "ciris-transit/v2/responder-to-initiator" ‖ bound, 32)
k_conf     = HKDF-Expand(prk, "ciris-transit/v2/confirm" ‖ bound, 32)
confirm_r  = MAC(k_conf, "responder" ‖ h3)
msg2       = 0x02 ‖ flags ‖ ct2[1120] ‖ [ct3[1120]] ‖ confirm_r[32]
```

The initiator checks `confirm_r` in constant time and closes the link on a mismatch. **The initiator's confirmation** is its first sealed frame, under `k_i2r`: `"CTKC" ‖ MAC(k_conf, "initiator" ‖ h3)`. The responder holds the initiator authenticated from the first sealed frame that opens under the session keys; that frame is the initiator's key confirmation, and it adds no flight. A first frame that is anything else closes the link. At first contact the same frame is computed under keys without `ss3`, and shows only that the initiator holds its ephemeral.

**Promotion.** Once the responder holds a binding whose static hashes to the commitment of message 1, it sends a third message on the sealed link, and both ends rekey; any other binding is refused for promotion:

```
(ct3', ss3') = XW.Encaps(pk(S_i))
msg3         = 0x03 ‖ ct3'[1120]
h3'          = H(h3 ‖ "promote" ‖ ct3')
prk'         = HKDF-Extract(salt = h3', ikm = k_i2r ‖ k_r2i ‖ ss3')
```

From `prk'` both ends derive the three keys under the labels of message 2, and the initiator's first frame under the new keys is `"CTKC" ‖ MAC(k_conf', "initiator" ‖ h3')`.

**The framing.** Each message travels in parts, at most 8 KiB a message, within one budget for both messages that scales with the interface's bitrate:

```
start        = "CTKX" ‖ 0x02 ‖ 0x00 ‖ total_len u32 ‖ bytes
continuation = "CTKX" ‖ 0x02 ‖ 0x01 ‖ bytes
```

**Three safeguards.** A first sealed frame that is not a valid `CTKC` closes the link. Until `CTKC` verifies, the responder serves only the first-contact plane, even when the handshake is mutual. A promotion whose binding names a different static from the commitment of message 1 is refused. Message 2 is 1,154 bytes at first contact and 2,274 bytes when mutual. The known answers of this wire are the verifier's, published at its tag ([CC 2.6.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.5)): three handshakes, one promotion, two framing cases and 38 refusals.

**The per-frame seal (normative).** Every frame after the handshake travels under this seal, keyed by message 2 or by the promotion:

```
frame = 0x02 ‖ phase u8 ‖ counter u64_be ‖ AES-256-GCM(k, nonce, aad, pt) ‖ tag[16]
k     = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = k_dir(phase), salt = link_id[16], info = "CIRIS-E1-LINK-SEAL-V2")
nonce = lane u8 ‖ 0x000000 ‖ counter u64_be
aad   = 0x02 ‖ lane u8 ‖ phase u8 ‖ link_id[16]
```

`k_dir(phase)` is `k_i2r` or `k_r2i` for the frame's direction, from the keys of the phase the frame names. Phase 0 holds the keys of message 2. Phase 1 holds the keys of the promotion, and a link is promoted at most once.

**Lanes and counters.** The lanes are Channel 1, Resource 2, Request 3, Response 4 and Datagram 5. Each lane keeps its own counter, and the counter continues across the phase change. The phase changes the key and the lane and counter make the nonce, so no key and nonce pair repeats.

**Switching.** A sender switches every lane to phase 1 once it has sent or received the promotion's confirmation. A receiver keeps phase 0's keys on a lane until a phase-1 frame opens there, or until the handshake budget expires.

**The receiver's classification.** The receiver reads the clear phase byte before it opens a frame:

- a phase-0 frame on a lane whose phase 0 is retired is dropped and counted as `seal_stale_phase`, and the link stays open, because such a frame is late, not forged;
- a phase of 2 or more (`seal_unknown_phase`), or a phase-1 frame before the promotion (`seal_phase_before_promotion`), closes the link;
- a frame of a held phase that fails to open (`seal_open_failed`) closes the link;
- a frame of version 0x01 (`seal_v1_refused`) closes the link.

**The replay window.** Each lane has a window of 128 counters, shared by both phases. The AEAD opens a frame first. A frame that opens but repeats a counter, or is 128 or more behind the lane's highest, is dropped and counted, and the link stays open. A frame that does not open never moves the window.

The known answers of this seal are the verifier's, published at its tag ([CC 2.6.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.5)): 25 scripted receiver sequences.

**E1, in full.** The two-layer rule, in numbered sentences:

1. Transit-key is a **hop-by-hop transport wrap around content already sealed under the E2E epoch DEK** (two independent crypto layers). It MUST NOT replace the cascade — a relay never sees plaintext. *Relay* in E1 means a transport node forwarding Link frames. A **member relay**, a member forwarding a call's chunks over the member relay tree ([CC 6.1.6](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.6)), is a different object with its own name. Transit-key is for path-confidentiality; epoch-DEK is for end-to-end content confidentiality.
2. **PQC in transit — the layered posture (normative).** The RNS link layer is classical (ephemeral X25519, Ed25519, AES-256-CBC + HMAC) and is **not relied on for post-quantum confidentiality**: the RNS link request is a fixed X25519‖Ed25519 layout, and a link-level ML-KEM would break interoperability with Python RNS.
3. The guarantee is carried above it, in three layers, all of them required: every content key is wrapped X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (the at-rest cascade, `wrap_algorithm: v2`, [CC 5.1](#5.1)); every federation record carries the composite signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)); and **every byte an edge sends over an RNS link, apart from the handshake and the one route exchange of item 9, MUST be under a hybrid transit seal** keyed by an X25519 + ML-KEM-768 exchange bound to that link's `link_id` and to a transit pair **authenticated to the identity the initiator means to reach** (that identity's own hybrid-signed binding, a Rooted binding, or a pairing pin — never a bare or unsigned announce).
4. That seal is the [CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) transit KEX, run once per link as its first frame and covering every frame that follows (replication, membership, pairing and the device-join request, chat row headers, the A/V outer seal alike), not only the A/V hop. On the pairing plane the initiator has no owner yet; the seal still binds its self-signed node key, never an anonymous one ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md), adding a device, (e)). The transit-key wrap E1 names is that seal.
5. **The pre-seal route fetch.** A dialler that holds no pair for the node it means to reach — two strangers on a bare mesh, each holding only the other's announce, which cannot carry a post-quantum pair — opens the link and sends, as its first frame, a **route request** naming the dialled key and saying whether it holds that key's record; the responder answers with its own hybrid-signed `transport_destination` row (and its own key record, when the dialler says it holds none) and nothing else, and only for its own key, from its own live row carrying a pair.
6. A stranger cannot check a row's hybrid signature without the signer's public record, which an announce does not carry; the key record is the same self-signed public row any holder serves to whoever asks for it, so sending it discloses nothing more. A record so received authenticates nothing by itself: an adversary who could forge the classical signature at connection time would mint a record carrying the real Ed25519 key and its own ML-DSA-65 key and sign both. The dialler therefore binds the received record to what it held before dialling: the commitment of the code that named the key, where that code carries one ([CC 2.6.8](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.8)), a record it already holds from the key plane, or a Rooted binding ([CC 5.3.4](#5.3.4)); a dialler holding none of these fails closed, as a code with no commitment fails closed at the pull check. The exchange itself is post-quantum against a passive adversary whatever the dialler held; the binding of the responder's identity is only as strong as that anchor.
7. The dialler checks that the signer and subject of each row equal the dialled key before it stores anything, admits the key record through the key door (proof of possession and the [CC 2.6.8](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.8) fingerprint), admits the route row through authenticated admission, verifies it under the rule above (fingerprint, in-row separation, signature), and only then runs the handshake; a row signed by or about another key is refused and never stored.
8. The responder answers a route request at most once per link and rate-limits route requests node-wide before parsing them past their tag.
9. That public, self-authenticating row is the one thing besides the handshake that crosses a link unsealed: it is the row a relay would hand over and an announce already makes public, so the round trip discloses nothing an announce does not; the three receiver rates (per-link, per-sender and node-wide) run before it as a set and not a sequence, each charging only the budget it names, so a frame a per-link or per-sender rate refuses spends no node-wide budget and one prober cannot spend the strangers' share; the responder serves nothing and delivers nothing until the seal completes, and what it holds for a link still keying is sealed frames in a bounded hold that refuses on overflow by name and never trims; and a link whose first frame is anything else is dropped.
10. Where even that fails — no reachable responder — the pairing pin ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) adding a device, (f)) is the failover, the only path for two nodes that cannot exchange a single public frame.
11. With that, there is no classical-only fallback for any content and no advisory phase: a node that does not run the seal cannot talk to the mesh until it upgrades; and there is no public classical lane — a standard LXMF client that cannot run the seal is outside the mesh and is not served by an edge's LXMF path. Classical-only transport is rejected for streaming.
12. The in-transit **KEX** identifier names a *different* construction from the at-rest `wrap_algorithm` and carries its own identifier string; the two MUST NOT be compared, substituted, or accepted in each other's field ([CC 5.1](#5.1) one-construction-one-identifier rule).
13. **Which key binds a non-member relay:** the relay's transit KEX pair published on its signed `transport_destination` binding ([CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)), static against the initiator's ephemeral; never a KeyPackage init key, never an ephemeral-only exchange; a node with no valid transit pair cannot relay.

#### 5.3.3.11 `delivery` — Delivery acknowledgements (normative)

A `delivery_ack:{stream_id}` Contribution is a subscriber's signed acknowledgement that they received chunk K under the named stream + epoch. **Best-effort default**; opt-in for **accountable** profiles (registry propagation, emergency). A stream is accountable when its binding's signed `profile` is 1 ([CC 5.3.3.5](#5.3.3.5)), and the receipt guard below reads that member. The word Receipt is a Transparency Service's ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)), so a subscriber's acknowledgement is an ack.

**The payload (normative).** The ack is the row's payload: `stream_id`, `epoch`, `k` and `chunk_root` ([CC 2.6.1.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.4)). The subscriber's own statement is its signature, and the row carries no inner signature and no length-prefixed preimage. `received_at` is not signed: it is the receiving node's local note and no part of the payload. The earlier form's signing bytes are [CC 8.11.30](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.30).

Both `epoch` (key-rotation index — for per-epoch entitlement / billing) and `K`/`chunk_root` (chunk position + its committed root) are independent indices — both required (each names a distinct authorization scope).

**Verify check is a JOIN, NOT a sig-check**:

1. **Signature valid** over the payload (the subscriber's one composite signature, [CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)). Necessary but **not sufficient**.
2. **`chunk_root` is the root of a held head.** It MUST equal the `root` of a held `stream:head` row of that stream at `tree_size` K or more ([CC 5.3.3.8](#5.3.3.8)). An ack over a root that no held head carries concludes nothing: it is kept and stays void until such a head is held, so a phantom or self-invented root never counts. For an accountable stream the head counts only once it is published: Receipts for it from `receipt_quorum` of the room's named services are held. So the subscriber cannot collude with the producer on a private root. An ack over an inline blob is checked against the blob's one leaf, since an inline file publishes no head.
3. *(Recommended for accountable)* **Inclusion proof** chunk K → `chunk_root`. Upgrades the ack from "subscriber saw a root" to "subscriber saw a root that provably commits to chunk K".

**Semantics — proof of acknowledged root, not proof-of-CONSUMPTION**: the ack attests that the subscriber signed over a published root at `tree_size ≥ K`. Receipt of chunk K is shown only with its inclusion proof, and then as a commitment: the root commits to chunk K. It does NOT prove they decrypted those bytes (they may not hold the epoch DEK). Consumers MUST NOT overclaim a delivery ack as proof of consumption. Per the fail-honest invariant + [CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md#1.7) "Verify authenticates origin, does not compose 'delivered'/'owes N'", Verify's role is validation-not-adjudication: emit the validated ack as an attestation on `delivery_ack:{stream_id}` — the "delivered" verdict is consumer policy.

**The accountable quorum** is the room's `receipt_quorum`, a strict majority of the services the room names ([CC 5.3.3.8](#5.3.3.8)). No other count applies to a stream.

#### 5.3.3.12 `normative` — Framing (normative)

A stream is **its own log**: its chunks are its leaves, and its heads are `stream:head` rows ([CC 5.3.3.8](#5.3.3.8)). A `live_stream` MUST NOT append chunks into a node's audit log or into the log of any Transparency Service ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)). Millions of media chunks would swamp either. A service registers a stream's heads and never its chunks. A stream's log and a service's log are separate logs under the same RFC 6962 hashing.

The 1+4 wire-format lockdown holds: there are no new `attestation_type` values. Stream chunks ride content addressing; a stream's head is a row of family `stream:head`; delivery acks ride `scores` against the `delivery_ack:{stream_id}` reserved prefix ([CC 3.4.6](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4.6)).

#### 5.3.3.13 `documents-what` — What the streaming surface documents

Scope pointer: the CC 5.3.3 streaming surface — delivery axis ([CC 5.3.3.8](#5.3.3.8)–[CC 5.3.3.9](#5.3.3.9)) — does **not** change the 1+4 primitive set ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4)) (delivery rides existing primitives) and does **not** bundle the streaming-half substrate implementation. The surface keeps broadcast fan-out pull-only, while a call's A/V chunks push through the member relay tree ([CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2)), and leaves the head interval above its floor and `MAX_CHUNKS_PER_EPOCH` operator-tunable.

### 5.3.4 `multi-steward` — Trust-root discovery — the GenesisBundle + accord holders

These endpoints publish the trust root itself — the accord-authorized GenesisBundle, and the accord holders it names — so a verifier can discover *whom* to trust before trusting anything. A consumer MUST verify the bundle's quorum against its own records before promoting any field to a trust root. This is the fidelity / fail-secure floor for the whole discovery surface. Nothing a serving install signs on its own account is a root.

### `GET /v1/trust-root/bundle` — the portable trust root (`/v1/steward-key` is an alias)

Returns the **GenesisBundle**: the accord holders' statements over one `ceg-genesis-bundle/2` payload, which carries the roster, the seats and the charter ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)), and the rows it names. A registry publishing its own key as its own root, `hardware_class` self-attested, is the weakest form of a producer claim ([CC 4.2.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.2.1)). The registry is a conferred slice of a canonical node, not a root. The same body is served at both paths.

Response (`200 OK`):

```json
{
  "bundle": {
    "statements": [ "<hex: holder A's ceg-genesis-bundle/2 statement>", "<hex: holder B's>", "..." ],
    "rows": [ "<hex: each statement of each row the bundle names: the holders', seats' and transparency services' key records, each seat's binding>" ]
  },
  // the bundle's object id (CC 2.6.1.11), served for the consumer to recompute; its member is an open encoding (CC 2.6.1.12)
  "charter_root_key_id": "<read off the bundle; verify it>",
  "served_by": { "node_key_id": "<relaying node>", "accepts_this_root": true }
}
```

**Authority lives inside `bundle` and nowhere else (normative).** The bundle is **tamper-evident, not authentic** ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T5). Its holders' statements over its payload prove the bundle is internally consistent, and an attacker's self-consistent bundle under the same identifiers verifies identically.

*The out-of-band anchor.* A consumer therefore MUST hold an **out-of-band anchor before accepting a bootstrap bundle**: either the pinned object id of the `ceg-genesis-bundle/2` object ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)) or the pinned thumbprints of the accord holders' composite keys. The anchor is the consumer's own, what it was built or configured to trust, and never a member of the response. A release carries a default anchor, and a consumer may be re-rooted to another. The default anchor is the set of the holders' thumbprints, which exists once the holders mint their keys and before the bundle is signed. The bundle's object id is published after signing, and a later release may carry it as the anchor. Under a thumbprint anchor, a first bundle verifies only where its holders equal the anchored set and every one of them signed it. Two such bundles are a fork and select nothing, and with nothing selected the consumer runs no agent and serves nothing of that mesh until its owner re-anchors it ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). The `bundle_fingerprint` of the earlier form is [CC 8.11.24](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.24). The consumer MUST compare the received bundle against the anchor it holds at attach time. `ciris-canonical` and `humanity-accord` are **names, not anchors**, and a consumer with no anchor MUST NOT promote anything in the response to a trust root. With the anchor held, the consumer re-derives the quorum from its *own* records (`verify_bundle_quorum` — the holders' statements counted against the roster the consumer holds or has just pinned). From then on the root is valid until revoked (T4) ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)).

*Outside `bundle`.* Everything outside `bundle` — the served object id, the charter root id, `served_by` — is unsigned convenience metadata the consumer recomputes (the object id against its pin) or ignores. The served object id is never itself the anchor. There is deliberately **no `response_signature`**. Signing the wrapper would prove only that the relaying node said it, which is worthless as a root. It would also invite consumers to check the envelope instead of the artifact. `hardware_class`, `signature_mode` and `threshold_policy` MUST NOT appear on the outer envelope. A holder's custody class rides that holder's signed key record and is corroborated, or not, per [CC 4.2.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.2.1). `served_by.accepts_this_root: false` is a legitimate state: a node MAY relay the bundle of a lineage its owner has not accepted ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T3). Acceptance is the owner's one row, and the node reads it. That state is the owner's un-trust lever made visible.

**What a consumer pins.** A consumer's trust policy names the bundle's lineage by `family_key_id`. Its holders and seats are read from the bundle in force ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)), and a consumer never hard-pins a serving install's fingerprint. `ciris-canonical` is a room of the canonical installs and no part of the pin ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). A root is valid until revoked, never until a timer lapses ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T4). What freshness gates is *attaching*, under T4a, and the object that carries it is served beside the bundle.

**The lineage head beside the bundle.** The accord's genesis head is the first bundle itself: its `holders` and its `charter` are the accord's roster and charter at version 1 ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6: the signed roster record at a version is the head). Its charter carries `attach_window_secs` and, where it names services, the three transparency members ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)). All are therefore pinned by the bundle's object id with everything else in it.

The route serves, outside `bundle`, a `lineage_head` member. It is the **head chain since genesis** of each lineage: every later bundle in order by `prev`, each with the Receipts held for it ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)). The same chain is served at `GET /v1/trust-root/lineage-head` (with `?since=<digest>` for a consumer refreshing before it attaches), any object in it fetchable by digest.

*Checking the head chain.* The chain is unsigned convenience like everything outside `bundle`: the consumer walks `prev` from the genesis head it holds from the bundle. It counts each head on its **predecessor's** holders ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). It counts each Receipt against the services its **predecessor's** charter names, never the head's own charter, which a fork head chooses. It counts only independent services and applies [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T4a. Fewer than `receipt_quorum` is `trust_root_head_unreceipted`. A newest counted Receipt older than `attach_window_secs` is `trust_root_head_stale`. In either case the consumer fetches a fresher head or refuses; it never attaches on the stale one. A consumer SHOULD obtain at least one counted Receipt directly from the service that issued it ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T6).

**Charter defaults.** A charter that names no services ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)) attaches through the consumer's out-of-band anchor (above), with `attach_window_secs` **604800**. The accord's charter carries `halt_fuse_secs` **86400** (24 hours, [CC 4.2.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.1.1)). Services are named by an amend, a later bundle counted at a strict majority of the predecessor's holders. With transparency members present, the accord charter's defaults are:

| Charter member | Default with transparency members present |
|---|---|
| `attach_window_secs` | **604800** (7 days) |
| `receipt_cadence_secs` | **86400** (24 hours) |
| `transparency_services` | **exactly three** independent services |
| `receipt_quorum` | therefore **2** (⌊3/2⌋ + 1 — a fourth service raises it to 3, since two of four is not a strict majority) |

All four are charter members, changed only by a later bundle. The window exceeds the cadence plus skew as T4a requires. Once attached, T4 governs: the served head's age is a liveness signal on the trust surface, never an expiry ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)).

**The bundle is the Rooted seed for transit pairs (normative).** Under the per-link hybrid seal of [CC 5.3.3.10](#5.3.3.10) E1 a node dials only a peer whose transit pair it holds **authenticated to the identity it means to reach**:

- that identity's own hybrid-signed `transport_destination` row ([CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6.2)), from any source;
- or a Rooted binding;
- or a pairing pin ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) (f)).

Such a row otherwise arrives over a sealed link, so a device that knows no one needs a first row from somewhere. For the seated serve nodes it is this bundle. Each serve seat's binding in the bundle therefore carries `dial_hints`, signed with the binding: an ordered list of places to dial in the hint types of the node code ([CC 2.6.8](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.8)), with at least one `tcp` hint. The list is a cold-start seed and nothing more. The seat's live signed route row supersedes it once a link is up, an operator's own configuration overrides it, and a counted re-bind MAY carry a new list.

*A canonical node is one source of route rows, never a required party.* The premise of this document is a network with no company in the middle. A trust decides what a node serves ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T8), not whether two keys may speak privately. Two peers holding each other's signed route rows seal, exchange their allegiance rows and root each other directly. They hold those rows from a contact code, from the owner's own hand at first contact (the contact rule of [CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6)), or, for an unowned node, from any relay of the bootstrap kinds.

*What the bundle names.* The bundle names, by row id in `refs`, each seated serve node's signed `transport_destination` binding ([CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6.2)), each carrying its transit key. Every holder's statement covers the payload that names them, so the count that seats a node seats its binding ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). At bundle verification each binding MUST be authored by a serve node listed in the bundle's `serve_nodes` and MUST carry a key that passes the in-row separation. On any failure the bundle concludes nothing.

*Seeding at first open.* At first open the rows are seeded through the ordinary transport-destination admission and land Rooted. So a fresh node with no network holds a canonical node's pair and dials it first under the seal. From there it holds what [CC 5.2](#5.2) moves to it: what it is required to hold, and what it asks for.

*The two forms of re-mint.* A bundle re-mint comes in two forms. A **fresh genesis** is the final-genesis ceremony: every holder signs the bundle. Every holder signs because only each holder can give their own recovery commitment and successor seat. Unanimity is what that ceremony gathers. The genesis of this edition is a fresh genesis with no predecessor ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). Its charter commits a new recovery commitment for each holder, and it names the holders' key records and the seats' key records and bindings, all of this form. Its count is each seat's conferral ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). Outside it, a change to the charter or the roster is an accord threshold: a strict majority of the standing accord roster ([CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.6)).

An **amend** is a later bundle. It names the verified bundle as `prev`, carries a `version` one greater, and names afresh every row it seats ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). It counts at a strict majority of the predecessor's holders. Each holder it adds, and each holder whose recovery commitment it changes, signs it too. An amend cannot change `family_key_id`: a different accord is a fresh genesis. A roster change of the accord is such an amend ([CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.2.6)). A recovery is the one exception to its count: it counts on the recovering holder's recovery key alone ([CC 2.6.1.11](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.11)). Seeding the canonicals' transit pairs is the same class of act as blessing a canonical, already a strict-majority act, so two holders gain no power they lack.

*The rows are each node's own.* The rows the bundle names are **signed** `transport_destination` rows, each the node's own signed self-emission.

*The first seed is emitted offline:* under the seal no existing node can dial a canonical whose pair it does not hold, and the re-mint cannot read a row the canonical has not emitted. So the cycle is broken on the host: a seated canonical's operator emits the node's hybrid-signed row, pair included, from the node's own custody with no network. The transit pair is derived deterministically from the custody seed, so the offline row and the row the node emits live later carry the same pair. The ceremony re-mints from those rows.

*The age of a seeded row.* Bundle verification checks each row's signature and its signer's seat, never its age ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T4: valid until revoked). So a row emitted before the ceremony seeds a node opened long after. The node's live row supersedes it on the first sealed link, same pair, later `asserted_at`.

*Overlap rule:* a seated serve node MUST keep the pair the pinned bundle carries valid until a re-minted bundle carrying its new pair has propagated, or make the rotation itself a re-mint. The node does not sign a rotation that would retire the pinned pair before it holds the replacement Rooted. A node that receives one does not count it (`serve_transit_pair_rotation_before_rebind`). The genesis of this edition retires no pair, since the earlier mesh shares no rows with this one ([CC 2.6.1.12](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.12)).

*A rotation is a quorum act, not a re-mint:* the holders' quorum re-binds a canonical's destination and transit pair by the accord-signed address update of [CC 3.3.6.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.6.2). That update lands as a Rooted `transport_destination` superseding the bundle-seeded pair on every node that holds the root. The re-mint is needed only to change what a *fresh* node seeds. A fresh node that seeds the old pair follows the supersede chain to the new one once it has sealed to any canonical.

*Before the first sealed link.* The bundle is the only seed before the first sealed link. Two other ways a transit pair reaches a node before any sealed link are defined. One is the owner's pairing payload at pairing ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2), adding a device, (f)), pinned for that link alone. The other is the pre-seal route fetch of [CC 5.3.3.10](#5.3.3.10) step 5, by which a dialler holding only a stranger's announce receives that key's own hybrid-signed route row as the link's first frame.

**What crosses before Rooted (normative).** A trust decides what a node *serves*, never whether two keys may speak privately ([CC 2.7.5](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.7.5)). On a sealed link to a peer the node has not Rooted, what the peer's own standing admits still crosses:

- the bootstrap kinds and the allegiance rows;
- the pairing plane;
- rows addressed to the peer;
- and every row a bounded cohort delivers to that peer as its member under [CC 5.2](#5.2) — `self`, `family`, `community`, `affiliations` — because cohort delivery is consent and membership, not service.

A node's allegiance rows are its owner's acceptance edges, and its owner-binding where that binding is placed at `federation`. A binding placed at `self`, a family or a room is no allegiance row. It crosses to no link peer by virtue of the link.

What waits for `Rooted` ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2) T8) is what the node serves to a third party: a federation-tier row, and any self-authored row about someone other than the peer.

### `GET /v1/accord-holders`

Returns the named holders with hybrid pubkeys, per-holder `hardware_class` and a `provisioned` flag. A holder not yet provisioned carries a placeholder fingerprint and `provisioned: false`. Consumers MUST NOT honor `constitutional` invocations against placeholders. The holders' authority is the bundle above. This route is a projection of `bundle.holders`, and a consumer cross-checks it against the bundle rather than trusting the projection.

### `GET /v1/accord/holders`

UI wrapper around `/v1/accord-holders` with per-holder `accord_emissions[]` for UI rendering. The same projection rule holds: there is **no response signature**. The wrapper carries no authority, and a consumer cross-checks every holder it shows against `bundle.holders` under the anchor it already holds. `accord_emissions[]` are the holders' own signed rows, verified individually.

### `GET /v1/rotation-history`

Chronological rotation events of the Registry's signing keys.

### 5.3.5 `registry-other` — Other Registry endpoints

`GET /v1/builds/{version}` returns the BuildRecordResponse with a `federation_provenance` block. `GET /v1/provenance/build/{project}/{version}/{target}` is the shipped route for a build manifest, and its answer holds what [CC 3.1.2.1](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2.1) lists. `GET /v1/verify/build-manifest/{project}/{version}/{target}` returns the BuildManifest of the earlier form ([CC 8.11](part_8_appendices.md#8.11)). `GET /v1/agent_files/{kind}?platform_or_target=...` returns the [CC 4.4.3.33](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.33) trust-composition layers. `GET /v1/partner/{key_id}` composes ProfileScorecard data from existing tables.

Full response schemas for these endpoints are published as a versioned OpenAPI document alongside this one.

### 5.3.6 `common` — Common response shape

All CEG endpoints return:

- **Content-Type**: `application/json` (`Accept: application/json` honored; other types respond `406 Not Acceptable`)
- **CEG-API-Version header**: `CEG-Version: <current spec major.minor>` on every response (this document's version); clients SHOULD echo `CEG-Accept-Version: <pinned-version>` on request, naming the version they were built against. Per [CC 2.6.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.4) SemVer policy, MAJOR mismatch is a wire-incompat reject; MINOR mismatch is compatible (clients MAY warn).
- **Time-Source header**: `X-CEG-Server-Time: <rfc3339_canonical>` per [CC 2.6.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.3) for client clock-skew bounds
- **Pagination** (where applicable): `?cursor=` + `?limit=` query params; response includes `next_cursor` (null if exhausted) and `total_estimate` (server's best estimate, may be approximate)

#### 5.3.6.1 `envelope-error` — Error envelope

All error responses MUST conform to:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "<ENUM_VALUE>",
    "http_status": <int>,
    "message": "<human-readable>",
    "request_id": "<server-assigned>",
    "details": {<error-specific fields>}
  }
}
```

| HTTP status | Error code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | Invalid JSON, missing required field, bad field type |
| 400 | `CANONICAL_BYTES_VIOLATION` | Date-time / hex / encoding doesn't match [CC 2.6.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.2), [CC 2.6.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.2) or [CC 2.6.3](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.3), or, for an earlier-form object, [CC 8.11.10](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.10) or [CC 8.11.11](part_8_appendices.md#8.11.11) |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Bearer token missing or invalid |
| 403 | `RESERVED_PREFIX_VIOLATION` | Producer attempted to emit under a reserved prefix without authority per [CC 3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4) |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Generic resource not found (build, partner, key) |
| 409 | `IDEMPOTENT_CONFLICT` | Replay detected: a request already answered arrives again with different content |
| 422 | `SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILED` | The composite signature failed to verify; it is one signature ([CC 2.6.1.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.7)) |
| 422 | `CLOCK_SKEW_VIOLATION` | `asserted_at` or `signed_at` exceeds [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.7) ±5 minute tolerance |
| 422 | `RECEIPT_QUORUM_NOT_MET` | Fewer counted Receipts are held for the head than its `receipt_quorum` ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)) |
| 413 | `ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE` | A payload's deterministic encoding exceeds the [CC 2.6.1.6](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.6) 1 MiB bound, or the octets buffered reach the write path's intake ceiling before the parse completes. Raised at **every** write path (HTTP body, capsule, FFI, tier-ingest), not only at an HTTP gate — the CC 2.6.1.6 rule is an admission bound, not a transport limit. The reason of the refusal is `envelope_too_large` on every write path ([CC 2.6.1.6](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.6)), and this code is how the HTTP surface carries it. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | `X-RateLimit-*` headers set; `Retry-After` honored |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Server-side fault; request_id usable for support |
| 503 | `SUBSTRATE_LAGGING` | Substrate replication lag exceeds liveness bound |

Admission refusal tokens are refusal reasons carried in the row's refusal, not HTTP statuses, and this table does not map them. That covers every refusal token, for example `attestation_type_unregistered`, `federation_malformed_row` with its closed reason set, `federation_set_semantics_unsorted` ([CC 2.6.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.2)), `asserted_at_stale` ([CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.7)), `trust_root_head_unreceipted` and `trust_root_head_stale` ([CC 5.3.4](#5.3.4)), and the census tokens of [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1).

Rate-limit headers on every response: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds-until-reset epoch).

## 5.4 `scope-privacy-wire` — Scope-Native Privacy wire profile

The wire-format absorption of the Scope-Native Privacy construction. These are the deterministic, byte-pinned primitives a conformant substrate uses to make real and cover traffic indistinguishable below the cohort boundary — record addressing, per-symbol AEAD, uniform fragmentation, the MLS Welcome wrap, the witness-chain discipline, and announce suppression. They are additive to the wire layer; the 1+4 surface is unchanged.

### 5.4.1 `record-id` — Deterministic `record_id` (CBOR profile, normative)

Scope-native distribution addresses each record by an HMAC-opaque `record_id` rather than any plaintext key. The `record_id` is a deterministic, group-keyed commitment to the record's identity: every member of the MLS group derives the identical `record_id` for a given record, while non-members observe an unlinkable 32-byte tag. This is the addressing argument of the deterministic ALM "directory" — a pure function, never a queryable authority ([CC 4.4.3.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.4) cohort-scope lattice).

The preimage `record_id_input` is the Core Deterministic Encoding of a fixed four-entry map; `record_id` is its HMAC under the per-epoch key `K_record_id`. The preimage, the key derivation, and the resulting tag MUST be byte-identical across producer, substrate, and every consumer. Any disagreement on CBOR byte order, integer minimal-encoding, major-type selection, or HKDF/HMAC suite yields a different `record_id`, silently partitioning holders of the same record. This is the same byte-exactness hazard class the STREAM nonce derivation guards ([CC 5.3.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.3.3.1)).

**Per-epoch key.** `K_record_id` is derived in two stages: an RFC 9420 exporter call under the record label, then a bare HKDF-Expand (no Extract, no MLS KDF-label framing) over that exporter output. `K_symbol` ([CC 5.4.2](#5.4.2)) is the second stage of the same chain under its own label:

```
S_record    = MLS-Exporter(label = "ciris-scope-record-v1", context = "", length = 32)

K_record_id = HKDF-SHA256-Expand(
    PRK  = S_record,
    info = "ciris-edge/scope-privacy/record-id/v1"  (ASCII),
    L    = 32
)
K_symbol    = HKDF-SHA256-Expand(
    PRK  = S_record,
    info = "ciris-edge/scope-privacy/symbol/v1"     (ASCII),
    L    = 32
)
```

The HKDF hash here is **SHA-256** (the ciphersuite 0x004D key-schedule hash). Implementations MUST derive `S_record` by the exporter call under `ciris-scope-record-v1`, and `K_record_id` and `K_symbol` by the bare HKDF-Expand over `S_record`; the second-stage labels MUST NOT be routed through RFC 9420 `MLS_Exporter()`, and the raw `exporter_secret` is never used directly. `S_dest` ([CC 5.4.6](#5.4.6)) is a separate exporter under its own label.

**Preimage and commitment.** Each record:

```
record_id_input = CBOR_dCE({
    "v":   1,
    "epc": mls_group_epoch,
    "iid": internal_id,
    "typ": record_type,    // integer per RecordType table below
})
record_id       = HMAC-SHA3-256(K_record_id, record_id_input)
```

`CBOR_dCE` is RFC 8949, section 4.2.1, Core Deterministic Encoding (shortest-form integer encoding, definite lengths only, no floating-point unless required), with map keys ordered **in the bytewise lexicographic order of their deterministic encodings**. The four-entry map at `v=1` therefore serializes keys in the canonical order `v, epc, iid, typ`.

**Major types are pinned.** Within the map the four keys (`v`, `epc`, `iid`, `typ`) are CBOR text strings (major type 3). The values of `v`, `epc`, and `typ` are unsigned integers (major type 0). The value of `iid` is a **CBOR byte string (major type 2)** — `internal_id` is committed as its raw bytes, never as a text string, even when those bytes are human-readable (e.g. `record-0001`). Encoding `iid` as a text string (major type 3) produces a different preimage and a different `record_id`; the byte-string header is why the vectors below carry `0x4b`/`0x41` (major-2) and not `0x6b`/`0x61` (major-3) at the `iid` value position.

**`RecordType` integer encoding** (pinned for cross-impl conformance):

| Type             | int |
|------------------|-----|
| reserved         | 0   |
| SelfRecord       | 1   |
| FamilyRecord     | 2   |
| CommunityRecord  | 3   |
| FederationRecord | 4   |

Additional record types extend this table by amendment under [CC 2.6.4](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.4).

**Conformance vectors (normative).** With `K_record_id = 0x11` repeated 32 times, conforming implementations MUST reproduce these exact CBOR preimage bytes and `record_id` tags (hex):

```
// Vector 1 — CommunityRecord (typ=3), epc=7, iid="record-0001"
record_id_input = a46176016365706307636969644b7265636f72642d303030316374797003
record_id       = 5428ddb514a8f8692cc4f254f3550ea75790f5069673e42afb6ef318517a0b21

// Vector 2 — FederationRecord (typ=4), epc=300, iid="record-0002"
//   (forces 0x19 u16 epc header: bytes[8..11] == 0x19 0x01 0x2c)
record_id_input = a46176016365706319012c636969644b7265636f72642d303030326374797004
record_id       = 04eebeee4d5b83f2fdd0012a205781e6c05fe9a587377e6161b347629a189ff2

// Vector 3 — SelfRecord (typ=1), epc=16909060 (0x01020304), iid="x"
//   (forces 0x1a u32 epc header: bytes[8..13] == 0x1a 0x01 0x02 0x03 0x04)
record_id_input = a4617601636570631a010203046369696441786374797001
record_id       = 79bee8b3f1e815a1df03ca9d83427dc5ab474e184f34e3876d3ef3c36559d6a3
```

The deterministic CBOR profile is normative here; the vectors are published with the release.

### 5.4.2 `symbol` — Uniform symbol AEAD framing for scope-privacy symbols (normative)

Within both encrypted crypto tiers, stored content moves and rests as encrypted chunks, replicated per item to its holders and never split by any node. The two tiers are the self/family **InvisibleEncrypted** tier and the community/affiliations **CommunityDek** tier ([CC 4.4.3.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.4), resolved through `crypto_tier(cohort_scope, cohort_subkind)` with non-`infrastructure` subkind). On the scope-privacy plane each such chunk crosses a shaped link as symbols: the indexed fragments of [CC 5.4.3](#5.4.3), real and cover alike. Each emitted symbol is sealed under its **own** AEAD key, so a relay or holder lacking the keys holds indistinguishable-from-random ciphertext. The realtime A/V plane ([CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2)) is not on this path: a sealed A/V chunk rides its link whole under the E1 seal ([CC 5.3.3.5](#5.3.3.5)) and emits no symbol. The two tiers differ in the shape of their roster, not in discoverability to outsiders, which is none for both ([CC 5.2](#5.2)). A community's roster may be larger and a family's is intimate. A `public` room is in neither tier: it is Commons-tier plaintext, discoverable by its listing ([CC 4.4.3.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.4)). The holder-inspectability principle ([CC 4.4.3.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.4)) says members hold what they can open and strangers hold nothing, which is what the keep and evict decision enforces. What a carrier forwards for others stays sealed and unreadable to it: a chunk under its own seal, a symbol under the symbol AEAD below without `K_symbol`. The substrate MUST seal every symbol it emits with the framing below. A holder lacking `K_symbol` MUST be unable to open a symbol, or to tell a real fragment from cover by its sealed bytes. That claim is about the sealed bytes alone: `record_id` and `symbol_index` are cleartext on every envelope, and what they show a carrier is stated below.

`record_id` is the per-record HMAC-opaque addressing tag of the group-keyed addressing construction ([CC 5.4.1](#5.4.1)) — `record_id = HMAC-SHA3-256(K_record_id, CBOR_dCE({v, epc, iid, typ}))`. `K_symbol` and `K_record_id` are the per-scope subkeys of the one derivation chain of [CC 5.4.1](#5.4.1) (`HKDF-SHA256-Expand` over `S_record`, the `ciris-scope-record-v1` exporter output, each under its own label); both rebind on MLS Add/Remove.

For each symbol the wire framing is byte-exact:

```
For each symbol:

    symbol_key = HKDF-SHA3-256(salt=record_id, ikm=K_symbol,
                               info="ciris-edge/scope-privacy/symbol/v1"
                                    || u16_be(symbol_index), len=32)
    symbol_envelope = (record_id, u16_be(symbol_index), nonce,
                       XChaCha20-Poly1305(symbol_key, nonce, fragment), tag)
```

Normative constraints:

- **`symbol_key` derivation is byte-identical across every implementation.** `salt = record_id` (the 32-byte HMAC tag), `ikm = K_symbol` (the 32-byte exporter subkey), and `info` is the **exact** concatenation of the UTF-8 bytes of the ASCII label `ciris-edge/scope-privacy/symbol/v1` followed by `u16_be(symbol_index)` (the symbol index as a 2-byte big-endian unsigned integer), with `len = 32`. The same ASCII label is both the second-stage `info` that derives `K_symbol` from `S_record` ([CC 5.4.1](#5.4.1)) and this info-prefix; producer, substrate, and every consumer MUST recompute this exact value. Any BE/LE disagreement on `symbol_index`, or any drift in the label bytes, yields a different `symbol_key` → AEAD authentication failure (silent decryption failure).
- **The AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 24-byte `nonce` and the Poly1305 `tag`** carried in the envelope. The same suite seals **both** real fragments and cover fragments — there is no separate cover cipher, no cleartext cover marker, and no length distinguisher. A holder lacking `K_symbol` holds a ciphertext and a tag indistinguishable from random bytes, under the standard assumptions on XChaCha20-Poly1305 and HKDF-SHA3 extract-then-expand. The sealed bytes of a cover envelope and of a real one have one form.
- **The fragment-set rebinds on MLS Add/Remove.** Because `symbol_key` chains from `K_symbol` and `record_id`, both of which rotate with the group epoch, a removed member's symbol keys do not open post-epoch fragments. Past-epoch `K_record_id` / `K_symbol` are deleted by honest holders per the community's archive policy.
- **`symbol_envelope` field order is fixed: `(record_id, u16_be(symbol_index), nonce, ciphertext, tag)`.** The cleartext `record_id` and `symbol_index` are the addressing argument to the HMAC-opaque directory function (the [CC 6.1.6](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md#6.1.6) deterministic ALM topology) and are NOT authority-bearing. They name no group, record type or author to a non-member, who cannot derive the corresponding `symbol_key`. They do link the symbols of one record to each other.
- **What a carrier of symbols learns.** A node that carries symbol envelopes without `K_symbol` reads `record_id` and `symbol_index` on each one. It counts the symbols under one `record_id`, which bounds that record's size. It recognises the same record on another link within an epoch. The uniform frames of [CC 5.4.3](#5.4.3) hide size and count from an observer outside the link's seal, and from no node that holds the envelopes.

This framing is the byte-level analogue of the [CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1) per-chunk stream seal: the costly key agreement is amortized into the MLS exporter, and the hot path is a per-symbol symmetric AEAD with a deterministically derived key. It composes with — and never substitutes for — the at-rest DEK cascade ([CC 4.4.3.16](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.16)); the symbol AEAD protects the scope-privacy plane's fragments in transit and at any relay that forwards them, the DEK cascade protects the record at rest.

### 5.4.3 `fragmentation` — Uniform-envelope fragmentation & reassembly (normative)

This entry says how a link is shaped, how a payload is cut into uniform frames for a shaped link, and how the frames are put back together. A claim's bytes rarely fit one packet, and the split is where privacy is most easily lost. A naive fragmenter leaks payload size, count, and cadence to anyone on the path. The discipline here is that every fragment on the wire (a real publication fragment or a synthetic cover envelope) is the **same size** and the **same AEAD shape**. So an on-path observer cannot distinguish a large publication from idle substrate maintenance. This composes with the chunk-seal of [CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1) (a *different* axis: streaming media chunks). Fragmentation is the substrate-emission layer beneath every send on a shaped link, not the streaming codec.

**Fixed frame size on a shaped link (normative).** On a shaped link (below) every frame is one constant size: the shaped frame. The shaped frame is **1,400 bytes** measured before the link's E1 transit seal with the frame header included, or the link's channel payload MDU where that is smaller (about 400 bytes at the Reticulum base MTU). A larger payload is fragmented to that size and a smaller one padded to it. Within a link the size is not a tuning knob, because a variable frame re-exposes the size channel that shaping exists to close. It is one constant for the fleet rather than a class or a negotiated value, because an observer already reads the class from the rate and a negotiated size is the knob this paragraph refuses. An unshaped link carries no padding requirement. There is no fixed envelope size for all outbound traffic: uniform frames add privacy only where both ends shape.
